title: Recent Advances in Convolutional Neural Networks
Abstract: Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) have revolutionized the field of machine learning and computer vision, achieving state-of-the-art performance in various applications, including image classification, object detection, and segmentation. Recent advances in CNNs have harnessed the power of large-scale datasets, powerful GPU architectures, and novel architectures to significantly improve model performance and efficiency. One of the key drivers of these advancements has been the development of transfer learning techniques, which enable the pre-training of CNNs on large datasets and subsequent fine-tuning on smaller datasets, allowing for faster and more accurate model adaptation. The introduction of attention mechanisms and neural architecture search has also enabled CNNs to focus on relevant regions of the input data and adapt to diverse input types, respectively. Furthermore, Recent studies have focused on improving CNN efficiency through techniques such as knowledge distillation, model pruning, and quantization, enabling the deployment of CNNs on edge devices. Additionally, researchers have explored the application of CNNs in tasks beyond traditional computer vision, including natural language processing, speech recognition, and sequential data analysis. With the rapid growth of IoT devices and increasing demand for real-time analytics, the development of efficient, robust, and versatile CNN architectures has become a critical research challenge, with significant potential for impacting various industries and applications.

title: Cost-based Feature Transfer for Vehicle Occupant Classification
Abstract: Vehicle occupant classification (VOC) is a critical component in various automotive applications, including airbag deployment systems and driver assistance systems, which necessitate the accurate identification of vehicle occupants' positions and postures. Existing VOC methods primarily rely on machine learning algorithms and feature extraction techniques, which can be computationally expensive, model-dependent, and suffer from data scarcity problems. To overcome these challenges, this research proposes a novel cost-based feature transfer framework for vehicle occupant classification. The proposed framework leverages transfer learning concepts and cost-sensitive learning methods to efficiently transfer features from source VOC datasets to target datasets with limited annotations. By employing a hybrid approach that combines feature-level and decision-level transfer, the framework adaptively selects relevant features based on their transfer costs, thereby ensuring robust classification performance on unseen data. Extensive evaluations on multiple VOC datasets demonstrate the superior performance and efficiency of the proposed framework compared to state-of-the-art VOC methods. Moreover, the framework's ability to handle varying occupancy postures, limited available data, and environmental noise makes it a promising solution for real-world VOC applications, paving the way for improved safety and driver assistance systems in the automotive industry.

title: Implementation of deep learning algorithm for automatic detection of brain tumors using intraoperative IR-thermal mapping data
Abstract: This study explores the implementation of deep learning algorithms for the automatic detection of brain tumors using intraoperative IR-thermal mapping data. Current clinical practices rely heavily on visual inspection and surgeon expertise, which may lead to variable detection accuracy and prolonged surgery durations. To address these limitations, this study developing a novel deep learning framework that leverages IR-thermal imaging data to identify and classify brain tumors in real-time during surgical procedures. The proposed system consists of a data preprocessing module to normalize and filter the temperature data, followed by a convolutional neural network (CNN) for feature extraction and classification. A comparative analysis of different CNN architectures and hyperparameters was conducted to optimize the model's performance. Experimental results showed that the proposed system achieved a mean accuracy of 92.5%, sensitivity of 89.2%, and specificity of 95.3% in detecting brain tumors from IR-thermal mapping data, outperforming comparable state-of-the-art methods. Furthermore, the proposed system demonstrated robustness and reliability in real-time performance, reducing the need for manual resection and promoting more accurate and efficient brain tumor surgery. The findings of this study have the potential to revolutionize brain tumor surgery by enhancing diagnostic accuracy, reducing surgical risks, and improving patient outcomes.

title: Deep Learning with S-shaped Rectified Linear Activation Units
Abstract: This study introduces a novel activation unit, the S-shaped Rectified Linear Activation Unit (S-ReLU), designed to reduce the vanishing gradient problem in deep learning networks. Motivated by the success of ReLU and its variant Leaky ReLU in deep learning models, S-ReLU aims to further enhance performance by incorporating an S-shaped curvature into the activation function. The proposed S-ReLU has a logistic-like S-shaped form, which is more robust to extreme input values and allows the network to adapt to both positive and negative inputs effectively. To evaluate the efficacy of S-ReLU, we conduct extensive experiments on various deep learning architectures, including feedforward neural networks and convolutional neural networks, and compare their performance on a range of benchmark datasets. The results show that the S-ReLU significantly improves the convergence speed, validation accuracy, and overall performance of the network compared to traditional ReLU and other activation functions. Moreover, S-ReLU exhibits excellent robustness and stability even when trained on challenging tasks with noisy and imbalanced data. Through comprehensive analysis and visualization, this study sheds light on the black-box nature of deep learning models and provides insights into the inner workings of the proposed S-ReLU activation unit, establishing a solid foundation for further exploration and applications in complex data recognition and processing tasks. The findings of this study contribute to the quest for more efficient and adaptive activation functions in deep learning and offer a promising path for potential future research in this field.

title: Seeing through the Human Reporting Bias: Visual Classifiers from Noisy Human-Centric Labels
Abstract: Human reporting bias poses significant challenges in supervised learning tasks, particularly when labels are obtained from subjective human judgments. This paper delves into addressing the issues associated with noisy human-centric labels and their impact on the performance of machine learning models. Traditional deep learning architectures often find themselves entangled in the variability that arises from biased human annotations, resulting in suboptimal predictive outcomes and biased classifications. To mitigate these effects, this research focuses on developing novel visual classifiers capable of uncovering such inconsistencies. By integrating techniques drawn from active learning, transfer learning, and multi-task learning, we design algorithms that effectively filter and utilize the inherently noisy datasets for enhanced accuracy. The emphasis is on leveraging domain knowledge to develop specialized modules that identify and adapt to specific reporting biases. Furthermore, we propose an active learning framework that systematically samples the most informative and least confident instances, promoting model updates with greater relevance and accuracy. Through extensive experimental evaluations and benchmarking on diverse datasets, our proposed methodology demonstrates notable improvements in model performance, robustness, and interpretability compared to existing solutions. Ultimately, this work aims to empower the development of visual classifiers capable of distinguishing between genuine and report-biased data, fostering in a more reliable, equitable, and transparent machine learning paradigm.

title: Multi-Instance Visual-Semantic Embedding
Abstract: This abstract provides an overview of our proposed Multi-Instance Visual-Semantic Embedding (MIVE) framework, which effectively leverages the relationships between multiple instances and their corresponding semantic information to develop a robust and discriminative representation for image recognition tasks. Our approach primarily involves learning a compact yet informative embedding space where visual and semantic attributes of instances are cohesively integrated. To accomplish this, we develop a novel module named the Multi-Instance Fusion Network (MIFN) that promotes feature sharing and refinement between instances based on their semantic alignment. The MIFN module learns to adaptively interleave features from different instances, thereby minimizing the effects of instance-level variations and capturing the commonality inherent in a semantic class. We implement our MIVE framework within a wide range of visual classification tasks and report competitive performance against state-of-the-art methods on several benchmark datasets, including CUB-200-2011, Stanford Cars, and NABirds. The superior generalization capabilities of the proposed framework are mainly attributed to its ability to successfully transform the information contained within multiple instances into a compact, yet informative, feature representation that accurately captures the underlying semantic structure of the data. Notable results demonstrate our framework's efficacy in reducing the reliance on heuristics and solely learning the optimal representation from input data, thus fostering seamless deployment in real-world applications.

title: Transformed Residual Quantization for Approximate Nearest Neighbor Search
Abstract: Approximate Nearest Neighbor (ANN) search has become a crucial component in many computer vision and machine learning applications, where efficient similarity search is essential for tasks like image retrieval, object recognition, and clustering. However, the query time complexity of traditional ANN methods grows rapidly with the size of the database, making them impractical for large-scale applications. Recent advancements in learning-based approaches have brought significant improvements to ANN search, but they often suffer from high computational costs during training and inference. In this work, we propose a novel approach called Transformed Residual Quantization (TRQ) that leverages neural networks to learn compact and accurate quantization functions for efficient ANN search. By transforming the input data through a learned residual mapping, TRQ enables the use of simple quantization methods that are robust to data distribution shifts and outliers. Our experiments demonstrate that TRQ outperforms existing methods in terms of both search accuracy and scalability, with significant reductions in computational costs and memory usage. Additionally, we provide a thorough analysis of the design choices and trade-offs involved in TRQ, as well as insights into the learned representations and their impacts on ANN search performance. Our contributions offer a promising direction for efficient and accurate ANN search in various applications, including but not limited to, image and object recognition, and recommendation systems.

title: Car Segmentation and Pose Estimation using 3D Object Models
Abstract:
This paper presents a novel approach to car segmentation and pose estimation using 3D object models. The proposed method leverages the strengths of both machine learning and computer vision techniques to achieve accurate and robust performance on challenging real-world scenarios. A 3D object model is employed to encode the geometry and visual appearance of cars, which serves as the foundation for segmentation and pose estimation. The model is trained using a combination of synthetic and real-world datasets, resulting in a robust representation of diverse car models and their variability in shape, size, and pose.

The approach is based on a two-stage architecture, where the first stage focuses on car detection and segmentation, utilizing a region-proposal network and a convolutional neural network (CNN) for accurate bounding box localisation and binary segmentation mask generation. The outputs of the first stage are then fed into the second stage, which estimates the car's pose by computing the transformation parameters necessary to align the detected car with the 3D object model. The model is extensively evaluated on several benchmark datasets, demonstrating state-of-the-art performance in car segmentation and pose estimation. Compared to existing techniques, the proposed approach shows improved robustness against cluttered backgrounds, varying lighting conditions, and other sources of intra-class variability. The introduction of 3D object models also enables the prediction of more meaningful features such as car dimensions and orientation, opening up new possibilities for a range of applications including automated driving, surveillance, and inventory management.

title: Beyond Classification: Latent User Interests Profiling from Visual Contents Analysis
Abstract: This abstract explores the creation of a novel latent user interests profiling system, focusing on the analysis of visual contents to uncover users' underlying interests and preferences. Traditional classification methods often rely on explicit feedback or shallow features, failing to capture the rich and nuanced aspects of human interests. In contrast, our proposed approach delves into the subterranean realm of human interests by analyzing visual contents, such as images, videos, and social media posts. We combine state-of-the-art computer vision techniques with machine learning algorithms to uncover patterns and relationships within the visual data, allowing us to identify and represent latent user interests in a compact and interpretable form. The system is designed to be scalable, flexible, and adaptive, enabling it to handle diverse datasets and user behaviors. Through an extensive evaluation, we demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach in capturing users' latent interests, achieving higher accuracy and recall rates compared to existing methods. Furthermore, we provide insights into the application and potential societal impact of our research, including personalized content recommendation, targeted advertising, and user-centric product development. Our study paves the way for the development of more sophisticated and user-centric systems, which can effectively navigate the complexities of human interests and preferences.

title: GraphConnect: A Regularization Framework for Neural Networks
Abstract: GraphConnect is a novel regularization framework for neural networks that leverages the topological structure of the graph to improve the performance and generalizability of neural models. Traditional regularization techniques, such as dropout and early stopping, rely solely on the weighted connections between neurons, whereas GraphConnect utilizes the comprehensive graph representation of neural networks to identify and eliminate redundant and over-specialized nodes. By doing so, GraphConnect aims to reduce the overfitting issue commonly encountered in neural networks, thereby promoting a more generalized and robust model. In this work, we propose a regularization strategy that iteratively refines the neural graph by removing edges with low connectivity strengths, thereby distilling the neural network into a more compact and efficient structure. Our experiments demonstrate that GraphConnect consistently improves the test accuracy of state-of-the-art neural models and enhances their robustness to adversarial attacks. Furthermore, we investigate the impact of GraphConnect on the evolution of neural network architectures, revealing that this regularization technique promotes the emergence of more interpretable and modular neural structures. Our study contributes to a deeper understanding of the interplay between neural architecture and regularization, ultimately advancing the development of more accurate and efficient neural models.

title: Instance-Level Segmentation for Autonomous Driving with Deep Densely Connected MRFs
Abstract: This paper presents a novel instance-level segmentation approach for autonomous driving using deep densely connected Markov random fields (Densely Connected MRFs). The proposed method combines a state-of-the-art instance-level segmentation model with a densely connected MRF framework to effectively capture complex relationships between objects in the scene and improve segmentation accuracy. The densely connected MRF architecture leverages both spatial and contextual cues to learn hierarchical representations of the scene, enabling the model to accurately detect and segment individual objects, such as vehicles and pedestrians. The approach also introduces a novel object proposal network to generate high-quality object proposals, which are used to initialize the densely connected MRF framework. Comprehensive experiments on the KITTI and Cityscapes datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach, achieving state-of-the-art results in term of instance-level segmentation performance. Compared to existing methods, the proposed approach shows significant improvements in speed and accuracy, while also exhibiting robustness to complex scenarios and challenging environmental conditions. The methodology presented in this paper has the potential to be integrated into autonomous driving systems, enabling improved sensing and decision-making capabilities. By leveraging the strengths of densely connected MRFs and object proposal networks, the proposed approach provides a robust and efficient solution for instance-level segmentation in autonomous driving applications.

title: Multilinear Subspace Clustering
Abstract: Multilinear Subspace Clustering (MSC) is a powerful technique for clustering high-dimensional data that resides in multiple subspaces. This abstract provides a comprehensive review of MSC, from its basic principles to its theoretical foundations and practical applications. MSC models the data as a union of multiple low-dimensional subspaces, where each subspace corresponds to a specific cluster. By leveraging the multilinear properties of tensors, MSC can effectively detect and separate data points across different clusters, even when they are embedded in different low-dimensional subspaces. We provide an in-depth analysis of the MSC framework, including its optimization algorithms, convergence properties, and robustness to noise and outliers. Our review also covers various extensions of MSC, including its applications to different domains such as computer vision, signal processing, and bioinformatics. Furthermore, we highlight the challenges and open problems in MSC research, including scalability and interpretability issues, and provide future research directions to address these challenges. By providing a thorough exposition of MSC, this review aims to facilitate a better understanding of this powerful clustering technique among researchers and practitioners, and to inspire further innovation in this exciting area of research.

title: Sparse Coding with Fast Image Alignment via Large Displacement Optical Flow
Abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to sparse coding with fast image alignment via large displacement optical flow. We propose a unified framework that leverages the recent advances in deep learning and sparse representation theory to achieve high-speed image registration and alignment. Our approach involves two concurrent processes: a learnable sparse coding module that generates sparse representations of patches, and a large displacement optical flow module that estimates the dense flow field between the input images. The performance of our module is improved by using a large displacement and deep learning architectures to enhance the accuracy and compute efficiency of the optical flow estimation process. Our model is trained end-to-end via a multi-task loss function, which combines the differences between the ground truth and estimated sparse codes, as well as the average end-point errors between the ground truth and estimated optical flow. Experimental results demonstrate that our approach achieves state-of-the-art performance on several benchmarks, including Middlebury Optical Flow dataset, which utilizes challenging test cases such as glass on glass, textureless areas, and slippery motion, providing a strong validation for the performance of our method when applied to more complex types of vision data. Overall, our approach is well-suited for applications requiring high-speed image registration, alignment, and matching, such as motion estimation for optical flow, stereo matching, surveillance systems, video compression, and object tracking in surveillance systems.

title: Deep Learning for Surface Material Classification Using Haptic And Visual Information
Abstract: This paper presents a novel deep learning-based approach for surface material classification, leveraging both haptic and visual information. By incorporating tactile feedback into the classification process, our method aims to improve the accuracy and robustness of surface material recognition. We propose a multi-modal fusion framework that concurrently processes visual and haptic data, using a combination of convolutional neural networks (CNNs) and graph neural networks (GNNs). The visual CNN module is designed to extract features from RGB images of surfaces, while the haptic GNN module captures the topological and geometric attributes of tactile interactions. We develop a weighted fusion mechanism to combine the outputs of the two modules, allowing the model to adaptively assign greater emphasis to either the visual or haptic information based on the specific task requirements. Our experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method significantly outperforms traditional single-modal and single-task learning approaches, achieving state-of-the-art performance on several surface material classification benchmarks. Furthermore, the results highlight the effectiveness of incorporating haptic feedback in material recognition tasks, particularly in scenarios where surfaces exhibit subtle variations in texture, color, or reflectance. Overall, this research provides a foundational framework for developing intelligent systems that can redundantly classify surface materials using a synergistic combination of visual and haptic modalities.

title: Local and global gestalt laws: A neurally based spectral approach
Abstract: This paper delves into the realm of Gestalt laws that govern how visual information is organized and perceived in the human visual system. Local and global Gestalt laws have been studied extensively in the context of human perception and cognition, with a primary focus on the phenomenological and empirical aspects of these laws. However, this study adopts a more nuanced approach by integrating insights from neural networks and computational modeling to provide a more fundamental understanding of these Gestalt laws. We propose a neurally-based spectral approach to quantify the global and local perceptual organization that underlies human visual perception, drawing on concepts from signal processing and neural coding theories. Through a combination of computational modeling and neurophysiological evidence, we demonstrate that local and global Gestalt laws can be effectively characterized in terms of spectral features, which capture the temporal and spatial structure of visual stimuli. Our approach reveals that the global Gestalt laws are associated with high-frequency spectral components, which reflect the rapid extraction of spatial information, while the local Gestalt laws are linked to low-frequency spectral components, which encompass the gradual buildup of contextual information. The integration of neural and spectrotemporal analysis provides a robust framework for unraveling the neural basis of Gestalt laws, offering new avenues for understanding the intricate processes that underpin human visual perception.

title: Analysis of Vessel Connectivities in Retinal Images by Cortically Inspired Spectral Clustering
Abstract: This study presents a novel approach to analyzing vessel connectivities in retinal images using cortically inspired spectral clustering, an unsupervised learning technique loosely based on the principles of neural processing in the cerebral cortex. The proposed method leverages the graph-theoretic representation of images, incorporating the structural and spatial information from retinal vasculature into a spectral clustering framework designed to capture contextual relationships between neighboring pixels. By exploiting local connectivity patterns and spectral centrality indices, the technique has the potential to outline the intricate network structures that underpin the complex vascular architecture of the retina, with implications for early disease detection and risk stratification. Experimental results demonstrating the efficacy of the proposed method against state-of-the-art retinal image analysis techniques highlight its ability to identify subtle aberrations in vessel connectivity patterns associated with diabetic retinopathy, AMD, and hypertension. The developed framework offers a powerful tool for exploring the intricate vascular networks within the retina, priming the ground for future investigations into the pathophysiology of ocular and systemic diseases, and paving the way for innovative image analysis applications across a range of biomedical disciplines.

title: Spatial Phase-Sweep: Increasing temporal resolution of transient imaging using a light source array
Abstract: Spatial Phase-Sweep: Increasing temporal resolution of transient imaging using a light source array is a novel approach that seeks to push the boundaries of image acquisition techniques in fields such as materials science, vision science, and medical imaging. Traditional imaging methods often rely on a single light source, which inherently limits the temporal resolution achievable in transient imaging applications. To address this constraint, our work proposes the utilization of a light source array, wherein multiple intensity-modulated emitters are strategically arranged to simultaneously illuminate the object of interest. By integrating the spatially swept phase information from each light source, our spatial phase-sweep method significantly enhances the temporal resolution of transient imaging, allowing for the acquisition of high-fidelity spatiotemporal data essential for understanding dynamic phenomena. The spatial phase-sweep technique exhibits exceptional robustness against light source inhomogeneities, enabling its widespread applicability in imaging scenarios where precise control over illumination is vital. Through a combination of theoretical derivations, simulations, and experimental validations, our research demonstrates the efficacy of spatial phase-sweep in significantly upgrading the temporal resolution of transient imaging and reveals its immense potential in imaging multiple transient phenomena associated with high-speed processes.

title: Harnessing the Deep Net Object Models for Enhancing Human Action Recognition
Abstract: Deep net object models have gained significant attention in recent years for their ability to recognize complex human actions accurately. These models learn to capture subtle spatial and temporal cues from videos to categorize various human actions. However, the effectiveness of these models heavily relies on the quality and quantity of training data, often comprising thousands of hours of annotated videos. This paper explores the potential of harnessing deep net object models to enhance human action recognition. We conducted a comprehensive review of existing research and evaluated state-of-the-art models, including 3D convolutional neural networks (CNNs), recurrent neural networks (RNNs), and graph neural networks (GNNs), to understand their strengths and weaknesses. We also designed and implemented a novel data augmentation technique by incorporating transfer learning from object recognition models to improve the generalization of action recognition models. Our experiments demonstrated that the proposed method can significantly enhance the recognition accuracy of human actions, especially when dealing with noisy or incomplete data. Furthermore, we investigated the possibility of utilizing pre-trained object models to detect and recognize human actions in a more efficient and effective manner. The results of our study suggest that deep net object models hold great promise for improving human action recognition tasks and can be beneficial for applications in surveillance, automation, and human-computer interaction.

title: Remote Health Coaching System and Human Motion Data Analysis for Physical Therapy with Microsoft Kinect
Abstract: This paper proposes a remote health coaching system integrated with human motion data analysis for physical therapy using Microsoft Kinect technology. The main objective is to provide patients with a non-invasive, cost-effective, and data-driven approach to rehabilitation after injury or surgery. The system utilizes a Kinect sensor to capture and track patient movement, enabling the analysis of kinematic data such as joint angles, trajectories, and velocities. Advanced algorithms are applied to process this data, providing accurate assessments of movement quality, symmetry, and range of motion. Machine learning techniques are employed to identify patterns and anomalies in the data, facilitating the early detection of potential complications or setbacks in the rehabilitation process. The system is designed to be accessible and user-friendly, allowing patients to conduct exercises and movement assessments remotely, with real-time feedback and coaching provided by healthcare professionals. The proposed system has the potential to improve patient outcomes, reduce healthcare costs, and increase accessibility to physical therapy services, particularly in underserved or rural areas. In this research, we present the design and development of the remote health coaching system, highlighting its technical capabilities, clinical applications, and future directions for implementation and research. The system's efficacy is evaluated through a case study involving patients with varying physical therapy needs, demonstrating its potential to enhance rehabilitation outcomes and patient engagement.

title: Quantized Convolutional Neural Networks for Mobile Devices
Abstract: The development of mobile devices has enabled widespread adoption of mobile applications and machine learning systems, but their limited computational resources pose a significant challenge to the efficient deployment of deep neural networks. Traditional convolutional neural networks (CNNs) tend to be computationally expensive and memory-intensive, leading to significant energy consumption and latency, making them less suitable for mobile devices. This paper explores the application of quantization techniques to reduce the computational and memory requirements of CNNs, with the aim of improving their performance on mobile devices. Quantized CNNs represent the weights and activations of the neural network using lower precision data types, such as integers, to reduce the computational complexity of matrix multiplications and memory usage. This can lead to significant reductions in energy consumption and latency, making them more suitable for deployment on mobile devices. In this paper, we design and implement a range of quantization techniques, including weight and activation quantization, and comparative experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of quantization in improving the performance of CNNs on mobile devices. The results of this study show that the quantized CNNs achieve comparable accuracy to their full-precision counterparts while reducing the computational speedup and memory usage by up to 80% and 70%, respectively.

title: Kernel principal component analysis network for image classification
Abstract: This paper introduces a novel deep learning framework, kernel principal component analysis network (KPCAN), for image classification tasks. By combining the strengths of kernel principal component analysis (KPCA) and convolutional neural networks (CNNs), KPCAN is designed to effectively capture the complex, non-linear relationships within high-dimensional image data. To address the issue of high-dimensional feature spaces, KPCAN applies KPCA to transform the data into a lower-dimensional feature space prior to the classification stage, significantly reducing the computational complexity and the risk of overfitting associated with traditional CNN approaches. Additionally, KPCAN incorporates gated recurrent units (GRUs) to facilitate the learning of temporal dependencies and contextual information from sequential input data. Experimental results demonstrate that KPCAN outperforms state-of-the-art image classification algorithms, including deep learning-based architectures, in terms of accuracy and robustness, achieving a competitive performance on benchmark datasets such as CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, and ImageNet. Furthermore, the proposed framework's ability to adapt to the geometry of the input data and its robustness to various types of distortions make it an attractive option for real-world image classification applications.

title: Neutro-Connectedness Cut
Abstract: The Neutro-Connectedness Cut is a novel concept that bridges the gap between graph theory and data mining. By introducing a new paradigm for analyzing and visualizing complex networks, this framework provides a unified approach to understanding the structural attributes of interconnected data. The Neutro-Connectedness Cut operates on the premise that connectivity is a multifaceted property, influenced by both structural and attribute-specific relationships within a graph. Through a combination of mathematical derivations and empirical validations, this work demonstrates the effectiveness of Neutro-Connectedness Cut in detecting influential nodes, uncovering community structures, and identifying anomalous patterns in network behavior. The proposed algorithmic framework, which leverages techniques from graph theory and machine learning, enables the development of a robust data mining tool for various applications, including social network analysis, recommendation systems, and epidemic modeling. Results from empirical studies conducted on both synthetic and real-world datasets demonstrate the superiority of Neutro-Connectedness Cut in capturing the intricate dynamics of complex networks, offering a compelling alternative to existing methods that rely on simplistic connectivity metrics. By providing a more nuanced understanding of network characteristics, Neutro-Connectedness Cut has the potential to revolutionize the field of graph analysis and data mining, enabling scholars and practitioners to uncover previously hidden patterns and relationships within interconnected data.

title: Multistage SFM: A Coarse-to-Fine Approach for 3D Reconstruction
Abstract: This paper introduces a novel multistage Structure-from-Motion (SFM) method, designed to tackle the complexity of 3D reconstruction from large-scale unordered image collections. Traditional SFM algorithms often struggle with scenes featuring repetitive or textured structures, which can lead to misalignment issues and correspondences with low reliability. To address these limitations, our proposed framework employs a coarse-to-fine strategy, starting with a preliminary step that entails the identification of distinctive geometric patterns and anomalies. This initial analysis serves as the foundation for a subsequent enhancement phase, during which iterated pairwise matching and robust feature optimization processes are applied to enrich data association and, subsequently, 3D structure recovery. By adopting a coarse-to-fine approach, our Multistage SFM strategy facilitates refined model generation and robust image alignment in scenes characterized by challenging topological factors. Meanwhile, comparison experiments against other popular reconstruction techniques in real-world datasets demonstrate our framework's ability to deliver improved 3D reconstruction performance in terms of both precision and efficiency. While providing an essential context for practical deployment within applications requiring accurate 3D mapping and modeling, our systematic treatment of scale-aware matching, geometric validation, and optimization also highlights potential avenues for further methodological development in the broader spectrum of the computer vision community.

title: Combining patch-based strategies and non-rigid registration-based label fusion methods
Abstract: This paper presents an innovative approach to medical image segmentation by seamlessly integrating patch-based strategies and non-rigid registration-based label fusion methods. Traditional image segmentation techniques often struggle to accurately capture intricate anatomical structures and variations, particularly in CT and MRI scans of organs such as the liver and brain. To address this challenge, a novel framework is proposed, leveraging the strengths of both patch-based and registration-based approaches. The patch-based strategy involves segmenting the input image into smaller regions, each of which is further processed using a deep learning-based network, enabling the model to learn complex patterns and relationships within the image. In parallel, a non-rigid registration-based method is employed to align the input image with a corresponding label image, thus robustly transferring the label information to the target image. This hybrid approach exploits the respective merits of patch-based and registration-based methods, allowing for the accurate segmentation of even the most complex anatomical structures. Experimental results demonstrate the superior performance of the proposed framework compared to state-of-the-art methods, showcasing its potential for wide-ranging applications in medical imaging analysis and clinical decision-making. Furthermore, the study highlights the importance of developing robust and adaptive segmentation algorithms that can accommodate varying imaging modalities and anatomical variations, ultimately contributing to improved clinical outcomes and enhanced patient care.

title: Poseidon: A System Architecture for Efficient GPU-based Deep Learning on Multiple Machines
Abstract: Poseidon is a novel system architecture designed to efficiently leverage the power of GPU-based deep learning on multiple machines, thereby tackling the computation-intensive problems associated with large-scale image and speech recognition tasks. Our proposed architecture streamlines the communication among distributed nodes and enables seamless scale-up and scale-down of computations as per the requirement. At the heart of our design is a heterogenous node cluster comprising CPU and GPU-based systems that are interconnected via a robust and low-latency interconnect. By harnessing the advantage of GPUs for accelerating floating point computations, each node in the cluster is capable of executing dense matrix multiplication and activation functions concurrently, thereby significantly enhancing the overall memory-bandwidth and FLOP efficiency. Furthermore, Poseidon incorporates an auto-tuning framework specifically designed to adaptively configure resource allocation and parameter tuning for minimizing the inter-node communication and synchronization overhead in distributed deep learning pipelines. Comprehensive performance evaluations have demonstrated that Poseidon delivers 10-25-fold speedup over several representative state-of-the-art deep learning benchmark and provides up to 4x reduction in memory overhead compared to existing solutions, thus showcasing its potential to serve as a highly scalable, adaptable, and efficient deep learning platform.

title: Modeling Colors of Single Attribute Variations with Application to Food Appearance
Abstract: This research focuses on developing a computational framework to predict and simulate color variations of foods under single attribute changes. Color appearance plays a significant role in consumer perception and product quality, yet its modeling remains a significant challenge in the food industry. Current developments in color science suggest the need for more mechanistic approaches to color prediction, moving beyond existing empirical models that do not account for underlying physical mechanisms. To address this gap, we leveraged advances in computer vision, machine learning, and material science to create a model integrating reflectance spectroscopy, pigment interactions, and observer perception. Our approach entails the analysis of chromatographic and spectroscopic data linked to computational geometry to accurately model food structures at the nanoscale and their physical optical properties, including pigment intermolecular forces, particle structure, and optical anisotropy. Upon simulating and predicting color responses, we found robust correlations with experimental color data, effectively demonstrating the utility and potential of our model for practical food color optimization. Moreover, case studies of a range of product images further illustrated its proficiency in modeling the effects of ingredient substitution, drying, extraction, and cooking procedures. Implications include expedited product development, streamlined production workflows through decreased testing stages leading to reduced product waste, accelerated formulations and possible development of new food products.

title: Multiclass Classification of Cervical Cancer Tissues by Hidden Markov Model
Abstract: This study presents a novel approach to multiclass classification of cervical cancer tissues using a Hidden Markov Model (HMM). The goal of this research is to develop an effective and efficient method for diagnosing cervical cancer, a leading cause of morbidity and mortality worldwide. In recent years, HMM has gained increasing attention in the field of image analysis and pattern recognition due to its ability to model complex and sequential data. By combining HMM with machine learning and image processing techniques, we propose a hierarchical framework for classifying cervical cancer tissues into different grades of severity. Our approach involves pre-processing the Pap smear images to extract relevant features, which are then fed into a HMM-based classifier. The classifier is trained on a dataset of labeled images, which consists of normal and abnormal cervical cells, and is evaluated on a separate test dataset. The results show that our proposed framework achieves a classification accuracy of 92.5%, significantly outperforming existing methods. The proposed approach also provides a clear visualization of the classification process, allowing clinicians to gain insights into the underlying mechanisms of cervical cancer development. This research has significant implications for the development of a diagnostic tool for early detection and prevention of cervical cancer, and can potentially be extended to other types of diseases and medical imaging modalities.

title: Face Hallucination using Linear Models of Coupled Sparse Support
Abstract: Face hallucination is a challenging problem in computer vision where the goal is to synthesize a face with high resolution from its degraded low-resolution counterpart. In this context, recent studies have demonstrated that coupled sparse support (CSS) can be an effective framework for face hallucination. Nevertheless, CSS-based methods often fail in practical applications due to their vulnerability to noise and occlusion. To overcome these limitations, this paper proposes a novel face hallucination method based on linear models of coupled sparse support (LMCSS). The proposed method involves two main stages: first, it utilizes sparse representation to extract the coupled sparse support from both the input low-resolution face and its degraded counterpart; second, it leverages linear models to reconstruct the face from the extracted coupled sparse support. The LMCSS model is designed by taking into account the non-linearity of the face imaging process, as well as the relationships between different facial features. Extensive experiments demonstrate that the proposed approach outperforms existing methods in various scenarios, including noise, occlusion, and pose variations. Additionally, the proposed method achieves better subjective quality and user acceptance in face hallucination tasks.

title: Deformable Distributed Multiple Detector Fusion for Multi-Person Tracking
Abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to multi-person tracking by introducing a deformable distributed multiple detector fusion framework. The framework utilizes a hierarchical architecture that combines the strengths of both conventional and deep-learning-based object detection methods to accurately identify individual pedestrians within crowded scenes. The deformable design of the framework enables it to adapt to varying individual poses, actions, and clothing styles, which is essential for reliable multi-person tracking. By utilizing a distributed configuration, the proposed framework can efficiently handle complex scenarios with numerous individuals, reducing computational overhead and improving real-time performance. A key component of the framework is a novel detector fusion module that effectively combines the outputs of conventional detectors and deep convolutional neural networks to generate a robust estimate of object locations and identities. The proposed framework is extensively evaluated using a range of challenging multi-person tracking benchmarks, demonstrating significant improvements over state-of-the-art methods in terms of accuracy and robustness. The results highlight the potential of the proposed deformable distributed multiple detector fusion framework to overcome the limitations of existing multi-person tracking solutions and provide valuable insights for real-world applications.

title: Can Pretrained Neural Networks Detect Anatomy?
Abstract: This study investigates the ability of pretrained neural networks to detect anatomical structures from medical images. The research focuses on a wide range of imaging modalities including MRI and CT scans, and evaluates the performance of various convolutional neural network architectures, both in isolation and in combination with transfer learning techniques. The results demonstrate that even without fine-tuning or explicit anatomical knowledge, pretrained neural networks exhibit remarkable robustness in correctly identifying anatomical structures. The accuracy of detection appears to be influenced by the image quality, resolution, and the presence of abnormalities. Furthermore, the study reveals that models trained on large, publicly available datasets can generalize well across different datasets and domain shifts, even when trained on image specific modalities. However, it is also observed that deeper models achieve higher detection accuracy but are also more prone to overfitting when trained on smaller datasets. These findings have significant implications for medical imaging research, hinting that the burgeoning trend of utilising already trained models can be effectively used with new data, with relative ease and acceptable accuracy. Additionally, the experiments provide insights into existing techniques and shed light on the avenues to explore for enhanced anatomy detection capabilities in neural networks.

title: Domain Adaptation and Transfer Learning in StochasticNets
Abstract: This paper delves into the realm of stochastic neural nets, a paradigm that emerges as a unifier of multiple prior research directions across deep learning, empirical probability, and stochastics. Aiming to reconcile the seemingly disparate components of the field and thereby yielding more seamless and expressive neural network constructions, stochasticNets introduce models that train neural networks in an inherently probabilistic manner without the sacrifice of probabilistic interpretability. The underlying probability fields inherent to stochasticNets allows for principled domain adaptation and transfer learning methodologies. By understanding the respective probability measures implemented in stochasticNets throughout differing problem-terms or the variations of environment related to both the domain adaption as well as the transfer learning tasks, we uncover the underlying framework behind how stochasticNets adapt models from one application regime to another, fostering deeper interpretation as well as integration of heterogeneous, data-driven tasks. Statistical techniques are intertwined with neural architectures in order to create unique meta-learning strategies. Through analytical and practical means, this paper further proposes an efficacious combination of probabilistic representations with the corresponding deep learning architecture facilitating an enhanced analysis of probabilistic model-based transfer learning and domain adaptation in stochasticNets. As a result of these methods, challenging and diverse applicative applications might be more adeptly solved.

title: Relay Backpropagation for Effective Learning of Deep Convolutional Neural Networks
Abstract: Relay Backpropagation leverages a mediator node to parallelize the forward and backward passes of deep neural networks, achieving significant efficiency gains in both computer power usage as well as in computational cost. The proposed neural network implementation overcomes conventional one forward propagations per epoch with just one for training data. This efficient backpropagation method in connection with the mediator has been compared in various deep neural network operations. Relay Backpropagation networks show substantial efficiency, and speed. A core part of this model works using multiple nodes to augment as required. Based on preliminary outcomes, relay backpropagation is clearly a more viable approach when compared to other method-based network structures in terms of efficiency. It takes support from the fact that backpropagation plays a highly significant role in computations that are mandatory for the production and development of deep network-architectures. Data efficiency has reduced upon relay backpropagation facilitating the training of network models that consists of immense numbers of units- learning algorithms for extensive amounts of data sets. Back propagation is most valuable for network-configuration by ensuring that it gets minimized and the result efficiently gets maximized. Implementation of relay backpropagation methods into deep network models will solve the constraints of computationally-intensive requirements better and higher learning outcomes were observed.

title: Probabilistic Programming with Gaussian Process Memoization
Abstract: This research presents an innovative probabilistic programming approach that integrates Gaussian process memoization to enhance the scalability and efficiency of probabilistic computation. By leveraging the kernel trick, we developed a Gaussian process-based memoization technique that enables the caching of intermediate computations and reuses them to avoid redundant updates in probabilistic models. Our approach, dubbed GPmemo, eliminates the need for exhaustive re-computation by leveraging the non-negative semi-definite gram matrix and using a pre-computed look-up table to store previous computations. The GPmemo technique has the advantage of being adaptive, allowing it to focus on regions of the parameter space where there is high uncertainty and thus improve the efficiency of probabilistic computations. Furthermore, our approach provides improved robustness against model complexity and large datasets, enabling the efficient inference of complex probabilistic models. We demonstrate the effectiveness of GPmemo on various probabilistic programming tasks, including Bayesian linear regression, variational inference, and probabilistic neural networks, achieving up to 100x speedup over traditional probabilistic programming methods. Our results show that GPmemo offers a novel and promising solution for accelerating probabilistic programming and opening the door to new applications in machine learning and data science. By providing an efficient and scalable solution for probabilistic computation, GPmemo has the potential to democratize access to probabilistic programming and enable widespread adoption in real-world applications.

title: Reconstruction of Enhanced Ultrasound Images From Compressed Measurements Using Simultaneous Direction Method of Multipliers
Abstract: This paper presents an innovative approach to enhance ultrasound images reconstructed from compressed measurements using the simultaneous direction method of multipliers (SDMM). The framework is designed to address the challenges associated with the limited resolution and compressed data inherent in ultrasound imaging. By leveraging the strengths of alternating direction methods and accelerated gradient methods, SDMM significantly accelerates the reconstruction process, allowing for faster and more efficient image formation. The core contribution of the proposed method lies in its ability to jointly optimize the sparse representation of the reconstructed image and the regularized optimization problem, leading to exceptional reconstruction quality and computational efficiency. To evaluate the efficacy of the proposed approach, a comparison is made with existing methods, including total variation regularization, Huber function-based method, and gradient descent algorithms. The results reveal that the SDMM outperforms these alternative methods in terms of peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR), structural similarity index (SSIM), and visual quality assessment. Extensive experiments are conducted on both synthetic and real-world ultrasound image datasets, demonstrating the effectiveness of the SDMM in reconstructing high-quality images from severely compressed measurements. This work has significant implications for the development of more efficient and accurate imaging modalities in various medical diagnosis and therapeutic applications.

title: Large Scale Business Discovery from Street Level Imagery
Abstract: This paper presents an innovative approach to large scale business discovery from street level imagery, which utilizes a complementary combination of Deep Learning and Geospatial technologies to identify and analyze businesses in high-resolution urban images. Our proposed method employs a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) to locate businesses, segment them from their surroundings, and recognize their respective attributes such as type, operational hours, and revenue. We have developed a dataset containing annotated images of various businesses, which serves as a gold standard for the evaluation of our proposed approach. Experimental results demonstrate an improvement in the accuracy of business discovery by leveraging contextual information from high-resolution images. We validate the effectiveness of our proposed approach on real-world datasets, comprising over 1 million street-level images, acquired from various cities around the world. This research has extensive applications in urban planning, economic development, and business intelligence, providing valuable insights into the spatiotemporal dynamics of businesses in urban areas. title: Numerical Demultiplexing of Color Image Sensor Measurements via Non-linear Random Forest Modeling
Abstract: This research paper presents a novel numerical demultiplexing framework for color image sensor measurements utilizing non-linear random forest modeling. Color image sensors are increasingly being utilized in various applications, including surveillance, medical imaging, and automotive vision systems, to capture high-quality images. However, these sensors typically produce raw data consisting of three color channels, which are multiplexed together, resulting in significant noise and interference. Traditional demultiplexing methods often employ linear techniques, which are insufficient in accurately reconstructing the original color image due to the non-linear nature of the multiplexing process. To address this limitation, we propose a non-linear random forest model to demultiplex the color image sensor measurements. Our model leverages the random forest algorithm's ability to capture complex non-linear relationships between the input features and outputs, thereby allowing for accurate demultiplexing of the multiplexed color channels. We evaluate the proposed framework on a range of color image sensor datasets and demonstrate its superiority over existing linear demultiplexing methods. The results show that our non-linear random forest model achieves improved image quality, reduced noise, and enhanced color accuracy, making it a promising solution for various color image sensor applications. This research contributes to the development of advanced demultiplexing techniques for color image sensors and has the potential to improve the quality of images captured by these sensors.

title: Ranking genetic factors related to age-related maculardegeneration by variable selection confidence sets
Abstract: This study presents an ensemble variable selection method, combined with confidence sets, to identify and rank genetic factors significantly associated with age-related macular degeneration (AMD). Based on a comprehensive analysis of genome-wide association study (GWAS) data for AMD, our approach systematically evaluates multiple feature selection algorithms to capture the underlying genetic architecture of the disease. By incorporating the concept of confidence sets, this framework provides a rigorous and transparent framework to quantify the reliability of selected genetic variants. Comparative evaluations using GWAS data from independent cohorts demonstrate that the proposed ensemble method outperforms traditional single-model approaches in identifying AMD-relevant genome-wide significant SNPs, while also accurately capturing a substantial proportion of associated but genome-wide nominally significant SNPs. Case-control studies revealed that a significant proportion of these captured SNPs are consistently strongly associated with AMD-related phenotypes, thereby refining our understanding of disease genetics. This study demonstrates the potential of using ensemble methods with confidence sets as a synergistic approach to refine our current understanding of how genetic variants collectively contribute to the complex etiology of AMD. The implicated SNPs are systematically prioritized based on their variable selection confidence, thereby translating our approach into a practical tool for genetic risk analysis that can aid in subsequent replication studies, clinical diagnostics, and potentially therapeutic interventions.

title: Multiregion Bilinear Convolutional Neural Networks for Person Re-Identification
Abstract: Person re-identification is a challenging task in computer vision that involves identifying individuals across different cameras and scenes. The task's complexity arises from various factors such as viewpoint changes, lighting conditions, and occlusions. Recent advancements in deep learning have led to the development of bilinear convolutional neural networks (B-CNNs) which can learn interactions between different feature maps, achieving state-of-the-art performance in various tasks. However, most existing B-CNN architectures have been designed for single-region inputs, limiting their performance when dealing with multiregion features. In this work, we propose a multiregion bilinear CNN (MRB-CNN) architecture specifically designed for person re-identification tasks. Our proposed model consists of two distinct branches that learn interactions between different feature maps across multiple regions. The proposed MRB-CNN model is compared against state-of-the-art person re-identification architectures, yielding significant improvements in identification performance. Extensive evaluations on several benchmark datasets demonstrate that MRB-CNN can effectively capture complex spatial relationships and variability in person appearance, leading to its robustness across different scenarios. This research work contributes to the vision community by shedding new light on advanced deep learning architectures for person re-identification, and paves the way for a wide range of applications in surveillance and monitoring systems, where robust and accurate identification of individuals is crucial.

title: Shape and Spatially-Varying Reflectance Estimation From Virtual Exemplars
Abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to estimate 3D shape and spatially-varying reflectance properties of real-world objects using virtual exemplars. Our method leverages the vast availability of photorealistic virtual 3D models and their corresponding rendering records to learn a robust and generalizable model of material appearance and geometric structure. We introduce a two-stage learning framework that first reconstructs the virtual exemplar's shape and normal map using a template-based method, and subsequently infers the material's reflectance properties by analyzing the rendering records and registered real-world photographs of the object. The core of our approach lies in designing a spatial mapping block to accurately align the virtual reflectance maps with their corresponding real-world observations, thus effectively capturing the spatially-varying geometry and material properties of objects. To evaluate the efficacy of our method, we conducted extensive experiments on a comprehensive dataset consisting of 15 real-world objects with diverse shapes and materials, as well as their corresponding virtual exemplars. Our results show that our model can predict highly accurate shape and reflectance maps for objects with varying levels of complexity and detail, demonstrating its potential for use in various applications, such as material analysis, computer vision, and computer graphics. By leveraging virtual exemplars, our method offers a computationally efficient and scalable solution for real-world shape and reflectance estimation, bridging the gap between photorealistic virtual models and real-world observations.

title: Blockout: Dynamic Model Selection for Hierarchical Deep Networks
Abstract: Hierarchical deep networks have become increasingly popular in recent years, especially in tasks involving multi-scale or multi-level representations such as computer vision and natural language processing. This proliferation has led to the development of numerous architectures and models, each optimized for different data distributions and tasks. However, selecting the most appropriate model for a given problem still remains a significant challenge, often requiring extensive domain knowledge and trial-and-error experimentation. To overcome this limitation, we propose Blockout, a novel approach that utilizes a novel dynamic model selection mechanism to adaptively choose the most suitable model within a hierarchical deep network, given the input data characteristics. By leveraging a spatial attention mechanism and a hierarchical inference strategy, Blockout identifies and selectively employs sub-networks that are best suited for specific input features, resulting in improved overall performance and reduced computational overhead. Through a comprehensive set of experiments on various benchmarks and tasks, including image classification, object detection, and language modeling, we demonstrate the efficacy of Blockout in achieving state-of-the-art results while exhibiting superior scalability and flexibility compared to traditional, fixed-architecture approaches. Our results indicate that Blockout can effectively navigate the complex space of hierarchical deep networks, discovering and exploiting novel representation modes that have the potential to revolutionize the field of deep learning.

title: Fine-grained Categorization and Dataset Bootstrapping using Deep Metric Learning with Humans in the Loop
Abstract: Fine-grained categorization, the process of distinguishing between closely related classes within a larger categorization system, is a fundamental challenge in various machine learning applications. The development of deep metric learning based methods has greatly improved the performance of object categorization tasks, however, creating the necessary training datasets for such methods often requires substantial human effort and resources. This is especially true for fine-grained categories where differences between classes may be almost imperceptible to the average person. This paper investigates the creation of training datasets for fine-grained categorization tasks using a hybrid approach that integrates human input with deep metric learning strategies. Through the integration of humans in the loop, we aim to improve the accuracy and efficiency of dataset creation and further apply it to fine-grained object recognition tasks. Our proposed iterative framework bootstraps from an initial coarsely labeled dataset and gradually refines it through active learning strategies that adaptively select the most informative samples for human labeling. The collected dataset and accompanying algorithms yield competitive performance on several benchmark datasets for object recognition, while accounting for the variability in human labeling accuracy and expertise, demonstrating the feasibility of hybrid approaches for fine-grained categorization tasks.

title: Effects of GIMP Retinex Filtering Evaluated by the Image Entropy
Abstract: This study investigates the effects of GIMP Retinex filtering on image entropy as a quantitative measure of image quality. The Retinex theory of color vision, formulated by Land and McCann in the 1970s, has been widely used in image processing to model the human visual system. However, its application in image filtering has been less explored, particularly in open-source image processing tools like the GNU Image Manipulation Program (GIMP). The present research evaluates the impact of GIMP Retinex filtering on image entropy by applying different Retinex algorithms, including the multiscale Retinex and the white-patch Retinex, to a diverse set of images with varying levels of noise, contrast, and texture. The results show that the GIMP Retinex filtering has a significant impact on image entropy, with a decrease in entropy corresponding to a perceived improvement in image quality. Notably, the multiscale Retinex algorithm exhibits the most pronounced effect on image entropy, particularly in images with high levels of noise and texture. The findings of this study reveal that GIMP Retinex filtering can be used to effectively restore and enhance image quality by adjusting the filtering parameters to optimize image entropy. The study's results contribute to the understanding of the effects of GIMP Retinex filtering on image entropy and highlight its potential applications in image processing and enhancement technologies, including photography, medicine, and surveillance systems.

title: Multiple penalized principal curves: analysis and computation
Abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to multiple penalized principal curves, which enables the recovery of multiple principal curves from high-dimensional data while incorporating regularization and group-sparse penalties. Our framework, dubbed Multiple Penalized Principal Curves (MPPC), addresses the challenges posed by existing single-curve methods, such as their inability to capture non-linear relationships and their sensitivity to outliers. By incorporating group-sparse penalties, MPPC identifies multiple principal curves that exhibit a sparse and structured representation of the data. We develop an algorithmic framework for computing the MPPC and provide theoretical guarantees for the method, demonstrating its consistency and convergence properties in various scenarios. Empirical studies on both simulated and real-world datasets showcase the efficacy of MPPC in discovering hierarchical and grouped patterns, highlighting its potential applications in fields such as image analysis, medicine, and social network analysis. In contrast to existing methods, MPPC offers an interpretable and robust approach to multiple-curve recovery, which facilitates the understanding of complex data structures. Furthermore, our theoretical and numerical results underscore the versatility and accuracy of the proposed MPPC framework, which can be successfully employed to uncover meaningful relationships within high-dimensional data.

title: Context Driven Label Fusion for segmentation of Subcutaneous and Visceral Fat in CT Volumes
Abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to the challenging task of segmenting subcutaneous and visceral fat in computed tomography (CT) volumes. Current deep learning-based methods for fat segmentation often struggle to distinguish between these two types of fat, which have significant implications for clinical diagnosis and treatment of metabolic diseases. Our proposed method, Context Driven Label Fusion (CDLF), addresses this challenge by introducing a fusion strategy that combines the strengths of different labeling schemes. Specifically, we utilize a combination of pixel-wise segmentation, regional labeling, and label uncertainty estimation to refine the segmentation results. Through the use of context-driven fusion, CDLF is able to leverage the relative strengths of each labeling scheme and improve overall segmentation accuracy. Our evaluation on a range of CT datasets with varying image quality and patient demographics demonstrates that CDLF outperforms state-of-the-art methods in terms of fat-separating accuracy and robustness to image noise. Moreover, our analysis of the labeling scheme distribution reveals that CDLF is more adept at detecting and quantifying the subtle differences between subcutaneous and visceral fat, making it a valuable tool for clinical research and diagnostics. The findings of this study highlight the potential of CDLF to revolutionize the field of fat segmentation and provide a significant step forward in the diagnosis and treatment of metabolic diseases.

title: On Deep Representation Learning from Noisy Web Images
Abstract: Deep representation learning from noisy web images is a challenging task due to the presence of diverse and complex data including varying resolutions, perspective distortions, occlusions, and object mislabeling, ultimately leading to decreased network accuracy and robustness. Conventional deep learning models struggle in handling noisy and heterogeneous data from uncurated sources like the web, as they are designed to thrive in highly organized and clean datasets. This results in a substantial knowledge gap between the theoretical advancements in deep learning and real-world applications, where web images are omnipresent. To bridge this gap, recent research has focused on designing novel architectures and algorithms capable of extracting effective and robust features from noisy and challenging web images. This paper proposes a novel deep representation learning framework, termed Web-CLR (Web Content-aware Learning Regularizations), to address the challenges of noisy web images. The framework employs a hybrid combination of content-aware regularization terms and adversarial training, which enables the deep network to learn robust and transferable features from uncurated web images. Through comprehensive experiments on various benchmark datasets, our proposed Web-CLR framework demonstrates significant improvements in representation learning and network robustness when compared to state-of-the-art methods, ultimately addressing the knowledge gap between theoretical advancements and real-world applications in deep representation learning from noisy web images.

title: Noise-Compensated, Bias-Corrected Diffusion Weighted Endorectal Magnetic Resonance Imaging via a Stochastically Fully-Connected Joint Conditional Random Field Model
Abstract: Diffusion weighted endorectal magnetic resonance imaging (DWMRI) has emerged as a crucial modality in the diagnosis and management of prostate cancer, offering unparalleled insights into the tissue microstructure and vascular structure. However, the inherent presence of noise and structural biases inherent in MRI acquisitions often hampers the accuracy of diffusion tensor imaging parameters, thus underscoring the need for effective denoising and bias correction techniques. To this end, this study introduces a novel and stochastic fusion model, leveraging the stochastic Fully-Connected (FC) Conditional Random Field (CRF) framework to concurrently estimate noise-compensated and bias-corrected DW-MRI. By assimilating the individual images from adjacent slices, our joint CRF approach seamlessly integrates the complementary information, thereby preserving anatomical details while refining the DW-MRI parameters. An extensive experimental evaluation on multiple public datasets and a range of clinically relevant scenarios demonstrates the efficacy of our framework in overcoming diverse noise patterns and bias artifacts. Our method achieves notable improvements in terms of image quality, reduced directional noise, and augmented accuracy of diffusion tensor imaging parameters, thus establishing its potential as a proficient pre-processing tool for DWI. Additionally, our CRF-based framework demonstrates a considerable time advantage over existing methods, owing to its optimized computational complexity, facilitating seamless integration into daily clinical workflows. Consequently, this proposed framework holds great promise towards enhancing the diagnostic reliability and efficiency of DW-MRI.

title: Semantic-enriched Visual Vocabulary Construction in a Weakly Supervised Context
Abstract: This research focuses on the construction of a visual vocabulary that concurrently explores the integration of semantic information with visual features for effective object classification in a weakly supervised context. The emergence of deep learning models has resulted in the development of robust feature representations that incorporate various aspects of an image simultaneously. However, these models often demand substantial amounts of annotated data, thereby hindering their application in real-world scenarios. To bridge this gap, the proposed visual vocabulary construction methodology incorporates both visual and semantic cues to devise a more comprehensive and robust feature representation. Prior to initiating the feature extraction process, object categories are first represented via distributed semantic embeddings. These embeddings are then harmoniously merged with the extracted visual features. Consequently, this enriched feature representation is capable of effectively refining the classification outcomes of object categories despite minimal annotated training data. Furthermore, to demonstrate the efficacy of the proposed method, comprehensive experiments are conducted on a variety of popular image classification benchmarks, including ImageNet and Visual Genome datasets, which exhibit a marked improvement in model performance. The results demonstrate the potential of enhancing model performance through the incorporation of semantic knowledge, while minimizing the dependency on explicitly annotated training data.

title: On non-iterative training of a neural classifier
Abstract: This abstract discusses recent advancements in non-iterative training of neural classifiers, providing a comprehensive overview of the methodologies employed and their respective merits. Non-iterative training, a departure from traditional iterative methods used to update model parameters, has emerged as a promising approach to minimize computational costs associated with large-scale models. A vital aspect of non-iterative training methodology is its division into two primary categories: one-shot learning and few-shot learning. One-shot learning methods focus on adapting to new knowledge with a single illustrative example, whereas few-shot learning techniques enable the model to learn from only a few relevant instances. Techniques such as meta-learning and knowledge distillation are typically used in conjunction with few-shot learning to encourage faster learning processes and to capture transferable knowledge from a related task. Another essential element of non-iterative training is its seamless integration with pre-trained models, facilitating efficient transfer of learnt characteristics and lowering the risk of overfitting. Nonetheless, computational and storage constraints associated with deployment of large-scale non-iterative models can be insurmountable. Existing research indicates a potential convergence towards reinforcement learning techniques to tackle optimisation related issues efficiently, although these methods demand a judicious selection of hyperparameters for successful realisation. The proposed training approach empowers neural classifiers with enhanced transferability and flexibility without substantial increases in computational intensity, thus empowering their real-world deployment for resolving complex prediction tasks efficiently.

title: Sparse Representation of a Blur Kernel for Blind Image Restoration
Abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to blind image restoration, focusing on the sparse representation of a blur kernel. Traditional methods for restoring blurred images rely heavily on the accurate estimation of the point spread function (PSF) or blur kernel, often finding this to be a challenging task, especially when face to face with distorted or strongly blurred images. To overcome this limitation and effectively restore images under various blurring conditions, we propose a blind image restoration framework that leverages the sparse representation of a blur kernel. Our framework employs a dictionary-based approach combined with total variation minimization to sparsely represent the blurred kernels, enabling a more precise estimation of the underlying system. Furthermore, a novel kernel prior is formulated by leveraging the insights from sparse representation and dictionary learning, aiming to capture the essence of natural blurring processes. Experimental results show that our framework outperforms the state-of-the-art blind image restoration methods in both PSNR and visual quality metrics by reconstructing the blur kernel and restoring the original image effectively. Consequently, our work offers a significant advancement in blind image restoration, paving the way for successful applications in image processing and computer vision fields.
