title: Instance-aware Semantic Segmentation via Multi-task Network Cascades
Abstract: This paper proposes a novel instance-aware semantic segmentation framework that leverages multi-task network cascades to effectively address the issue of distinguishing between different instances of the same class within an image. The proposed architecture consists of a sequence of three neural networks, each of which is trained on a different task: the first network identifies instances by learning to segment out individual objects; the second network refines the instance segmentation by predicting the boundaries of each object; and the third network performs semantic segmentation using the instance-aware features obtained from the previous two networks. The multi-task cascading approach allows the model to gradually refine its understanding of the instance-aware features, leading to more accurate and robust instance segmentation. Furthermore, the proposed framework employs a novel object proposal mechanism to generate high-quality instance proposals, which are then fed into the cascading network to facilitate more accurate instance-aware semantic segmentation. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed framework outperforms state-of-the-art instance-aware semantic segmentation models, achieving state-of-the-art performance on various benchmark datasets, including Pascal Context, Cityscapes, and COCO-Stuff. The framework's ability to adapt to diverse datasets and scenarios highlights its potential for practical applications in image understanding and computer vision.

title: We Are Humor Beings: Understanding and Predicting Visual Humor
Abstract: Humor has long been a cornerstone of human communication, providing a unique means of social bonding, stress relief, and entertainment. Despite its importance, understanding and predicting visual humor remains a challenging task, with numerous variables influencing individual perceptions and preferences. This research delves into the complex realm of visual humor, aiming to uncover the underlying mechanisms driving human appreciation of humor in visual stimuli. Through a multi-disciplinary approach combining cognitive psychology, neuroscience, and computer vision, we seek to elucidate the key factors contributing to visual humor, including incongruity, exaggeration, and Surprise. Our study focuses on both the human perception and computational processing aspects of visual humor, employing various methodologies such as surveys, eye-tracking, and machine learning algorithms. We also investigate the impact of cultural background, personal experiences, and emotions on humor perception, striving to develop a more nuanced understanding of the intricate relationships between visual elements and humor. By shedding light on the cognitive and computational processes involved in visual humor, our research aims to provide novel insights for the development of more effective humor recognition and generation systems, as well as to contribute to a deeper understanding of the multifaceted nature of humor in human communication.

title: Passive Communication with Ambient Light
Abstract: Active research has been carried out to explore possibilities in transforming ambient light into a communication medium to develop passive interfaces for users. Given the proliferation of ambient displays in various places like smart homes, and office space, tapping into users' pre-existing knowledge of and connection to the subtle dynamics of lighting has made it imperative to introduce an intelligent communication system composed of ambient lighting systems. As distinct attributes and properties of light, such as intensity, polarity, and spectral properties can be programmed and rearranged to convey messages. Furthermore, various light ambiance states ranging from monochrome to polychromic representability in indoor environments are readily visible to the user, provide a fundamental method of communication using otherwise omnipresent, yet hidden possibilities in electrical lighting. Developing an intuitive means of interaction by incorporating passive interfaces such as those based on light into a scenario, without making users realize this newly formed, ambient interface would let users subtly engage and become knowledgeable with intelligent communication through any standard intelligent lighting system. The studies' findings emphasize an experimental approach demonstrating that certain variables like room exposure and luminary visual content are determinants of and effect performance variability of lighting-aided passive human-computer interaction.

title: Origami: A 803 GOp/s/W Convolutional Network Accelerator
Abstract: This paper presents Origami, a novel, ultra-low power and area-efficient Convolutional Network (CNN) accelerator. Designed with the increasing demands of edge AI applications in mind, Origami achieves an impressive performance of 803 GOP/s/W, making it a strong candidate for real-world deployments. By leveraging a unique combination of folding-based spatial decomposition, approximate computing, and hybrid pipelining, Origami reduces the number of expensive digital multipliers required for CNN computation, leading to a substantial decrease in power consumption and area footprint. The proposed architecture is also highly scalable, capable of executing a wide range of CNN topologies with varying sizes and complexities. Experimental results demonstrate Origami's effectiveness and efficiency, demonstrating an average performance gain of 3.5x over a state-of-the-art CNN accelerator, while reducing power consumption by over 85% and area utilization by up to 70%. Through a comprehensive analysis of Origami's energy efficiency, area usage, and computational performance, this work provides valuable insights into the design of ultra-low power CNN accelerators and sheds light on the promising prospects of Origami as a building block for future edge AI computing systems. Additionally, the proposed architecture is highly adaptable and can be easily integrated with various edge devices, making it an attractive solution for real-world AI applications, including but not limited to, computer vision, robotics, and traffic monitoring systems.

title: On the Relation between two Rotation Metrics
Abstract: This abstract delves into the hitherto underexplored realm of evaluating rotational phenomena through juxtaposing two disparate approaches: the net-to-gross rotation (NGR) ratio commonly employed in petroleum exploration and the newly introduced rotational spectral graph (RSG) theory, reminiscent of machine learning constructs. The NGR ratio, typically reckoned from log-derived gamma-ray and density curves, offers an estimate of the rotating component of a system relative to the non-rotating components. In contrast, the RSG method extracts pertinent rotational characteristics in the wavenumber spectrum of seismic data by treating seismic arrays as graph-structured objects that can be processed parallel to spectral signal components. Leveraging the distinction between the NGR ratio and RSG, this study compares, contrasts, and analyzes the former's applicability and robustness in varying seismic environments where either or both metrics' validity may be diminished by geometrical, structural, or directional diversity. Quantitative comparisons are achieved through integration with real and synthetically-generated datasets, thus providing evidence in support of the mutual interaction between NGR and RSG in enabling enhanced quality and precision of predictive models, validating the concept of comprehensive rotational analysis that reconciles traditional and modern methods.

title: Watch-Bot: Unsupervised Learning for Reminding Humans of Forgotten Actions
Abstract: Unsupervised Learning for Reminding Humans of Forgotten Actions is a novel approach aimed at alleviating the burden of remembering and completing various tasks. This initiative draws inspiration from existing personal assistants and artificial intelligence-driven home automation systems, emphasizing a personalized experience for users. By leveraging unsupervised learning, the created system is capable of automatically identifying frequently needed actions and developing strategies to remind users of these forgotten tasks without necessitating extensive manual configuration. Incorporating machine learning with a conversational interface to engage users in a structured manner is key. Furthermore, the system utilizes ambient intelligence, integrating user behavior, spatial reasoning, and situational awareness to proactively perform actions typically handled by humans. This hybrid of AI-driven and user-centric design encourages Watch-Bot's functionality to progressively reinforce user experience and promote healthy interaction between humans and technology. Effectively assisting individuals in maintaining a consistent task routine is among the primary objectives. The absence of an explicit instruction-based user interface provides an intuitive experience, thus enabling seamless and transparent adoption by users.

title: Compressed Dynamic Mode Decomposition for Background Modeling
Abstract: This paper presents a novel application of Compressed Dynamic Mode Decomposition (cDMD) to the problem of background modeling, a crucial step in various computer vision tasks. The existing background subtraction methods suffer from issues such as slow processing speed, high computation complexity, and sensitivity to lighting variations and scene changes. To address these limitations, we propose a cDMD-based background modeling framework that combines the sparsity regularized DMD analysis with a compressed sensing-based compression algorithm. Our approach involves first extracting a set of dynamic modes from the observed video frames using cDMD, and then using these modes to rebuild the background model that can accurately recover from scene changes and varying lighting conditions. The proposed method is capable of capturing both periodic and transient dynamics of the detected background objects, making it particularly suitable for modeling complex and dynamic backgrounds prevalent in real-world applications. Experimental results demonstrate the efficacy of our cDMD-based framework in accurately modeling diverse backgrounds and foreground objects, producing state-of-the-art results in terms of accuracy and processing efficiency compared to existing methods. Additionally, we provide a theoretical analysis of the cDMD-based background modeling framework, establishing its computational complexity and providing insights into the choice of relevant system parameters.

title: Understanding Human-Centric Images: From Geometry to Fashion
Abstract: This abstract introduces Human-Centric Images, a new paradigm that blurs the boundaries between geometry, visualization, and fashion. By analyzing fashion as a manifestation of human behavior, fashion designers and manufacturers now rely heavily on creating objects that not only outline the aesthetic desires of consumers but also respond to changes in real-time, thereby marking the advent of human-centric images in the realm of human-aware products. The increasing proliferation of high-resolution cameras coupled with the widespread use of augmented reality (AR) and virtual reality (VR) technologies have played a pivotal role in spawning human-centric images, defined as images that incorporate the human element while retaining a style of geometric simplicity. Human-centric images have not only significantly simplified the process of visualizing items before buying but have also dramatically shortened the duration required to be able to combine design, prototyping and production, thereby streamlining the entire process of clothing production. By combining principles from human psychology, computer vision, and fashion design, researchers have been successful in creating human-centric interfaces, ultimately making clothing manufacturing a high-tech yet increasingly human-aware field. The impact of this technology is estimated to be monumental, enabling new value chains in sustainable growth, with immense benefits in the reduction of costs and saving production timelines.

title: Learning Deep Features for Discriminative Localization
Abstract: Deep learning architectures have made significant strides in image classification tasks, achieving high accuracy rates and state-of-the-art performance on various benchmarks. However, their interpretation and understanding remain limited, hindering their adoption in real-world applications. Visualizing and understanding how neural networks localize discriminative features is crucial for applications in computer vision, surveillance, and medical diagnosis. To address these challenges, this study focuses on developing deep neural networks that can learn discriminative features and localize them accurately within an image. We propose a novel framework that combines the strengths of convolutional neural networks (CNNs) and visualization techniques. Our method leverages gradient-based visualization to highlight regions in an image that contribute most to the classification decision. The proposed framework significantly improves the effectiveness of localization by efficiently utilizing attention mechanisms and multi-scale features. The primary strength of our approach lies in its ability to adapt to different datasets and learn robust features. Our experimental evaluation showcases the superior performance of our model compared to existing methods, with notable improvements in both precision and recall. By providing strong interpretability and discriminative feature localization capabilities, our framework opens up possibilities for improved image analysis and understanding in a wide range of applications.

title: Inside-Outside Net: Detecting Objects in Context with Skip Pooling and Recurrent Neural Networks
Abstract: The Inside-Outside Net is a novel, context-aware computer vision framework designed to detect objects within their natural environments. Building upon traditional convolutional neural networks (CNNs), this model combines the strengths of skip pooling and recurrent neural networks (RNNs) to better capture the nuances of semantic relationships and spatial hierarchies within images. The skip pooling architecture enables hierarchical feature extraction and aggregation, while the incorporation of RNNs facilitates the sequential and contextual processing of object instances. This approach enables the framework to learn context-dependent object representations, taking into account the relationships between objects and their surroundings. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of the Inside-Outside Net in detecting objects within cluttered and complex scenes, achieving state-of-the-art performance on benchmark datasets such as the PASCAL VOC and COCO. Furthermore, the model's ability to capture contextual dependencies and hierarchies facilitates its generalizability to various object recognition tasks, including but not limited to object detection, image classification, and scene understanding. Overall, the Inside-Outside Net presents a versatile and powerful vision engine for real-world object recognition applications, capable of operating in a wide range of scenarios and conditions. Its scalability, reliability, and interpretability make it a promising area of research in computer vision and artificial intelligence.

title: Evaluation of Pose Tracking Accuracy in the First and Second Generations of Microsoft Kinect
Abstract: This study evaluates the pose tracking accuracy of two generations of Microsoft Kinect, with a focus on its potential applications in various fields such as gaming, healthcare, and education. The first generation of Kinect, released in 2010, utilized infrared and color cameras to track user movements, providing limited motion sensing capabilities. In contrast, the second generation of Kinect, introduced in 2013, incorporates an upgraded infrared camera sensor, improved depth mapping, and a more efficient processing unit, allowing for more precise and robust motion sensing. This research aims to investigate the difference in pose tracking accuracy between the two Kinect generations, employing established methodologies for evaluating pose tracking performance, including the calculation of mean absolute error and angular difference error. A mixed-methods approach is undertaken, combining both quantitative and qualitative analysis of pose tracking data collected using each Kinect iteration. The experimental results demonstrate a marked improvement in pose tracking performance with the second-generation Kinect, yielding lower error values and higher accuracy rates in comparison to its predecessor. These findings offer implications for digital human-computer interfaces, human-machine interaction, and gesture recognition. Overall, this work provides critical insights into the comparative performance of the first and second generations of Microsoft Kinect, shedding light on the evolution of pose tracking technologies and their potential applications across various domains.

title: A Person Re-Identification System For Mobile Devices
Abstract: A person re-identification (Re-ID) system for mobile devices involves the development of a robust and scalable framework to identify and track individuals across non-overlapping camera views, utilizing mobile device constraints. This study proposes a real-time and energy-efficient Re-ID system, designed to operate on resource-constrained mobile devices, by leveraging the strengths of deep learning and computer vision techniques. A novel architecture is developed, integrating a small-footprint feature extractor with a lightweight similarity measure, to reduce the computational overhead and memory requirements. The system is trained on a modified version of the commonly used CUHK03 and Market1501 datasets, tailored to resemble the characteristics of mobile device captured images. A series of experiments are conducted to evaluate the system's accuracy, efficiency, and robustness, considering various factors such as view angle, occlusion, and sample variability. The results show that the proposed system achieves competitive performance while significantly reducing the computational cost and memory footprint, making it suitable for real-time deployment on mobile devices. title: Articulated Pose Estimation Using Hierarchical Exemplar-Based Models
Abstract: This research introduces a novel hierarchical exemplar-based approach for articulated pose estimation in images and videos, showcasing significant improvements over traditional methods. By leveraging a hierarchical structure, our proposed model can handle varying degrees of body articulation and variability in human body pose. The model is composed of multiple stages, each catering to specific aspects of pose estimation, such as detection, segmentation, and prediction. In each stage, we employ a hierarchical exemplar-based representation to capture the spatial relationships between body parts and predict the joint angles and 3D pose of individuals. Our approach effectively integrates bottom-up and top-down cues to produce more accurate and robust results, particularly in challenging scenarios with occlusions, self-occlusions, and varying body pose. By enabling effective representation learning, alignment, and pose inference, our hierarchical exemplar-based model displays state-of-the-art performance in articulated pose estimation on popular benchmarks. Our results demonstrate improved robustness to variation in clothing, background clutter, and varying levels of body articulation, underscoring the efficacy of our approach as a viable solution for real-world pose estimation applications, such as action recognition, human-computer interaction, and video surveillance. Moreover, our method is computationally efficient and could be easily integrated into existing computer vision pipelines, making it a valuable asset for a wide range of applications.

title: Unsupervised Temporal Segmentation of Repetitive Human Actions Based on Kinematic Modeling and Frequency Analysis
Abstract: This study presents a novel approach to unsupervised temporal segmentation of repetitive human actions. We propose a framework that combines kinematic modeling and frequency analysis to identify and isolate individual actions within a sequence of repetitive movements. Our method relies on capturing the kinematic characteristics of a human action by modeling the temporal pattern of joint displacements as a circular motion equation. This representation allows us to extract the intrinsic frequency content of each action using the short-time Fourier transform, enabling us to distinguish between similar actions based on their unique temporal signatures. Furthermore, we utilize techniques from spectral clustering to group and isolate individual actions within a sequence. The proposed framework is evaluated on various action datasets, demonstrating its ability to adapt to different action classes and environments, and achieving state-of-the-art performance in terms of accuracy, precision, and recall. The results show that our approach can not only segment repetitive actions across different scenarios but also learn to recognize the context-dependent changes in actions, thus providing a comprehensive solution for temporal segmentation of human movements. Our method has significant implications for various fields, including human-computer interaction, surveillance, and physical rehabilitation, where the ability to automatically detect and segment human actions can greatly facilitate data analysis, decision-making, and personalized interventions.

title: Deep Relative Attributes
Abstract: This paper presents an investigation into the concept of deep relative attributes, a novel approach to image classification that focuses on capturing the relative similarities and differences between multiple instances of a same class. By learning to represent images as hierarchical, structured features, deep models can effectively discern the nuances in attribute manifestations across varying visual contexts. Our proposed method involves augmenting a pre-trained convolutional neural network (CNN) with a relative attribute module, which is trained to predict the attribute differences between pairs of images from the same class. This allows the network to learn a nuanced understanding of the attribute configurations that are unique to each visual category. Through experiments on several benchmark datasets, we demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach in improving the classification accuracy and generating more meaningful and interpretable feature representations. Furthermore, we show that our method can be applied to a wide range of real-world applications, including product variation identification, human-centric attribute prediction, and content-based image retrieval. The results highlight the potential of deep relative attributes in enabling more nuanced and context-aware image classification capabilities, and we hope that our work will inspire further research in this direction.

title: Deep Learning-Based Image Kernel for Inductive Transfer
Abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to inductive transfer learning for image classification using deep learning-based image kernels. Traditional kernel methods have proven effective for image classification but often fail to generalize well to new datasets due to limited representation capacity and difficulty in designing effective kernels for complex image data. To address these issues, this work integrates deep learning with kernel methods, allowing the deep neural network to learn a feature representation that can be effectively encoded into a high-dimensional Euclidean space via a trainable deep kernel function. The proposed approach can learn feature representations tailored to specific image classification tasks while remaining invariant to task-irrelevant information. This paper demonstrates the effectiveness of the approach by training deep kernels on several benchmark image classification datasets, including CIFAR-100, STL-10, and ImageNet. Extensive experiments show that the proposed method improves state-of-the-art results for many tasks by leveraging the strengths of both deep learning and kernel methods, outperforming traditional deep learning approaches on diverse image datasets with varying levels of complexity and domain shifts. The proposed method opens new avenues for inductive transfer learning in image classification by enabling accurate and robust adaptation to new image datasets with minimal additional training data.

title: Learning the Correction for Multi-Path Deviations in Time-of-Flight Cameras
Abstract: The precise measurement of depth using Time-of-Flight (ToF) cameras is fundamental in various applications such as 3D modeling, robotics, and autonomous vehicles. However, ToF cameras often suffer from multi-path deviations, which can significantly compromise the accuracy of depth measurements. This phenomenon arises due to the reflections of photons entering the ToF camera system, where these reflections can originate from either the direct path or indirect paths such as multiple-peak returns. The effects of multi-path deviations can be exacerbated further by factors like scattering, non-uniform illumination, and atmospheric interference. Consequently, the errors introduced by multi-path effects can lead to inaccuracies in depth measurements and may even cause unstable camera performance and false positives. To mitigate this issue, this research aims to develop a deep learning-based correction technique specifically tailored for ToF cameras to leverage photometric and geometric cues associated with the multi-path phenomenon. The experimental evaluation and validation of the proposed correction method on various benchmark datasets show significant improvements in depth accuracy and demonstrate robustness against diverse environmental conditions. The proposed correction method has the potential to unlock the full precision of ToF cameras, enabling them to be utilized in a wide range of applications.

title: Cross-dimensional Weighting for Aggregated Deep Convolutional Features
Abstract: This paper presents an innovative approach, termed Cross-dimensional Weighting for Aggregated Deep Convolutional Features (CW-AF), to enhance the performance of deep convolutional neural networks (CNNs) in image representation and classification tasks. By analyzing the feature aggregation process in existing CNN architectures, the CW-AF method discovers that feature maps from different convolutional layers often convey redundant or complementary information, resulting in suboptimal utilization of aggregated features. To address this limitation, CW-AF introduces a novel cross-dimensional weighting strategy that adaptively adjusts the contribution of each feature map from different layers, enabling the model to selectively emphasize the most informative features while suppressing the redundant ones. The CW-AF method consists of two primary components: a feature significance estimator, which evaluates the importance of each feature map based on its relevance to the target task, and a weight updater, which recalibrates the feature maps based on the significance estimates. Through extensive experimental evaluations on various benchmark datasets, including ImageNet, CIFAR-10, and PASCAL VOC, CW-AF demonstrates significant improvements in accuracy and robustness over state-of-the-art feature aggregation techniques, underscoring its potential as a valuable tool for various computer vision applications. The CW-AF method can be readily integrated into existing CNN architectures to improve their generalization capabilities and adaptability, paving the way for more efficient and accurate deep learning applications.

title: Deep Tracking: Visual Tracking Using Deep Convolutional Networks
Abstract: Deep tracking is a fundamental problem in computer vision that deals with the continuous estimation of the location, scale, and orientation of an object in a series of consecutive frames from a video. In recent years, deep convolutional networks (DCNs) have emerged as a powerful tool for addressing this problem, offering significant improvements over traditional tracking methods. DCNs leverage the shared hierarchical representation capabilities to locate and track objects in challenging scenarios, such as partial occlusions, varying illumination, and non-rigid transformations. However, designing effective DCNs for tracking remains an open challenge due to the need for robust feature extraction, accurate temporally coherent predictions, and efficient processing in real-time applications. This paper proposes a deep tracking framework that exploits the strengths of DCNs by incorporating a novel and efficient learning approach, termed as multi-stage incremental learning, to guide the tracking process. By sequentially updating the model with adaptive learning rates, our framework mitigates the catastrophic forgetting phenomenon and enhances the stability of the tracking results over time. Furthermore, we adopt an off-policy reinforcement learning formulation to learn an active control policy for selecting the most informative frames to update the model, leading to improved tracking perfor-mance and inference efficiency. The experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness and robustness of the proposed framework in comparison to state-of-the-art visual tracking methods, showcasing its potential for various applications, such as robotics, autonomous vehicles, and surveillance systems.

title: Action Recognition with Image Based CNN Features
Abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to action recognition using image-based Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) features. The proposed system leverages the strength of CNNs in image feature extraction and applies this to human action recognition tasks. A comprehensive review of existing action recognition systems highlights the limitations of traditional approaches that often rely on 3D video features, depth sensors, or explicit temporal modeling. In contrast, this work focuses on the effectiveness of 2D image features in capturing the essence of human actions. Our approach involves training a deep CNN on a large-scale image dataset, wherein the final convolutional layer is used to extract spatial and temporal features from image sequences. These features are then classified using a support vector machine (SVM) or a long short-term memory (LSTM) network to recognize human actions. Experimental results on several benchmark datasets demonstrate the superiority of our approach in terms of recognition accuracy and computational efficiency, showcasing the significance of image-based features in action recognition tasks. Moreover, a thorough analysis of the proposed framework reveals the advantages of this approach in terms of flexibility and scalability, making it an attractive solution for real-world applications, such as surveillance systems and human-computer interaction technologies. Ultimately, the proposed system aims to fill the gap between traditional video-based action recognition systems and image-based approaches, paving the way for the development of more efficient and robust action recognition systems in the future.

title: RNN Fisher Vectors for Action Recognition and Image Annotation
Abstract: This paper proposes an novel approach to action recognition and image annotation by employing Recurrent Neural Network (RNN) Fisher Vectors. Conventional methods primarily rely on hand-crafted features and local descriptors to capture temporal and spatial information, which often fail to fully capture the complex dynamics of human behavior. In contrast, RNN Fisher Vectors learn hierarchical and discriminative representations using stacked long short-term memory (LSTM) networks, enabling robust and temporally-invariant feature learning. The proposed RNN Fishers are designed to exploit temporal hierarchies through global pooling and dimensionality reduction techniques, allowing for a compact and informative representation of video sequences. By incorporating these descriptors into a standard bag-of-features model, our method significantly outperforms state-of-the-art action recognition benchmarks on challenging datasets like UCF-101 and HMDB-51, with an average improvement of 7.5% in classification accuracy. Furthermore, the novel features learned by RNN Fishers allow for highly accurate image annotation and annotation transfer across datasets, demonstrating their potential as a universal feature representation for visual recognition tasks. Overall, our approach integrates state-of-the-art deep learning and information retrieval techniques to deliver a unified solution for complex visual recognition problems.

title: Improving Human Activity Recognition Through Ranking and Re-ranking
Abstract: Human activity recognition has garnered significant importance in the realm of computer vision and machine learning, particularly in healthcare, security, and transportation systems. However, existing methods often struggle with categorizing complex and nuanced activities, resulting in inaccurate detection and recognition. To address this challenge, we propose a novel ranking and re-ranking framework to enhance human activity recognition. By initially utilizing a robust 3D Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) to detect key activity-related features, we then adopt a ranking-based approach to establish a preliminary activity ranking, prioritizing those with the highest detection confidence. This initial ranking is iteratively refined through a re-ranking mechanism, where each activity is re-estimated by aggregating both local context and global information. To further enhance the framework's robustness, we incorporate transfer learning and spatial-temporal attention modules to adapt and focus on relevant areas of interest within the video sequence. Comprehensive experiments conducted on freely available benchmark datasets demonstrate substantial improvements in activity recognition performance, with our ranking and re-ranking framework achieving significant boosts in precision, recall, and F1-score. Notably, we identify meaningful scenarios where domain adaptation enhances classification results and contributes an additional 5-10% of recognition accuracy, compelling its inclusion in our framework's configuration arsenal.

title: A New Approach of Gray Images Binarization with Threshold Methods
Abstract: Binarization of gray-scale images plays a crucial role in various image processing and analysis applications such as object detection, segmentation, and feature extraction. However, traditional threshold-based binarization methods often fail to achieve optimal results due to complexity and variability of image content, leading to noisy or inaccurate binary output. This paper proposes a new approach for binarization of gray images using a novel thresholding method, which combines the benefits of deterministic and adaptive thresholding techniques. The proposed approach, named hybrid binary binarization, utilizes both local and global information of the image content to determine the optimal threshold values. An adaptive neighborhood characterization technique is employed to capture local intensity changes and patterns, while a global threshold calculation method is applied to ensure consistent and robust binarization results across different image areas. By integrating these complementary techniques, the proposed hybrid approach is capable of achieving superior binarization performance and adaptability to various image types and complexity levels, thus resolving the limitations of existing thresholding methods. Comprehensive experiments and comparative studies with state-of-the-art binarization algorithms demonstrate the efficacy and robustness of the proposed hybrid binary binarization method, highlighting its potential as a reliable and versatile solution for real-world image processing applications.

title: Deep Feature Learning with Relative Distance Comparison for Person Re-identification
Abstract: This paper explores the concept of person re-identification (Re-ID) using deep feature learning and relative distance comparison. Person Re-ID is a challenging problem in computer vision that involves recognizing individuals across different cameras with varying poses, viewpoints, illuminations, and environmental factors, a primary challenge being the disparity in distance between the cameras. Our method tackles these challenges by employing a novel architecture that combines relative distance comparison and a self-attention based feature extractor to generate spatial-temporal features. We utilize relative distance comparison to model the discrepancy in inter-camera distances, enabling the model to effectively learn relevant inter-camera distance-aware features from the same camera. Furthermore, we propose a new distance-aware feature fusion module that aggregates multi-scale features from the global feature extractor and distance-aware local feature extractor, providing a compact representation that encodes inter-camera distance-aware information. We evaluate our method on five benchmark datasets, showing consistent improvements in accuracy compared to state-of-the-art methods. Our approach combines a relative distance comparison module with a spatial-temporal feature extractor, resulting in a person re-identification system with a favorable balance between accuracy and efficiency. Experimental results demonstrate our approach's ability to provide robust features, achieving superior performance on challenging scenarios involving camera height. Overall, our work provides a strong baseline for future research in person Re-ID, particularly when tackling varied camera perspectives and non-uniform distances.

title: Robust Dictionary based Data Representation
Abstract:
This abstract presents an in-depth investigation into the development of robust dictionary-based methods for data representation. The primary focus lies in addressing the challenges associated with existing dictionary learning approaches, which often suffer from high computational complexity and limited adaptability to changing environments. To overcome these limitations, a novel dictionary learning framework is proposed that integrates concepts from compressive sensing and sparse representations. The framework involves an iterative process of dictionary update and sparse code estimation, where the dictionary is refined based on the sparse representation of the input data.

The proposed framework is evaluated on various image and signal processing tasks, including image denoising, compressed sensing, and anomaly detection. Results demonstrate significant improvements in accuracy and robustness compared to state-of-the-art dictionary learning methods. Additionally, the computational efficiency of the proposed framework is demonstrated through its ability to handle large-scale datasets and high-dimensional data. The framework's ability to adapt to changing environments is also showcased through experiments involving noisy and corrupted data. 

A key feature of the proposed framework is its ability to learn dictionaries that are robust to outliers and variations in the data distribution. This is achieved through the incorporation of regularization terms that promote sparse and stable representations. The effectiveness of the proposed framework is further validated through comparisons with established dictionary learning methods, including K-SVD and dictionaries learned through compressive sensing. Overall, the proposed framework represents a significant advancement in the field of dictionary-based data representation, with broad applications in machine learning, signal processing, and image analysis.

title: Randomized Low-Rank Dynamic Mode Decomposition for Motion Detection
Abstract: This paper introduces a novel randomized low-rank dynamic mode decomposition (RLRDMD) approach for motion detection, which leverages the low-rank property of the dynamic mode decomposition (DMD) analysis. In the context of time-series data, accurate and efficient motion detection is crucial, particularly in applications such as surveillance, traffic monitoring, and medical image processing. The existing state-of-the-art DMD methods often suffer from high computational complexity and noise sensitivity, which hinders their practical implementation. To address these challenges, this work adapts the randomized SVD (Singular Value Decomposition) technique to efficiently compute the low-rank DMD matrix, thereby replacing the traditional deterministic approach with a probabilistic and computationally attractive alternative. The key innovation lies in the integration of randomized linear algebra with the DMD framework, yielding a robust and scalable solution for motion detection. The proposed RLRDMD method is evaluated using representative datasets in both synthetic and real-world scenarios, demonstrating superior performance in terms of detection accuracy, robustness to noise, and computational efficiency. The experimental results also highlight the advantages of the proposed approach over existing DMD-based methods, underscoring its potential to become a state-of-the-art solution for motion detection applications.

title: Highly Dynamic Spectrum Management within Licensed Shared Access Regulatory Framework
Abstract:
Highly Dynamic Spectrum Management within Licensed Shared Access Regulatory Framework implements innovative methods for efficient utilization of the precious electromagnetic spectrum, thereby reducing administrative overhead and allowing for rapid deployment of wireless networks. This regulation addresses spectrum regulators' growing need for innovative regulatory structures that allow and support a vast array of technological advances and spectrum utilizations. Licensed Shared Access (LSA), initially conceived by Ofcom in the UK, is particularly relevant for the utilization of licensed spectrum and unused capacity. The utilization of advanced radio access technologies such as future mMTC, ultra-high density networks, and 5G URLLC applications poses great challenges in real-time characterization of unused spectrum capacities, interference mitigation and maximized QoE.

Leveraging advanced software-defined radio technologies and machine learning-based artificial intelligence, the LSA regulatory approach ensures sharing possibilities by allowing temporary and dynamic access to licensed spectrum bands for varied utilization periods, therefore optimizing resource configuration and efficiency in capacity distribution. A further complicating factor involves timely characterization of interference potential and its mitigation, factoring real-time variability and interference sensitivity. The paper analyzes the technical aspects and regulation model implications of deploying a highly dynamic management mechanism on the licensed shared access regulatory framework.

title: Neural Self Talk: Image Understanding via Continuous Questioning and Answering
Abstract: Neural Self-Talk is a novel neural network architecture that integrates a continuous questioning and answering mechanism to improve image understanding. By adopting a dialog-like interaction paradigm, this framework enables the model to iteratively refine its understanding of an image, fostering a more in-depth and nuanced comprehension of complex visual scenes. The proposed architecture comprises two primary components: a questioner network that poses successive questions to itself about the image, and an answerer network that generates answers in response, updating the model's internal representation of the image. This relentless cycle of questioning and answering enables the model to identify and incorporate additional contextual information, contextually relevant features, and relationships within the image, ultimately leading to enhanced performance on a range of visual perception tasks. Experimental results on several challenging benchmarks demonstrate the efficacy of Neural Self-Talk, yielding state-of-the-art performance in image classification, object detection, and image segmentation tasks. Furthermore, this research offers new insights into the effectiveness of self-querying processes in facilitating neural networks' ability to capture intricate visual structures and relationships, paving the way for the further development of more adaptive and context-aware visual understanding models.

title: Deep Residual Learning for Image Recognition
Abstract: Deep residual learning has revolutionized image recognition by largely addressing the vanishing gradient problem in deep neural networks. By forming residuals between the input and output of multiple layers, it allows gradients to backpropagate easier and faster, enabling networks to train hundreds of layers deep. This approach enables the learning of complex and abstract features in images that may not be directly related to their input or output. The deep residual learning concept was first introduced in the form of residual networks (ResNets), which have since led to significant improvements in object detection, image classification, and segmentation tasks. One of the key benefits of residual learning is that it allows pre-trained networks to serve as a starting point for fine-tuning on specific dataset and tasks, making it an efficient way to exploit learned representations without requiring full retraining. This property has made ResNets one of the most popular architectures in computer vision, being adopted in various applications ranging from facial recognition to cancer diagnosis. However, training residual networks can be computationally expensive, requiring significant computational resources and expertise, limiting access to their capabilities for many users and applications. Recent studies have explored the use of transfer learning and knowledge distillation to address these limitations, potentially paving the way for broader adoption of deep residual learning in image recognition tasks.

title: VRFP: On-the-fly Video Retrieval using Web Images and Fast Fisher Vector Products
Abstract: Our work proposes a novel video retrieval system, denoted as Virtual Reality-based Fast Fisher Vector Product (VRFP), which leverages web images and fast Fisher vector products to effectively retrieve videos from large-scale video databases. The increasing demand for video-based applications has led to the proliferation of extensive video collections, resulting in time-consuming search processes that hinder their usability. Traditional video retrieval methods rely heavily on text-based descriptions or manual annotation, which not only introduce a semantic gap but also slow down the search process. To address this challenge, we introduce the concept of web images as contextual information to guide on-the-fly video retrieval. By computing fast Fisher vector products between video features and web images, our system efficiently associates videos with contextually relevant images. Furthermore, we develop an efficient indexing scheme that significantly reduces the computational complexity of nearest neighbor search, resulting in instantaneous query processing. We demonstrate the effectiveness of VRFP through extensive experiments on several public video retrieval benchmarks. The results demonstrate that VRFP significantly outperforms the state-of-the-art methods in terms of accuracy and scalability. The proposed system enables on-the-fly video retrieval from massive video databases at unprecedented speed and performance, opening up promising avenues for real-world applications in various domains.

title: 3D Reconstruction of Crime Scenes and Design Considerations for an Interactive Investigation Tool
Abstract: The 3D reconstruction of crime scenes has become a crucial tool in modern forensic analysis, providing investigators with a unique perspective on the physical layout and dynamics of a crime scene. This methodology enables them to interactively explore and analyze complex spatial relationships, reconstruct events, and identify potential evidence that might have been overlooked or not captured during initial on-site examination. In this research, we aim to design and develop an interactive investigative tool that incorporates 3D reconstruction of crime scenes. Our investigation focuses on the development of a multi-tiered system that integrates computer vision, 3D modeling, and geospatial analysis to facilitate the automated generation of high-resolution 3D crime scene models. We also examine various design considerations for the interactive investigation tool, including user-centered interface design, data visualization strategies, and intelligent query support systems. The ultimate goal of this research is to provide investigators with a comprehensive framework for efficiently analyzing and reconstructing crime scenes, thereby enhancing their ability to solve complex crimes and mitigate forensic challenges associated with large and complex crime scenes.

title: Enhanced image feature coverage: Key-point selection using genetic algorithms
Abstract: This research focuses on optimizing key-point selection in image feature coverage, a crucial step in various computer vision applications such as object recognition, tracking, and scene understanding. The conventional method of selecting key-points based on strong image gradients can result in inefficient coverage and reduced accuracy, particularly in complex scenarios with varying illumination, texture, and scale. To address this, a novel approach using genetic algorithms is proposed, which leverages the principles of natural selection and evolution to determine the optimal key-point configuration. By encoding the feature space as a binary chromosome, the genetic algorithm can efficiently explore the vast solution space and identify the most informative key-points for image representation. The approach is particularly beneficial in scenarios with high-dimensional feature spaces, where traditional methods often struggle to maintain efficiency and accuracy. The proposed algorithm demonstrates improved key-point coverage, robustness to variations in image conditions, and enhanced object recognition performance compared to state-of-the-art methods. Experimental results on several benchmark datasets validate the effectiveness of the genetic algorithm-based approach, highlighting its potential to significantly advance the field of image feature coverage and object recognition.

title: Evaluation of Object Detection Proposals Under Condition Variations
Abstract: This study investigates the impact of condition variations on object detection performance, with a focus on the evaluation of object detection proposals. Object detection is a crucial component of various computer vision applications, including autonomous vehicles, surveillance systems, and robotics. While numerous object detection algorithms have been proposed in recent years, the evaluation of these proposals often relies on images captured under specific conditions, which may not reflect real-world scenarios. The condition variations considered in this study include different lighting conditions (daytime, nighttime, and varying intensities), camera properties (resolution, focal length, and field of view), and environmental conditions (weather, background clutter, and occlusion). We analyze the performance of state-of-the-art object detection algorithms under these condition variations, using a comprehensive dataset with annotations that cover a wide range of scenarios. Our results show that the performance of these algorithms degrades significantly under real-world condition variations, highlighting the need for more robust and condition-invariant object detection models. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the proposed architectures, which incorporate additional features and modifications to existing frameworks, can improve the robustness of object detection proposals under various conditions, paving the way for more reliable and accurate object detection in real-world applications.

title: Deep Learning Algorithms with Applications to Video Analytics for A Smart City: A Survey
Abstract: Videos play a crucial role in modern city infrastructure, serving as a valuable asset for law enforcement, urban planning, and smart city development. The rapid growth of video data brings significant opportunities for advanced analytics, which can be leveraged to create a safer and more efficient city environment. To explore the huge amounts of video data systematically, researchers and practitioners are increasingly turning towards deep learning algorithms, which are shown to far surpass traditional machine learning methods in terms of video analysis performance. This study provides a comprehensive survey of the current state-of-the-art in deep learning algorithms for video analytics, focusing on object detection, action recognition, and scene understanding, as well as topic modeling and crowd monitoring. We delve into existing video analysis architectures, discuss various deep learning techniques used, and compare different algorithmic approaches for different urban planning applications, such as automated traffic management, surveillance and monitoring, emergency services, disaster management, crime prevention, city planning and vehicle tracking. To aid in comprehending the proposed study we provide deep analysis and comparisons of different deep learning methods and provide a categorization of existing techniques. The goal of this study is to provide helpful insights and guidelines to researchers and practitioners for understanding and utilizing deep learning and video analytics for smart city applications.

title: Minimally Supervised Feature Selection for Classification (Master's Thesis, University Politehnica of Bucharest)
Abstract: The goal of this research is to develop a novel, minimally supervised feature selection methodology that can effectively identify the most relevant features for a given classification problem, even in the absence of large amounts of labeled data or domain-specific knowledge. This is achieved by integrating ideas from different fields, including feature selection, active learning, and exploratory data analysis. The proposed approach uses a combination of statistical tests and machine learning algorithms to evaluate the usefulness of individual features, as well as their synergistic interactions with each other. The supervised component of the methodology makes minimal requirements on the availability of labeled data, relying instead on active learning techniques to query the user for evaluations on a small number of strategically selected instances. Through a series of experiments on both synthetic and real-world datasets, we demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed methodology in accurately identifying the most informative features for classification, even when faced with high-dimensional data and limited supervision. Furthermore, we evaluate the proposed approach on several publicly available datasets and compare its performance with state-of-the-art feature selection methods, showing that it offers a competitive alternative for applications where labeled data is scarce. Overall, this research provides insights into the potential benefits of minimally supervised feature selection for various machine learning tasks and domains.

title: ShapeNet: An Information-Rich 3D Model Repository
Abstract: ShapeNet is a comprehensive database of 3D models, crafted to bridge the gap between artificial intelligence and computer vision researchers in the realm of 3D understanding. Established to provide researchers with an extensive library of 3D models, each annotated with semantic attributes, the repository consists of over 3,000 categories of 3D models including furniture, vehicles, and anatomy. Notably, over 2.4 million models are meticulously curated and cataloged, each boasting precise attribute annotations. The database's dataset includes both detailed and coarse-grained class labels enabling researchers to experiment freely with various exploration techniques that enhance their models to accommodate different requirements. Beyond conventional applications, ShapeNet paves the way for the potential of 3D scene understanding, enabling researchers to reach out to a myriad of subsequent research areas such as scene segmentation, object detection and reconstruction, and robotics. Furthermore, ShapeNet facilitates easy data exchange by offering downloadable categories of models; thereby fueling collaboration and streamlining the workflow among experts across diverse fields. Nonetheless, it is worth noting that ShapeNet faces challenges in scale, and processing large datasets can be a bottleneck. Ultimately, ShapeNet emerges as a cornerstone for a global shift towards in-depth 3D research, fostering a future of groundbreaking advancements that promise to transform various sectors of global industry.

title: Get More With Less: Near Real-Time Image Clustering on Mobile Phones
Abstract: This paper presents an innovative approach to near real-time image clustering on mobile phones, aimed at overcoming the limitations of traditional clustering methods that are computationally expensive and require extensive resources. By leveraging the inherent parallelism of mobile processors and exploiting the spatial locality of image features, our proposed method efficiently detects and clusters similar images in a fraction of the time required by state-of-the-art approaches. The algorithm is built around a novel feature extraction module that utilizes a sparse representation-based technique, followed by a spatial-hierarchical clustering module that efficiently groups similar images together. Empirical results demonstrate that our method achieves a clustering accuracy of up to 90% on a dataset of 10,000 images within a time constraint of 5 seconds, showcasing its potential for real-time deployment on mobile devices. Furthermore, our method is scalable to larger datasets and supports multi-threading, allowing it to efficiently process a wide range of images on mobile phones with varying processing capacities. The proposed approach addresses the trade-offs between computational efficiency, memory requirements, and accuracy, making it a powerful tool for multimedia applications and a significant step forward in the development of image clustering methods for mobile devices.

title: Video captioning with recurrent networks based on frame- and video-level features and visual content classification
Abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to video captioning using recurrent networks that incorporate frame- and video-level features, as well as visual content classification. In contrast to earlier video captioning architectures that focus solely on frame-level features, our proposed model leverages a hierarchical framework that captures both local and global patterns within a video. The frame-level feature extraction module utilizes convolutional neural networks (CNNs) to extract spatial and temporal features from each frame, which are then fed into a recurrent neural network (RNN) to generate a sequence of words that describe the content of the video. To further enhance the performance of the model, a video-level feature extraction module is incorporated to capture the higher-level semantic information present in the video. This module employs temporal convolutional networks (TCNs) to extract video-level features, which are then combined with the frame-level features to generate the final caption. Additionally, a visual content classification module is applied to the video to provide a global understanding of its content, such as the presence of actions, objects, and scenes. By integrating these multiple components, our model is able to generate more informative and accurate video captions, improving the overall performance of the video captioning task. Experimental results on several benchmark datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of our proposed approach, showcasing its ability to outperform existing state-of-the-art methods.

title: Yet Another Statistical Analysis of Bob Ross Paintings
Abstract: This study employs a quantitative methodology to statistically analyze the characteristics of Bob Ross paintings, examining the interplay between visual patterns, brushstroke energies, and artistic styles. Through a thorough content analysis of 500 Bob Ross paintings, involving the coding of over 300 variables, researchers uncovered intriguing correlations between painting style, brushstroke dynamics, and atmospheric perspective. One key finding revealed that 85% of Ross's landscapes exhibited dominant vertical brushstrokes in the foreground, reducing in amplitude as the horizon receded. Conversely, 55% of his series displayed low-angle vistas accompanied by dense, diagonally oriented brushstrokes, heightening atmospheric effects and emotional impact. Data modeling suggests that Ross's distinctive approach to painting embodied both deterministic and stochastic processes, creating an artistic structure that is at once intuitive and calculable. This research contributes to our understanding of Bob Ross's unique artistic voice, highlighting its interplay between expression and structure. Additionally, the exploration of statistical patterns within Bob Ross's art may serve as a catalyst for the development of new generative art methodologies, reconciling art and science through systematically deciphered relationships between paint strokes, color selection, and viewer perception. As such, this study endeavors to illuminate the intricate connections between Bob Ross's artistic modus operandi and the systematic principles governing his work.

title: MovieQA: Understanding Stories in Movies through Question-Answering
Abstract: This paper delves into the realm of movie understanding through the lens of question-answering task, further known as MovieQA. The increasing availability of multimedia content has led to a significant growth in the demand for effective methods to evaluate these contents. MovieQA seeks to gauge the understanding of a text-based description of movies in the form of a question-answering task. This provides a comprehensive framework for evaluating movie understanding capabilities of state-of-the-art models. The task involves answering a series of natural language questions about a given movie, considering time, entities, object-action relations, and character events in the narrative. Through in-depth experiments using a diverse set of models, it is demonstrated that this task adequately captures the level of multimodal reasoning as well as the temporal reasoning and cognitive aspects required for comprehending a movie's storyline. Furthermore, it is showcased that these methods have the capacity to recognize a wide range of movie-specific details and characters from various genres. This effectively supports the argument that MovieQA can be used as a comprehensive benchmark for movie understanding capabilities in visual understanding and computer vision research. Overall, MovieQA offers impressive insights into movie comprehension as well as a more comprehensive framework for thorough movie understanding. It also serves as a strong indicator of the efficiency and effectiveness of various models built using it for better comprehension of visual and multimedia content.

title: Embedding Label Structures for Fine-Grained Feature Representation
Abstract: This research proposes a novel embedding method that synergistically combines label structures with traditional metric learning techniques to achieve fine-grained feature representation. Recent advances in deep learning have led to the development of numerous feature extraction methods capable of capturing complex patterns and relationships within data. However, the resulting representations often lack subtle nuances and distinctions between closely related classes, hindering their ability to classify fine-grained categories accurately. To address this limitation, our proposed label embedding framework exploits the inherently structured nature of class labels to inject rich information into the feature space. By incorporating relationships between labels as explicit constraints in the optimization process, our method induces a more comprehensive and discriminative representation that preserves not only the general semantics of each class but also the intricate details that distinguish between similar classes. Comprehensive experiments conducted on state-of-the-art benchmark datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of our label embedding framework in significantly improving fine-grained classification accuracy, underscoring the potential of structured label information in enhancing the representational capabilities of deep neural networks. Compared to existing methods, our approach offers a unique blend of unsupervised learning and structured knowledge integration, providing a powerful tool for applications that demand robust feature representations capable of finely distinguishing between closely related classes.

title: Affinity CNN: Learning Pixel-Centric Pairwise Relations for Figure/Ground Embedding
Abstract: This work proposes Affinity CNN, a convolutional neural network architecture designed to learn pixel-centric pairwise relations for figure/ground embedding task, which is crucial in understanding visual scenes. The proposed approach is built upon a novel and differentiable formulation of pairwise affinities that takes into account both spatial and semantic dependencies between pixels in images. To effectively capture long-range and context-aware relations, the Affinity CNN incorporates a multi-resolution feature fusion module that hierarchically processes different scales of feature maps, allowing it to aggregate information from both local and global contexts. During the process, it uses two orthogonal attention mechanisms to adaptively select informative and relevant pixels, integrating spatial coherence and local features' inter dependencies to promote robust and context-aware figure/ground reasoning. Evaluations on standard benchmarks, including the PASCAL VOC2007 and SBD datasets, demonstrate the efficacy of the proposed Affinity CNN, achieving state-of-the-art performance in figure/ground embedding task compared to other relevant learning-based methods. Furthermore, extensive experiments also validate the strengths and benefits of its different component parts, providing valuable insights into the effectiveness of spatial, semantic information acquisition and processing upon this problem.

title: Sensor Fusion of Camera, GPS and IMU using Fuzzy Adaptive Multiple Motion Models
Abstract: This research paper delves into the realm of sensor fusion, specifically focusing on the integration of camera, GPS and Inertial Measurement Unit (IMU) data to create an adaptive multiple motion model. The sensor fusion problem is a classic challenge in the field of robotics and computer vision, where accurate estimation of vehicle or robot motion is crucial for navigation, mapping, and control. The proposed approach utilizes fuzzy logic to adapt to changing environmental conditions and handle uncertainty in the sensor data. Multiple motion models are employed to cater to different driving styles, road types, and weather conditions, thereby improving the overall robustness and accuracy of the system. A novel architecture is developed that combines the strengths of each individual sensor to generate a cohesive and accurate estimate of vehicle motion. The GPS data provides a coarse but reliable position estimate, while the camera and IMU complement this with rich visual and inertial information. The fuzzy adaptive approach enables the system to automatically adjust its model complexity and adapt to new situations, ensuring optimal performance under a wide range of scenarios. Experimental results demonstrate the efficacy of the proposed system in estimating vehicle motion with high accuracy, even in challenging conditions such as urban canyons and infrastructure interruptions.

title: Perfect Recovery Conditions For Non-Negative Sparse Modeling
Abstract: This paper presents a comprehensive study on the perfect recovery conditions for non-negative sparse modeling, a mathematical technique used to identify meaningful patterns in noisy and high-dimensional data. Non-negative sparse modeling has been widely employed in various fields, including computer vision, natural language processing, and bioinformatics, to uncover the underlying structures behind complex data sets. The paper focuses on the theoretical foundations of non-negative sparse modeling, specifically addressing the challenges associated with sparse signal recovery in the presence of non-negativity constraints. We provide a detailed analysis of the fundamental limits of non-negative sparse recovery, including necessary and sufficient conditions for exact recovery, and the characterizing parameters that influence recovery performance. Our results demonstrate that the recovery performance of non-negative sparse modeling is heavily dependent on the choice of algorithm, data representation, and sampling strategy, and that the existing recovery conditions are not universally applicable to all non-negative sparse models. Based on these insights, we propose novel recovery conditions, tailored to specific model and data characteristics, which significantly improve the recovery quality and robustness of non-negative sparse models. Our findings have important implications for the development of efficient and effective algorithms for non-negative sparse modeling, and we provide experimental evidence to illustrate the practical benefits of our proposed recovery conditions in real-world applications.

title: Window-Object Relationship Guided Representation Learning for Generic Object Detections
Abstract: The detection of generic objects in diverse visual contexts remains a fundamental challenge in the field of computer vision, owing to the complexities involved in characterizing the varying visual appearances and contexts of objects. Recent advances in deep learning have led to the development of powerful object detection approaches however, these methods often struggle to generalize effectively across different scenes and objects. This paper presents a novel representation learning framework that leverages the window-object relationship (WOR) to facilitate more effective generic object detection. By incorporating the WOR into the learning process, we aim to capture the relationships between objects and their surrounding contexts, enabling the model to adapt more effectively to diverse situations. Our approach involves designing a neural network architecture that integrates a window-object relationship branch with the standard object detection pipeline, allowing for the simultaneous learning of object features and contextual relationships. Through extensive experiments on popular benchmarks, we demonstrate the effectiveness of our WOR-guided representation learning framework, achieving state-of-the-art results and showcasing its robustness to variations in object size, location, and contextual scene details. By providing a more comprehensive understanding of the intricate relationships between objects and their contexts, our approach has the potential to revolutionize generic object detection in diverse visual scenes, offering a valuable contribution to computer vision research and applications.

title: Fine-grained Image Classification by Exploring Bipartite-Graph Labels
Abstract: Fine-grained image classification is a challenging task that involves distinguishing between subtle variations of the same category, often yielding outstanding results when applied in the realm of computer vision. Conventional deep learning methods, based solely on Euclidean structure, have exhibited limitations in capturing discriminative features from visually similar classes, ultimately restricting their fine-grained classification performance. To overcome these limitations, a novel bipartite-graph label-based approach is proposed, effectively exploring the non-Euclidean distance metric that inherently lies within the graph structure. This approach delineates label-sparse bipartite graphs, where images are denoted as vertices of two disjoint sets, represented by a homogeneous bipartite graph. Each vertex is assigned with edge weights that encode image similarities, thereby avoiding direct comparison between visually discriminative instances. By infusing graph signal processing techniques, such as sparse graph representation learning, with classification networks, the proposed framework successfully extracts discriminative image features that embody the underlying structural information of the bipartite graph. Consequently, the empirically evaluated experimental results validate the superior fine-grained classification performance achieved by the proposed approach in comparison to Euclidean-based methods. Moreover, the proposed framework showcases adaptability in being applicable to various fine-grained classification domains, underscoring its versatility, robustness, and efficacy.

title: Deep Exemplar 2D-3D Detection by Adapting from Real to Rendered Views
Abstract: This research explores the synergistic fusion of 2D and 3D object detection through a novel deep exemplar learning paradigm, specifically designed to adapt from real-world views to rendered views. We aim to bridge the seemingly disparate domains of computer vision and computer graphics by developing a unified framework that seamlessly transfers prior knowledge from 2D real-world object detection tasks to improve 3D detection performance in complex and dynamic scenarios. To achieve this, we propose a dual-modality neural network, dubbed Deep Exemplar Network (DEN), that harmoniously integrates a 2D-3D alignment module with an exemplar-based learning component. The alignment module ensures precise cohesiveness between the real and rendered views, while the exemplar-based learning module effectively captures the essential spatial-temporal cues between static and dynamic objects, thereby significantly enhancing the robustness and accuracy of 2D-to-3D object detection. Comprehensive experiments on challenging datasets, such as KITTI and SUN3D, demonstrate remarkable detection performance boosts by leveraging information from both real and rendered views. Our research provides an insightful perspective on the co-development of real-world and scene-understanding understanding, opening up the door for expanded application scenarios in robotics, autonomous navigation, and augmented reality.

title: Tracking Objects with Higher Order Interactions using Delayed Column Generation
Abstract: Our work addresses the challenging problem of tracking objects that exhibit complex, higher-order interactions in large-scale environments. Existing object tracking methods often struggle to accommodate these intricate relationships, particularly in scenarios where delays in updates or dynamics significantly change the state of objects. We present a novel delayed column generation (DCG) approach to efficiently track objects under higher-order interactions. In DCG, we generate columns of the subproblem just in time, as needed, to reduce the dimensionality of the problem, facilitating tractable solutions. Our key insight is to utilize the DCG framework to handle the interactions by formulating the higher-order relationships as nested subproblems, which can be solved using column-generation techniques. This approach enables handling interactions of any order, regardless of their size or complexity. The efficacy of our approach is demonstrated through extensive experiments on a range of scenarios, including complex tracking tasks, where objects interact with multiple other objects in varying ways. Our results show significant improvements in tracking accuracy compared to state-of-the-art methods on these problem spaces with many higher-order interactions, and we verify the efficiency of our proposed approach by characterizing its scalability properties in large-scale scenarios.

title: Towards the Application of Linear Programming Methods For Multi-Camera Pose Estimation
Abstract: Multi-camera pose estimation has garnered significant attention in recent years, with numerous applications in various fields including robotics, computer vision, and autonomous systems. The estimation of an object's pose from multiple camera viewpoints is a complex problem that involves 3D object reconstruction and alignment of 2D projective images. Traditional approaches have mainly used machine learning-based methods that rely on deep neural networks to learn the relationships between 2D image features and the estimated 3D pose. However, the lack of interpretability and the necessity for large amounts of labeled training data have limited the broader adoption of these methods. In this paper, we explore the application of linear programming methods for multi-camera pose estimation. By formulating the pose estimation problem as a linear program, we can utilize the power of linear programming solvers to efficiently estimate the object's 3D pose from noisy and incomplete data. Our approach leverages the strengths of linear programming to handle the scalability and robustness issues associated with traditional methods. We present a novel linear programming formulation for the problem, and demonstrate its effectiveness on a range of benchmark datasets. The results show that our linear programming-based method achieves comparable performance to state-of-the-art deep learning methods, while offering significant computational efficiency and interpretability advantages. The proposed method has the potential to be applied in scenarios where real-time estimation of object pose is necessary, such as in robotic grasping and object manipulation tasks.
