title: Collecting and Annotating the Large Continuous Action Dataset
Abstract: The ability of machines to understand and learn from large-scale action datasets has been pivotal in the advancement of various AI-driven applications. However, current state-of-the-art large-scale action datasets predominantly focus on fragmented frames of actions, neglecting the temporal dynamics and continuous nature of actions in real-world scenarios. To bridge this gap, we present a novel large continuous action dataset, comprising over 100,000 instances of continuous actions from real-world scenarios such as sports, dance, and everyday activities. The dataset is collected through a custom-designed annotation framework that captures both high-resolution videos and corresponding continuous action labels, enabling further exploration of complex relationships within actions. Our dataset leverages a more intuitive, graph-based annotation schema that incorporates relationships between various action states and parameters, facilitating more precise modeling of continuous actions. We evaluate the efficacy of our dataset and annotation framework through a series of comprehensive experiments and results demonstrate its ability to capture finer nuances of continuous actions compared to existing datasets. Our novel large continuous action dataset serves as a valuable resource for researchers and developers working on action recognition, action anticipation, and other related applications, offering unprecedented opportunities for addressing the shortcomings of existing datasets and driving innovation in the field.

title: Dense Human Body Correspondences Using Convolutional Networks
Abstract: This article presents an efficient computational framework for establishing dense human body correspondences between multiple views of a subject. The proposed method, termed as Convolutional Network-based Human Pose Estimation (CNN-HPE), utilizes a specially designed convolutional neural network architecture to establish correspondence between points on the human body across different poses and viewpoints. The CNN-HPE framework leverages a cascade of fully convolutional neural networks (FCNs) to progressively refine the estimation of human body keypoints. In the first stage, a Faster R-CNN-based network detects the human body region within the input images, followed by the keypoint estimation phase that generates an initial set of keypoints using the Hourglass network. Subsequently, a densely connected multi-resolution convolutional neural network is employed to refine the estimated keypoints and establish dense correspondences between the keypoints. Experiments conducted on several benchmark datasets, including the SMPL-X, NYU-H+P, and Human3.6M datasets, demonstrate the superiority of the proposed method over existing approaches in terms of accuracy, robustness, and computational efficiency. The CNN-HPE framework is shown to achieve state-of-the-art performance on various human pose estimation tasks, including 2D and 3D keypoint estimation, and has the potential to be extended to a wide range of applications in computer vision and human-computer interaction.

title: Particular object retrieval with integral max-pooling of CNN activations
Abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to particular object retrieval (POR) using integral max-pooling of convolutional neural network (CNN) activations. The proposed method leverages the strengths of CNNs in feature extraction and introduces a pooling strategy that selectively aggregates the activation patterns at different spatial locations. By combining max-pooling with integral calculus, the proposed method is able to rank-order feature maps based on their discriminative power for the target object, resulting in a more robust and accurate retrieval performance. The method is compared with state-of-the-art retrieval approaches and is shown to achieve superior performance on several benchmarks. Furthermore, experiments demonstrate that the proposed method can effectively adapt to variations in object pose, scale, and viewpoint. The proposed approach also significantly reduces the computational cost associated with traditional max-pooling methods by selectively processing a subset of feature maps. Extensive evaluations on datasets such as Oxford Buildings, Paris StreetView, and NUS-Wide are conducted to demonstrate the efficacy of the proposed method. The results show that the method can achieve superior retrieval accuracy and efficiency compared to traditional methods, making it a promising approach for various computer vision applications, including object recognition, image retrieval, and scene understanding.

title: Eigenspectra optoacoustic tomography achieves quantitative blood oxygenation imaging deep in tissues
Abstract: Deep in vivo blood oxygenation imaging is a critical aspect of studying various physiological and pathological processes, especially in the field of cancer research and neurological disorders where alterations in oxygen metabolism are hallmarks. However, conventional imaging modalities such as magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) and functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS) often face challenges in achieving quantitative blood oxygenation imaging, particularly at considerable depths within tissues. Recent advances in optoacoustic imaging have opened new avenues for overcame these limitations by employing the photoacoustic (PA) phenomenon. Specifically, optoacoustic imaging (OA) based on the eigenspectra has emerged as a promising technique for achieving quantitative blood oxygenation imaging in deep tissues. By leveraging matrix-based representations to capture multi-spectral photoacoustic (PA) signals, eigenspectra optoacoustic tomography demonstrates improved sensitivity, spatial resolution, and robustness against depth-dependent optical scattering and absorption that plague conventional imaging modalities. Preliminary results in healthy subjects and tumor-bearing animal models have shown the potential of eigenspectra optoacoustic tomography in visualizing regional and hemodynamic changes that associated with changes in blood oxygenation, highlighting its potential as a valuable diagnostic and monitoring tool.

title: From Pose to Activity: Surveying Datasets and Introducing CONVERSE
Abstract: This study delves into the realm of human pose estimation and its progression towards recognizing activities from 3D poses. The advent of pose estimation has led to a surge in research towards modeling human movements and interactions, which has numerous applications in fields such as computer vision, robotics, and healthcare. A comprehensive survey of existing datasets has been conducted to identify the key factors and challenges involved in activity recognition. The findings of this survey highlight the limitations of current datasets and highlight the need for datasets that capture a wide range of activities, different environments, and varying lighting conditions. To overcome these limitations, this study introduces CONVERSE (CONtinuous motion and VERbal activity recognition SYndrome), a novel dataset that showcases diverse human activities in everyday settings. The CONVERSE dataset is designed to capture not only the 3D poses but also the corresponding activity labels, providing a rich source of data for developing activity recognition models. Results from the CONVERSE dataset demonstrate the effectiveness of our proposed approach in recognizing activities, even in challenging scenarios such as occlusions and varying environments. The contributions of this study offer a promising direction for the development of more robust and accurate activity recognition systems, pushing the boundaries of human pose estimation and its applications.

title: Labeled pupils in the wild: A dataset for studying pupil detection in unconstrained environments
Abstract: The Labeled Pupils in the Wild dataset provides a comprehensive collection of images and annotations for studying pupil detection in unconstrained environments, serving as a valuable resource for researchers and developers working on vision-based applications that require accurate pupil detection. This dataset comprises over 100,000 images captured in various real-world scenarios, including indoor and outdoor environments, with diverse lighting conditions, head poses, and eyeblink states. Each image is annotated with precise pupil location and bounding box coordinates, as well as subject identity, head position, and gaze direction, allowing for extensive analysis and experimentation. By leveraging this dataset, we can better understand the limitations and challenges of pupil detection in unconstrained settings, enabling the development of more robust and accurate vision-based applications, such as emotion recognition, attention tracking, and human-computer interaction. We also analyze the shortcomings of existing pupil detection algorithms and propose novel evaluation metrics for assessing their performance in real-world scenarios. By sharing this dataset, we aim to foster research collaboration and accelerate advancements in vision-based applications that rely on pupil detection, ultimately enhancing the capabilities of human-machine interfaces and increasing our understanding of human behavior and cognition. The dataset is made available under a permissive license, enabling wide dissemination and facilitating future research directions.

title: Image Question Answering using Convolutional Neural Network with Dynamic Parameter Prediction
Abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to image question answering tasks by integrating a convolutional neural network (CNN) with a dynamic parameter prediction module, enabling the model to effectively capture and reason about object relationships within images. Traditional CNN-basedQA models often rely on fixed or shared parameters for feature extraction and answer prediction, which can limit their ability to accurately reason about complex relationships between objects. To address this challenge, we introduce a dynamic parameter prediction module that generates task-specific parameters for the CNN to focus on relevant features, adapt to varying input scenarios, and mitigate overfitting. Our proposed model, dubbed Dynamic Parameter CNN (DPCNN), consists of a multi-resolution feature pyramid network (ResNet) as the backbone CNN, a parameter prediction module based on the self-attention mechanism, and a knowledge fusion module for incorporating external knowledge graphs. Through extensive experiments on benchmark datasets such as Visual Question Answering (VQA) v1.0, VQA v2.0, and OpenEnded Visual QA, our results demonstrate that DPCNN achieves state-of-the-art performance, with a significant improvement of 2.5% in accuracy on VQA v1.0 and 3.2% on VQA v2.0, compared to the baseline ResNet model. We also provide in-depth ablation studies to validate the effectiveness of the proposed dynamic parameter prediction module, showcasing its potential in improving the robustness and generalizability of image QA models.

title: Compositional Memory for Visual Question Answering
Abstract:
Compositional Memory for Visual Question Answering abstract:
Visual question answering (VQA) is a complex task that requires both visual understanding and reasoning abilities. Traditional approaches to VQA typically employ neural networks that learn to represent visual features and question semantics separately, which limits their ability to model the compositional relationships between visual inputs and question components. In contrast, compositional memory networks aim to address this limitation by incorporating a distinct memory module that can store and retrieve visual features in a compositional manner. This memory module enables the network to selectively retrieve and combine relevant visual features based on the question components, facilitating more accurate and robust VQA performance. Our proposed compositional memory network for VQA consists of a visual encoder, a memory module, and a reasoning module, where the memory module stores a set of visual features and allows the network to selectively retrieve these features based on the question components. The reasoning module then combines the retrieved features to generate a final answer. By leveraging compositional memory, our proposed network effectively improves its ability to capture intricate visual and question relationships, leading to significant improvements in VQA accuracy and robustness. Experimenting with the CLEVR and Visual Genome datasets demonstrates the efficacy of our approach in surpassing state-of-the-art models for VQA.

title: Super-Resolution with Deep Convolutional Sufficient Statistics
Abstract: This paper proposes a novel deep learning approach to super-resolution that leverages sufficient statistics, addressing the computational efficiency and interpretability challenges encountered in traditional deep convolutional approaches. Building upon the concept of sufficient statistics, our method employs a probabilistic model that combines the merits of variational autoencoders and deep convolutional networks. By modeling the sufficient statistics of image data, our approach achieves high-quality super-resolution with significant computational savings, making it feasible for real-time applications. The proposed method inherits the interpretability of sufficient statistics, allowing for meaningful feature extraction and providing insights into the components that define high-resolution images. Our experiments demonstrate competitive performance with state-of-the-art methods, including notable improvements in inference time without compromising on resolution quality. By integrating principles of information theory and probabilistic modeling into deep learning architectures, this work sets a new foundation for developing efficient and interpretable super-resolution techniques. The efficacy of our approach is established through quantitative comparisons with prominent baseline methods, as well as extensive evaluations on various challenging datasets, showcasing its versatility in handling diverse image contents and degradation profiles. Overall, our contribution offers a fresh perspective on the synthesis of deep learning and sufficient statistics, enabling the efficient and interpretable recovery of high-resolution image details, thereby expanding the scope of practical super-resolution applications.

title: A New Smooth Approximation to the Zero One Loss with a Probabilistic Interpretation
Abstract: This paper introduces a novel smooth approximation to the zero-one loss function, a critical component in binary classification problems. The zero-one loss function evaluates the accuracy of a classifier by penalizing it for each misclassified instance, providing a stringent evaluation. However, the lack of smoothness often causes difficulties in the optimization process. The proposed approach, termed as the ' Probabilistic Zero-One Loss' (PZOL), achieves smoothness by considering the probabilistic interpretation of misclassification. By modeling misclassification as a probabilistic event, the PZOL approximates the zero-one loss while maintaining its original evaluation characteristics. Unlike other smooth approximations, the PZOL ensures a clear probabilistic correlation between the predicted probabilities and actual class labels, thus, facilitating a better understanding of model's predictions. The PZOL introduces a tunable parameter, controlling the degree of smoothness, and provides a closed-form expression, enabling efficient computations. Empirical evaluation on various benchmark datasets demonstrates the competitive performance of the PZOL, compared to existing smooth approximations, while retaining the theoretical guarantees of the zero-one loss. The results confirm that PZOL successfully balances smooth optimization with accurate classification performance, offering a compelling alternative in machine learning applications. Furthermore, the probabilistic interpretation of the PZOL facilitates explainability and offers new insights into understanding the behavior of binary classifiers.

title: Competitive Multi-scale Convolution
Abstract: This paper proposes a novel deep learning framework, referred to as Competitive Multi-scale Convolution (CMC), designed to address the limitations of current state-of-the-art models in capturing nuanced patterns and relationships within complex data. Traditional convolutional neural networks (CNNs) rely heavily on hand-engineered features and fixed receptive fields, which can lead to reduced expressive power and difficulties in modeling hierarchical representations. In contrast, CMC introduces a competitive mechanism to dynamically adapt the receptive field of convolutional kernels across multiple scales, allowing for more efficient learning of context-dependent features. By leveraging a multi-scale architecture, CMC is able to contextually combine features from different scales to effectively capture local and global patterns. The competitive mechanism is realized through a scalable and computationally efficient architecture, which integrates a novel "winner-takes-all" pooling approach and adaptive weighting of feature maps. Comprehensive experiments on diverse computer vision benchmarks demonstrate the efficacy of CMC, achieving superior performance compared to state-of-the-art models in tasks such as image classification, object detection, and segmentation. The results showcase the potential of CMC to serve as a versatile and high-performance solution for a wide range of applications.

title: Predicting distributions with Linearizing Belief Networks
Abstract: Predicting distributions such as model parameters, location, or times of events, is a fundamental challenge in various fields, including climate studies where such estimates are often used in hydrological modeling and weather forecasting. For instance predicting the distribution of climate variables such as precipitation in different regions requires sophisticated models that consider multiple factors, including but not limited to temperature, humidity, and wind patterns. Linearizing belief networks presented in this paper provide an approach to address this by simplifying complex interactions and thus can lead to better estimates of various outputs by reducing model complexity. The proposed method achieves linearization using a local quadratic approximation of probability functions, which enable the usage of traditional linear-in-the-parameters models while capturing complex dependencies. This reduces dependence on several hyperparameters which usually complicate the models while allowing the integration of information from both linear and probabilistic models. Evaluation through experiments involving hydrological data demonstrates the potential effectiveness of the framework where predictive skills lead to better outcomes without a significant increase in model complexity. These promising outcomes point to the potential use of linearizing belief networks for other environmental applications where better control over uncertainty remains an unsolved challenge.

title: Learning Structured Inference Neural Networks with Label Relations
Abstract: Structured inference neural networks have been increasingly used to solve various structured prediction tasks, such as image classification, natural language processing, and scene understanding. However, traditional structured neural networks lack the ability to capture complex label relations among output variables, leading to suboptimal prediction accuracy. This paper proposes a novel learning framework, called LR-INFOMAP, which incorporates label relations into the structured neural network inference architecture. By modeling the dependencies among output variables, LR-INFIMAP improves the accuracy of structured predictions and provides interpretable insights into the relationships between labels. Specifically, our approach uses a dynamic programming approach to compute the marginal distributions of individual labels and calculates the optimal assignment of labels based on the estimated label relations. Our experiments demonstrate that LR-INFIMAP outperforms existing structured neural networks on several benchmark datasets, including Pascal VOC, COCO, and Few-Shot learning. Furthermore, we show that the learned label relations provide meaningful insights into the underlying data structure and facilitate transfer learning across related tasks. Our results highlight the efficacy of LR-INFIMAP in capturing complex label relations and demonstrate its potential applications in various real-world domains.

title: Identifying the Absorption Bump with Deep Learning
Abstract: This study focuses on utilizing deep learning techniques to identify the absorption bump, a phenomenon commonly observed in spectroscopic data that can be indicative of specific chemical interactions or structures within a sample. Researchers have extensively employed traditional machine learning algorithms and conventional methods to analyze the absorption bump in various fields, including chemistry, physics, and materials science; however, deep learning techniques have been relatively unexplored for this particular application. Our research uses convolutional neural networks (CNNs) to automatically detect the absorption bump from spectroscopic data by learning the underlying features within the data. This approach offers a more objective and efficient means of identifying the absorption bump, reducing the reliance on human expertise and manual analysis. Furthermore, our study evaluates the robustness of the trained models against varying amounts of noise and artefacts present in real-world spectroscopic data. Experimental results demonstrate the potential of our proposed approach for accurate absorption bump identification and pave the way for its widespread adoption in various applications where deep learning techniques can be applied.

title: Return of Frustratingly Easy Domain Adaptation
Abstract: Domain adaptation, a fundamental problem in machine learning, has garnered significant attention in recent years for its ability to enable models trained on one dataset to generalize effectively on a different, yet related, dataset. Techniques for achieving domain adaptation have primarily focused on establishing alignment between source and target distributions, typically through adversarial training, feature alignment, or adversarial discriminative domain adaptation methods. However, despite significant advances, the performance gap between adapted and fine-tuned models remains substantial, particularly under the "Frustratingly Easy Domain Adaptation" scenario. Traditional methods still fall short in leveraging shared label information between domains to facilitate adaptation. Recent studies have demonstrated that, in certain instances, a precise solution or exact adaptation between the domains can be feasible. Therefore, the goal of this research is to explore the theoretical foundations, algorithmic frameworks, and practical applications of "Return of Frustratingly Easy Domain Adaptation" strategies, where an adapted model exhibits comparable or even superior performance to its fine-tuned counterpart on the target domain. This work aims to bridge the gap between theory and practice by developing and evaluating novel algorithms that can effectively adapt to domain shifts and leverage shared label information for improved performance under the Frustratingly Easy Domain Adaptation scenario.

title: Learning Articulated Motion Models from Visual and Lingual Signals
Abstract: This paper presents a comprehensive framework for learning articulated motion models from a combination of visual and linguistic signals. The proposed framework leverages the strengths of both modalities to jointly infer the motion models of complex articulated objects such as humans. The visual signal is represented by a series of images or videos, which are processed using convolutional neural networks (CNNs) to extract a set of motion features. These features are then projected onto a low-dimensional subspace, allowing for efficient representation and comparison of complex motion patterns. In parallel, the linguistic signal is represented by a sequence of natural language descriptions or instructions, which are processed using recurrent neural networks (RNNs) to extract a set of motion intent features. The two types of features are then fused using a novel attention-based mechanism, allowing the model to selectively focus on relevant features from either modality. Through this fusion, the proposed framework is able to learn a more comprehensive and accurate articulated motion model that captures both the low-level motion cues and the high-level motion intent. The effectiveness of the proposed framework is evaluated on several benchmarks, including the CMU movie datasets and the Human3.6M dataset, demonstrating superior performance over state-of-the-art methods. The framework has far-reaching implications for various applications, including human motion forecasting, motion planning, and natural language motion interaction.

title: Moral Lineage Tracing
Abstract: Moral Lineage Tracing explores the concept of inheritance and its impact on moral obligations, examining how our moral values and behaviors are shaped by our ancestral history. This study delves into the idea that moral principles and virtues are not solely a product of individual decision-making, but also have a collective dimension, emanating from the moral values and actions of our predecessors. By tracing the moral lineages of individuals and communities, researchers can gain insight into the depth and richness of moral inheritance. This approach recognizes that our moral compass is influenced by the cumulative wisdom and experiences of those who have come before us, and that moral values can be passed down through generations, taking the form of stories, cultural norms, and collective memories. The study sheds light on the complexities of moral development and the ways in which our actions influence not only our own moral character but also the moral legacy that we leave behind for future generations. Moral Lineage Tracing also offers a new perspective on the concept of intergenerational justice, emphasizing the importance of acknowledging and honoring the moral debts we owe to our ancestors, as well as our responsibilities towards the moral futures of our children and grandchildren.

title: Learning Neural Network Architectures using Backpropagation
Abstract: The development of complex neural network architectures has been a major driving force behind the recent advancements in deep learning. However, designing and optimizing these architectures can be a time-consuming and labor-intensive process, often requiring months of trial and error. This paper proposes a novel approach to learning neural network architectures using backpropagation, a technique commonly used for training neural networks. By integrating backpropagation into the architecture search process, we can leverage the power of gradient-based optimization to efficiently explore the vast space of possible neural network configurations. Our approach, dubbed "PropArch," uses a hierarchical representation of neural network architectures to parallelize the architecture search process, allowing for the simultaneous exploration of multiple architectures. Through a combination of backpropagation-based optimization and a novel regularization technique, we can selectively prune and modify existing architectures to encourage the growth of more efficient and effective neural network topologies. Our experimental results demonstrate that PropArch is capable of learning neural network architectures that outperform state-of-the-art models on a range of benchmark datasets, including ImageNet and CIFAR. With the potential to accelerate the development of neural network architectures by orders of magnitude, our approach presents a promising research direction for the field of deep learning.

title: Deep multi-scale video prediction beyond mean square error
Abstract: Deep multi-scale video prediction beyond mean square error has garnered significant attention in the realm of video generation, particularly in capturing the intricate relationships between consecutive frames. Conventional methods primarily rely on minimizing the mean square error (MSE) between predicted and ground truth frames, which often leads to artifacts such as blurry textures, unrealistic motion, and inadequate handling of complex scenes. Furthermore, these methods typically apply a single-scale architecture, disregarding the scale-aware characteristics of video data that encompass both fine-grained details and coarse motion trajectories. To address this limitation, we propose a novel deep multi-scale video prediction framework that integrates both temporal and spatial convolutional layers across multiple scales. This design enables the model to concurrently capture motion patterns and contextual details, thereby generating more realistic and accurate predictions. We verify the efficacy of our approach by comparing it to state-of-the-art architectures on a range of benchmarks, including the widely used UCF-101 and HMDB-51 datasets, showcasing improved performance in terms of peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR), structural similarity index (SSIM), and human evaluation metrics. Our results demonstrate the superiority of our framework in facilitating a more comprehensive understanding of video sequences and, as a consequence, highlighting the importance of surpassing MSE-based objectives in deep video prediction tasks.

title: Structural-RNN: Deep Learning on Spatio-Temporal Graphs
Abstract: Structural-RNN is a novel deep learning framework designed to effectively handle spatio-temporal graphs, where both the topology and the node features evolve over time. This framework addresses the limitations of existing approaches, which often struggle to capture the complex relationships between temporal and spatial information in graph data. For instance, in social network analysis, user interactions can be modeled as temporal graphs, where edges represent communication between individuals, and node attributes denote user characteristics. Furthermore, in traffic management, traffic congestion can be represented as a spatio-temporal graph, where nodes correspond to intersections or traffic signals, and edges indicate traffic flow between them. Structural-RNN leverages a hierarchical graph neural network architecture to recursively compute temporal graph representations, aggregating both spatial and temporal context. This enables the model to identify nuanced patterns and relationships that are critical in a wide range of applications, such as anomaly detection, node classification, and link prediction. By integrating a attention-based mechanism, Structural-RNN can focus on the most relevant graph components and dynamically adjust its representation learning based on evolving graph topologies, thereby improving its ability to tackle challenging real-world problems. Experimental results on various datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of Structural-RNN in capturing intricate spatio-temporal relationships and yielding state-of-the-art performance in multiple tasks.

title: Towards Predicting the Likeability of Fashion Images
Abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to predicting the likeability of fashion images, which is a critical aspect in the ever-evolving world of fashion. The increasing importance of social media platforms in fashion marketing has made it essential to understand what features of a fashion image are likely to capture the audience's attention and evoke their interest. Recent advances in computer vision and deep learning have enabled the development of models that can automatically analyze and understand visual content. Our proposed approach combines a convolutional neural network (CNN) with a gradient-boosting regressor to predict the likeability of fashion images. The CNN is trained on a dataset of fashion images labeled with their corresponding likeability scores, and the generated features are then used to train the gradient-boosting regressor. Our experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach, achieving a mean absolute error (MAE) of 0.67 and a correlation coefficient of 0.81 between the predicted and actual likeability scores. Additionally, we conduct an ablation study to investigate the impact of different visual features on the model's performance, and provide insights into the factors that contribute to the likeability of fashion images. Our findings have significant implications for the fashion industry, where designers and marketers can use our model to optimize the design and presentation of fashion images, leading to increased engagement and sales.

title: Hierarchical Spatial Sum-Product Networks for Action Recognition in Still Images
Abstract: This paper proposes a novel hierarchical spatial sum-product network (HSSPN) architecture for action recognition in still images, aiming to tackle the inherent spatial hierarchies and temporal dynamics of human actions. The proposed model excels in capturing complex spatio-temporal interactions within images, thereby enhancing the discriminative power for action recognition tasks. The HSSPN architecture incorporates a hierarchical structure, comprising two primary components: the spatial sum-product network (SSPN) and the temporal attention mechanism. The SSPN is designed to learn spatial hierarchies of visual features by modeling the mutual dependencies between pixels using a high-order probabilistic model, while the temporal attention mechanism exploits temporal dependencies by selectively weighting the spatial features across time. Integration of both components enables the model to effectively capture the spatial and temporal contexts of actions, thus improving the recognition accuracy for action classes. Experiments conducted on several benchmark datasets, including the widely used Stanford 40 action dataset and the more challenging MPII MPII humans dataset, demonstrate the superiority of the proposed HSSPN model over existing approaches, achieving state-of-the-art performance and highlighting its potential as a robust and efficient solution for action recognition tasks in still images. The findings of this research have implications for various computer vision applications, including surveillance, human-computer interaction, and medical image analysis, where accurate action recognition is of paramount importance.

title: Classifying and Segmenting Microscopy Images Using Convolutional Multiple Instance Learning
Abstract: Convolutional multiple instance learning (ConvMIL) has recently emerged as a crucial technique for classifying and segmenting microscopy images, which are complex and high-dimensional data sets. These images often contain various types of cellular features and provide critical information for disease diagnosis and understanding biological processes. However, manually analyzing and segmenting the features from microscopy images can be highly time-consuming and labor-intensive. To address this limitation, we propose a deep learning-based approach that combines the strengths of ConvMIL and convolutional neural networks (CNNs). Our proposed method consists of two main components: an image-level CNN for feature extraction and a bag-level CNN for classification and segmentation. The image-level CNN extracts localized features from the microscopy images, while the bag-level CNN mines and aggregates the relevant features to make a final decision. We achieve state-of-the-art results on several publicly available microscopy image datasets, including the Breast Cancer and WHIM-Fungi datasets. Experimental results demonstrate that our proposed method significantly outperforms existing state-of-the-art techniques in terms of accuracy, sensitivity, and specificity. Furthermore, we conduct a comprehensive analysis of the importance of different features in microscopy images to provide insights into their relevance for disease diagnosis and biological processes. This study provides a new perspective on the role of deep learning-based approaches for classifying and segmenting microscopy images and sheds light on the importance of feature extraction and aggregation in this context.

title: Deep Compositional Captioning: Describing Novel Object Categories without Paired Training Data
Abstract: Deep compositional captioning has garnered significant attention in the field of artificial intelligence and computer vision as a means of generating descriptive and informative captions for images. Despite the advancements in this field, most state-of-the-art models rely on the availability of paired training data, which can be expensive and time-consuming to obtain, particularly when addressing novel object categories. This paper proposes a novel approach to deep compositional captioning that eliminates the need for paired training data, thereby reducing the requirement for extensive manual annotation. By leveraging the power of reinforcement learning and pre-trained convolutional neural networks, the proposed model is able to learn the compositional structures and spatial relationships within images, enabling it to generate coherent and accurate captions for images containing novel object categories. The evaluation of the proposed model on several benchmark datasets demonstrates its robustness and efficacy, outperforming state-of-the-art models that rely on paired training data. Furthermore, the model's ability to generalize across image domains and novel object categories suggests its potential for real-world applications, including image description, scene understanding, and visual storytelling. By addressing the limitations of existing deep compositional captioning models, the proposed approach opens up new avenues for image understanding and generation, enabling the creation of more accurate and engaging visual content.

title: Robust PCA via Nonconvex Rank Approximation
Abstract: Robust Principal Component Analysis (PCA) via Nonconvex Rank Approximation is a novel approach to handle the perturbed rank-one structure in data, driven by emerging concepts from machine learning and theoretical computer science. Current methods relying on convex relaxation suffer from limited applicability due to their optimality gap and computational complexity. This paper presents a nonconvex optimization framework geared towards accurate rank approximation via efficient smoothing techniques. By leveraging this framework, we develop a new algorithm, referred to as Nonconvex Robust PCA (NRP), which can adapt to the actual data geometry and adapt to a range of perturbation settings. Our theoretical analysis yields an optimality gap of up to order 1/r and provides bounds on the sample complexity. Furthermore, we demonstrate the empirical superiority of NRP relative to several popular PCA algorithms in multiple challenging scenarios. Using both synthetic and real-world datasets contaminated with various perturbations (outliers and heavy-tailed errors), our simulations indicate that NRP efficiently extracts underlying principal components while achieving robustness against sub-Gaussian as well as heavy-tailed data perturbations. As the demand for robust and accurate representations of high-dimensional noisy data grows, our research offers practical and statistically sound advice for the application of robust PCA.

title: Ask, Attend and Answer: Exploring Question-Guided Spatial Attention for Visual Question Answering
Abstract: The ability to answer questions that require spatial reasoning in visual question answering has seen significant advancements with the introduction of spatial attention mechanisms. However, these existing mechanisms are primarily centered around localizing objects or regions within an image and then extracting the corresponding information. A more refined approach is to employ a question-guided spatial attention, allowing models to delve deeper into the nuances of a question and precisely where to focus within the image. The proposed framework, dubbed "Attend and Answer", incorporates a self-modulating attention mechanism, capable of processing complex queries that span multiple objects and their contextual relationships. By effectively leveraging the fine-grained details within an image and the logical structure inherent in a question, this framework enables the model to yield accurate, informative answers that resonate with human judgment. A series of comprehensive experiments conducted on various benchmark datasets demonstrate that the question-guided spatial attention significantly outperforms existing baselines in terms of answering accuracy, bridging the gap between state-of-the-art performance and human-level expertise.

title: Learning Expressionlets via Universal Manifold Model for Dynamic Facial Expression Recognition
Abstract: This study presents a novel approach to dynamic facial expression recognition leveraging the Universal Manifold Model (UMM) and the concept of expressionlets. The proposed methodology aims to effectively capture the nuanced temporal dynamics of facial expressions by breaking down the complex process into manageable components called expressionlets. These expressionlets are defined as localized and coordinated patterns of facial muscle movements that contribute to the overall recognition of emotions. By incorporating the manifold learning framework, the Universal Manifold Model transforms raw facial expression data into a lower-dimensional latent space, preserving the inherent structural properties and nuances characteristic to each expression. This leads to improved robustness against variations in expression, face pose, and lighting conditions. Furthermore, the UMM enables the efficient identification of expressionlets by mapping the expression sequence onto a continuous manifold. Experiments conducted on benchmark datasets demonstrate the efficacy of the proposed approach, outperforming state-of-the-art methods in terms of accuracy, precision, and recall. The findings of this study contribute significantly to the development of universal facial expression recognition systems capable of classifying the full range of human emotions with high accuracy, paving the way for their application in affective computing and human-computer interaction. The proposed method's capacity to capture subtle expression dynamics and adapt to non-stationary expression patterns makes it a promising solution for real-world scenarios involving dynamic facial expression recognition.

title: Visualizing and Understanding Deep Texture Representations
Abstract: Deep texture representations have become a crucial component in various computer vision tasks, including image classification, object detection, and image segmentation, due to their ability to capture intricate textures and patterns present in natural images. However, interpreting and understanding the features learned by these texture representations remain a challenging problem, primarily due to the complex and hierarchical nature of deep convolutional neural networks (CNNs). This paper proposes a novel approach to visualize and comprehend deep texture representations, focusing on understanding how the texture features contribute to visual perception. By employing a combination of visualization techniques, such as heatmaps, feature importance analysis, and attention mechanisms, we aim to elucidate the complex interactions between different texture elements and their corresponding semantic meanings. our proposed approach employs state-of-the-art deep learning architectures, including residual connections and bottleneck features, to capture detailed and high-level texture information. Furthermore, we design a custom loss function to modulate the learning process of the texture features and enhance their saliency and relevance to the visual tasks at hand. Through extensive experimentation and analysis on various texture-based datasets, our results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach in improving the interpretability and robustness of deep texture representations. The insights gained from this study have the potential to advance the field of computer vision and facilitate the development of more practical and user-friendly texture-based applications.

title: Convolutional Models for Joint Object Categorization and Pose Estimation
Abstract: This paper proposes a novel deep learning framework that integrates object categorization and pose estimation tasks into a single, end-to-end convolutional model. The model is designed to simultaneously predict both the category label and the 3D pose of an object from a single RGB image, thereby achieving a more comprehensive understanding of the visual scene. Inspired by recent successes in joint tasks, our proposed architecture leverages a shared convolutional backbone and employs separate but shallow branches for object categorization and pose estimation, which are connected through a mid-level feature fusion layer. This allows for richer and more informative feature representations to be shared across the two tasks, bypassing traditional sequential processing pipelines that suffer from information loss and diminished accuracy. Extensive experiments are conducted on several benchmark datasets, including the PASCAL VOC and PASCAL-Person-Part datasets, demonstrating significant improvements in both object categorization and pose estimation accuracy, with a notable increase in precision and recall. The results of these experiments highlight the practical benefits and potential applications of our joint convolutional model in robotics, autonomous vehicles, and other real-world scenarios where accurate object categorization and pose estimation are crucial for decision-making. The contributions of this work include a novel architecture that efficiently integrates two critical tasks and achieve superior performance on multiple datasets, thus advancing the state of the art in deep learning-based computer vision and paving the way for future research in this area.

title: Cross-scale predictive dictionaries
Abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to cross-scale predictive dictionaries, which aims to bridge the gap between local and global resolution in high-dimensional data analysis. Building upon the fundamental idea of traditional dictionaries, the developed framework leverages hybrid learning strategies to capture localized features and adaptability at different scales, significantly improving the robustness and interpretability of dictionary learning. By utilizing multi-scale analysis and fusion techniques, the proposed approach effectively identifies coherent representation patterns across a wide range of scales, which can be tailored to various applications and computational complexities. Key benefits of this method include the ability to automatically detect and resolve cross-scale representations from raw data, enabling more accurate and efficient inference of tasks such as data compression, denoising, dimensionality reduction, feature extraction, and predictive modeling in a variety of domains. The proposed cross-scale dictionary learning framework is demonstrated to outperform existing state-of-the-art methods in experiments involving both synthetic and real-world datasets, including those exhibiting inherent scale invariance. The obtained results demonstrate great potential for extending the applications of traditional dictionary learning methods to domains where accurate modeling of cross-scale dynamics is essential.

title: Nonlinear Local Metric Learning for Person Re-identification
Abstract: Person re-identification (Re-ID) is a challenging task in computer vision and pattern recognition that involves identifying the same individual across non-overlapping camera views. Current state-of-the-art approaches primarily rely on metric learning, which aims to learn the similarity measure between instances, assuming that the same identity corresponds to a small distance in the feature space. However, most existing methods are linear and overlook the inherent non-linearity in the data, resulting in suboptimal performance in handling variations in environments, poses, and occlusions. This paper focuses on addressing these limitations by proposing a nonlinear local metric learning approach for person Re-ID. The proposed method, named Nonlinear Local Distance Metric Learning (NL DML), effectively models the non-linear relationships between instances from the same identity by learning the distance metric between local features. NL DML comprises two main components: a spatial-temporal attention module that captures the context-dependent features and a local metric learning module that learns the non-linear distance metric. Extensive experimental results on six benchmark datasets demonstrate that NL DML significantly outperforms state-of-the-art Re-ID methods, achieving higher accuracy and robustness against variations in environments and poses. The proposed approach has the potential to be applied in various practical applications, including surveillance and security, pedestrian detection, and multi-camera tracking.

title: Adversarial Manipulation of Deep Representations
Abstract: Deep neural networks have become ubiquitous in modern computing, revolutionizing tasks such as image classification, object detection, and natural language processing through their ability to learn complex patterns in data. However, a growing body of research has highlighted the vulnerability of these models to adversarial manipulation, where an attacker carefully crafts input data to elicit a specific, often undesirable response from the model. In this paper, we explore the phenomenon of adversarial manipulation of deep representations, where an attacker injects malicious information into a model's intermediate layer outputs to achieve targeted outcomes. We survey recent advances in adversarial manipulation techniques, including attack methods that leverage gradient masking, input preprocessing, and model compression, and examine the threat posed by these attacks in real-world applications. Our analysis reveals a disturbing trend: as models become increasingly sophisticated, their vulnerability to adversarial manipulation grows, threatening the integrity and reliability of critical systems that rely on them. We highlight several open challenges in the field, including the need for more robust attack detection methods and more efficient model defenses. Our findings contribute to a broader understanding of the risks and limitations of adversarial manipulation of deep representations and underscore the critical need for further research in this area.

title: Yin and Yang: Balancing and Answering Binary Visual Questions
Abstract: This paper proposes an approach to image processing for answering binary visual questions, a task where a model must determine if an object or attribute exists or does not, such as "does the image contain a cat?" or "is the object red?" Traditional approaches to image understanding have focused on classifying objects into predefined categories, but this task requires a different set of skills, including object localization, feature extraction, and question-specific reasoning. The yin and yang principle, a philosophical concept describing the interconnected opposites of the universe, serves as the foundation for our proposed method. We argue that an image and its corresponding question can be represented as a dualistic system, where one side (yin) includes the visual features and context, while the other side (yang) comprises the question-specific criteria and reasoning mechanism. Our approach utilizes a two-stream neural network framework, where the yin stream is responsible for extracting visual features, and the yang stream represents the processing of question-specific information. The output of the yin stream is then combined with the yang stream to generate the final answer. Through extensive experiments on multiple benchmark datasets and question types, we demonstrate the effectiveness of our method in answering binary visual questions with high accuracy, even when the question is ambiguous or requires a nuanced understanding of the visual features. Our results show promise for applications in visual dialogue systems, image-only question answering, and more.

title: Understanding learned CNN features through Filter Decoding with Substitution
Abstract: This research delves into the unknown world of deep neural networks, particularly Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs), to unravel the secrets behind their learned features through novel Filter Decoding with Substitution approach. The rise of CNNs has led to unprecedented success in various computer vision tasks, yet understanding the mechanics behind their feature extraction process remains challenging. To address this issue, a Filter Decoding with Substitution framework is proposed, aiming to decode and interpret the learned features of CNNs through iterative substitutions of original learned weights with approximate and decomposite representations. This method leverages the concept of feature deconstruction, where individual learned features are decoded back to the domain of convolutional and pooling operators, enabling researchers to gain insights into how CNNs perceive and process visual information. The proposed framework is composed of three primary components: feature aggregation, substitution, and reconstruction. Initially, aggregated features from multiple filter responses are computed, followed by the substitution of original feature maps with the reconstructed ones, allowing for the representation of learned weight connections. Alongside theoretical in-depth analysis, extensive experiments are conducted on several benchmark datasets, demonstrating the efficacy and interpretability of the proposed Filter Decoding with Substitution approach in visualizing and understanding the feature learning process of CNNs.

title: Proposal Flow
Abstract: This paper provides an in-depth analysis of the concept of proposal flow, examining the intricate network of factors that influence the proposal development process across various industries and organizational settings. By leveraging insights from business management, operations research, and organizational behavior, the authors uncover the key drivers of proposal success, including strategic planning, stakeholder alignment, knowledge management, and performance measurement. A mixed-methods approach combining both qualitative and quantitative data collection and analysis techniques was employed to gather empirical evidence from both published sources and real-world case studies of organizations that have successfully leveraged proposal flow to secure lucrative contracts and improve their competitive positioning. The results of this study reveal that effective proposal flow requires a delicate balance between human elements, such as communication and collaboration, and technological enablers, such as project management information systems and collaboration platforms. The study also demonstrates that iterative refinement of the proposal content and process is essential to aligning it with stakeholder needs and preferences. The findings of this research have significant implications for practitioners seeking to improve the accuracy, efficiency, and effectiveness of their proposal development processes, and offer a framework for the design and implementation of tailored proposal flow strategies that can enhance the chances of securing contracts and achieving project success.

title: An Empirical Study of Recent Face Alignment Methods
Abstract: Recent face alignment methods have undergone significant advancements, fueled by the proliferation of facial analysis in various applications such as computer vision, deep learning, and human-computer interaction. This study aims to provide an empirical investigation of several state-of-the-art face alignment techniques, exploring their efficacy, efficiency, and robustness in handling varying lighting conditions, pose, and facial expressions. By comparing the performance of different alignment methods, including Regression-based approaches, Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs), and Attention-based networks, we seek to identify the strengths and weaknesses of each approach and provide insights into the ideal conditions for their application. Furthermore, we investigate the effect of data augmentation on the performance of face alignment methods, as well as the impact of using pre-trained models, such as those pre-trained on large-scale datasets like FaceNet, to initialize the alignment process. Our empirical study leverages a diverse dataset consisting of images with varying lighting conditions, pose, and facial expressions, and evaluates the performance of each method using metrics such as mean squared error, peak signal-to-noise ratio, and qualitative assessments. The findings of this study will contribute to a deeper understanding of the current state-of-the-art in face alignment, enabling researchers and practitioners to make informed decisions when selecting the most suitable method for their specific application.

title: Handcrafted Local Features are Convolutional Neural Networks
Abstract: This study delves into the intersection of classical computer vision and deep learning techniques to design a novel handcrafted local feature extraction framework, known as LCNN-Feats. LCNN-Feats employs the principles of convolutional neural networks (CNNs) to effectively capture essential information from images, while simultaneously using traditional local feature properties such as spatial co-occurrence, saliency, and spatial periodicity. Through extensive experimentation using the benchmark datasets for object detection and recognition, LCNN-Feats is compared with several state-of-the-art deep learning architectures, revealing its superior performance and efficiency in extracting descriptive local features. The designed handcrafted local feature extraction framework was demonstrated to reduce the dimensionality of the feature space while incrementally increasing the recognition accuracy through effective detection and description of subtle image patterns that are often lost in purely deep learning-based approaches. The significance of LCNN-Feats resides in its ability to serve as a viable alternative to conventional CNNs for a wide range of computer vision applications, including visual search, image retrieval, object detection, and scene understanding, due to its improved performance and feasible computational complexity. Furthermore, our results suggest that LCNN-Feats could facilitate transfer learning for various deep learning architectures, and empower researchers to selectively combine the strengths of traditional computer vision and deep learning techniques for advancing their research endeavours.

title: Sample and Filter: Nonparametric Scene Parsing via Efficient Filtering
Abstract: Scene parsing plays a crucial role in computer vision, enabling the understanding and interpretation of images by mapping pixels to semantic labels. Most existing scene parsing methods rely on deep learning architectures, which, although achieving remarkable results, often require a substantial number of labeled training examples, are computationally expensive, and assume prior knowledge of the datasets's statistical properties. This limitation imposes significant constraints on deployment in resource-scarce environments and real-world settings where data may not be readily available or may exhibit non-rigid structures. Acknowledging these challenges, this paper introduces a novel nonparametric scene parsing approach that abandons reliance on conventional parametric models and presents an efficient filtering technique to deal with intricate scenes. By combining nonparametric components with computationally efficient filtering, this method effectively circumvents the limitations imposed by conventional deep learning-based architectures. Our proposed model, empowered by efficient filtering, promotes robustness and accuracy, allowing it to handle complex scenes while leveraging minimal labeled data. Extensive experiments validate the efficacy of our method, demonstrating capabilities that surpass those of deep learning-based approaches in certain scenarios. The proposed framework not only opens new avenues for scene parsing in resource-constrained environments but also provides a more adaptable paradigm for real-world applications where robust and generalizable scene understanding is essential.

title: Identification and Counting White Blood Cells and Red Blood Cells using Image Processing Case Study of Leukemia
Abstract: This paper presents a case study on the application of image processing in the identification and counting of white blood cells (WBCs) and red blood cells (RBCs) with a specific focus on diagnosing leukemia. The proposed system utilizes a combination of image filtering, thresholding, and feature extraction techniques to accurately identify and classify the morphology of WBCs and RBCs from microscopic images. A thorough literature review is conducted to identify the current state-of-the-art methods employed in image-based blood cell analysis, highlighting their limitations and opportunities for improvement. The proposed system is evaluated on a dataset of 200 images of peripheral blood smear samples, obtained from patients with suspected leukemia and age-matched controls. Results show that the proposed method achieves a high accuracy of 92.5% in distinguishing between abnormal and normal WBCs and an accuracy of 89.2% in differentiating between RBCs and other blood cells, based on their morphology. A systematic comparison is made with existing methods, demonstrating the superiority of the proposed system. Furthermore, the proposed system is capable of efficiently counting blood cells in a relatively short time, which is particularly useful in clinical settings where time-sensitive decisions require precise results. The findings of this research demonstrate the potential of image processing in improving the diagnosis of leukemia, reducing the complexity of the process, and providing more accurate and reliable results.

title: Performing Highly Accurate Predictions Through Convolutional Networks for Actual Telecommunication Challenges
Abstract: Predicting technological issues and disturbances in telecommunication networks is critical for providing uninterrupted service to customers. Despite advances in machine learning and its applications, actual telecommunication challenges such as predicting network congestion, signaling failures and identifying frequency bands occupied by other networks, and equipment faults pose significant challenges. Convolutional neural networks have shown great potential in solving computer vision and image processing tasks, but their applications in telecommunication domain remain under researched. This study aims to address this research gap by designing and implementing a highly accurate convolutional neural network framework for predicting telecommunication challenges. The proposed framework incorporates feature extraction and selection methods to identify salient features from telecommunication temporal signal data and maps them to appropriate probability distributions. Using simulated telecommunication data with a large number of patterns, we demonstrate the ability of our framework to make highly accurate predictions at both regional and global levels, outperforming state-of-the-art models by large margins. The results of this study have significant implications for the development of intelligent network monitoring and control systems, enabling proactive interventions to prevent network failures and ensure high-quality communication services. Our findings also shed light on potential applications of convolutional neural networks in other time-series analysis tasks.

title: Graph-based denoising for time-varying point clouds
Abstract: This paper presents an innovative graph-based denoising approach for time-varying point clouds. Point clouds, obtained from various sources such as LiDAR scanners or 3D cameras, often suffer from noise and outliers, hindering their applications in fields like computer vision, robotics, and 3D reconstruction. Conventional denoising methods, primarily algebraic or iterative approaches, may not effectively address the complexities of time-varying point clouds where data is dynamic and experiences variations over time. To address these challenges, the proposed method utilizes a graph-based formulation where points are represented as nodes in a dynamic graph, connected by edges that capture the spatial and temporal relationships between them. By employing a spectral graph regularization function and iteratively refining the graph structure, the method effectively removes noise and outliers, preserving the underlying structure of the time-varying point cloud. Extensive experiments and comparisons with state-of-the-art methods demonstrate the superiority of the proposed approach in terms of noise reduction, accuracy, and computational efficiency, making it an attractive solution for applications involving dynamic and noisy point cloud data. The approach also exhibits robustness to varying point density and temporal resolution, underscoring its practicality in real-world scenarios.

title: Coarse-to-fine Face Alignment with Multi-Scale Local Patch Regression
Abstract: This paper presents an enhanced face alignment approach leveraging coarse-to-fine processing via multi-scale local patch regression, showcasing a novel framework to refine facial feature detection precision. By incorporating an optimization strategy, our proposed method demonstrates significantly improved handling of various facial landmark identification scenarios, particularly under challenging conditions such as facial expressions, poses, and occlusions. Initially, a coarse face alignment stage employs a highly efficient convolutional neural network (CNN), designed for rapid, initial face processing and landmark localization. This stage generates an initial estimate that informs the subsequent, more refined facial landmark adjustment process, operational at a finer spatial scale. In the refinement stage, we aggregate and adapt multiple hierarchical feature representations from a pre-trained, deep-face model, capturing patch-wise locality, scale-varying relationships, and distribution-constrained information relevant to more accurate face alignment outcomes. Through its comprehensive coarse-to-fine strategy effectively integrating global and local knowledge, this face alignment method noticeably enhances the accuracy and dependability of facial feature landmark localization, notably when addressing relatively rare, but critical face representation scenarios. Consequently, our framework is suitable for more dependable applications in the field of computer vision, where accurate and robust facial feature detection is paramount.

title: Fast clustering for scalable statistical analysis on structured images
Abstract: This paper addresses the pressing need for fast and scalable statistical analysis on structured images, which is a fundamental task in various applications such as computer vision, medical imaging, and geographic information systems. Existing approaches often rely on k-means clustering, which can be computationally expensive and may not be suitable for large-scale structured images due to its high time complexity. To overcome this limitation, we propose a new fast clustering algorithm specifically designed for structured images. Our approach, called hierarchical spectral clustering (HSC), leverages the inherent structure of images to reduce the dimensionality and identify clusters efficiently. HSC first transforms the image into a graph representation, where each pixel is a node connected to its neighbors, and then applies a combination of spectral techniques and hierarchical clustering algorithms to identify clusters. Experimental results on various datasets show that HSC can achieve significant speedups over traditional k-means clustering, while maintaining competitive accuracy. Furthermore, HSC can handle large-scale images with millions of pixels, making it a viable solution for scalable statistical analysis on structured images. The proposed method has been implemented and made available for public use, providing a user-friendly interface for researchers and practitioners.

title: Sherlock: Scalable Fact Learning in Images
Abstract: This paper presents Sherlock, a state-of-the-art fact-learning framework designed to scale up the extraction of implicit relations from image data. Unlike previous methods that rely on annotating relationships or employing off-the-shelf knowledge graph embeddings, Sherlock learns to reason about image-based facts directly from raw pixel data. Capitalizing on the strengths of weakly-supervised learning, Sherlock disentangles the complex interplay between image features, object locators, and contextual understanding using a novel multi-modal learnable architecture. The architecture seamlessly integrates pairwise image embeddings, graph networks, and a structured representation parser, enabling it to automatically discover new object-attribute co-occurrences and object-relationship patterns in a scalable manner. Empowered by transfer learning and adversarial training, Sherlock efficiently adapts to diverse image datasets, successfully bridging the semantic gap between attributes and relationships. By tapping into the power of generalization and transferability, Sherlock demonstrates impressive accuracy in common sense reasoning and graph-based inference tasks, outperforming existing state-of-the-art models on large-scale image fact-learning benchmarks. Additionally, Sherlock exhibits robustness to varying image complexities, annotated sparsity, and external biases, illuminating its adaptability and generalizability in practical applications, from image-based knowledge retrieval to social graph construction.

title: Deep learning is a good steganalysis tool when embedding key is reused for different images, even if there is a cover source-mismatch
Abstract:
Abstract: 
The proliferation of digital images in various applications has led to an increasing demand for secure communication through steganalysis, which enables the detection of hidden secrets within seemingly innocuous files. Deep learning, with its potent feature extraction capabilities, has emerged as an effective steganalysis tool in recent years. Notably, a novel threat has arisen in the form of steganographic attacks where a reusable key is employed for modifying and embedding secret data across multiple images, even when there is an apparent source mismatch between the cover images and the embedded data. In this context, this research explores the security vulnerability posed by such attacks and delves into the efficacy of deep learning-based steganalysis techniques in detecting embedded secrets under these conditions. Our work reveals that traditional machine learning-based steganalysis approaches often falter in the face of reused keys and cover source-mismatch attacks, highlighting a pressing need for more robust and adaptive steganalysis strategies. Conversely, we demonstrate that deep learning-based methods can effectively bypass these security breaches and identify embedded secrets with remarkable accuracy, even in the presence of significant variations in cover images. Our comprehensive experimental evaluation and theoretical analyses demonstrate the potential of deep learning in developing highly effective steganalysis solutions, underscoring its transformative value in maintaining the integrity and confidentiality of digital communications.

title: Learning Mid-level Words on Riemannian Manifold for Action Recognition
Abstract: This research focuses on devising a novel approach for action recognition that leverages the learning of mid-level words on a Riemannian manifold. The proposed approach, denoted as Mid-level Words on Riemannian Manifold (MWRM), recognizes that complex actions can be decomposed into a set of fundamental motion patterns or mid-level words. These mid-level words are abstract representations that capture the essence of different phases within an action. The Riemannian manifold is used as a challenging but meaningful framework to model the geometric variability and similarities between different mid-level words, rendering it suitable for representing and comparing complex action sequences. To achieve this, the MWRM approach employs a novel combination of spatial-temporal convolutional neural networks (CNNs) and Riemannian geometry. The spatial- temporal CNNs learn to extract motion features from video sequences, which are subsequently mapped onto the Riemannian manifold using a Riemannian metric. The mapped representations are then clustered to obtain mid-level words, which serve as a language-free representation for complex actions. In the recognition phase, the learned mid-level words are assigned to action categories by computing proximity-based similarity with weighted shortest path algorithms. Experimental results on several benchmark datasets demonstrate the compelling efficacy of MWRM in accurately recognizing complex actions, outperforming state-of-the-art methods. The proposed approach not only showcases the value of Riemannian geometry in action recognition but also paves the way for developing more effective and robust methods for modeling and recognizing human actions.

title: Heterogeneous Knowledge Transfer in Video Emotion Recognition, Attribution and Summarization
Abstract: This research paper explores the development of a comprehensive and adaptive video emotion recognition, attribution, and summarization framework, allowing it to incorporate and adapt knowledge from diverse sources, including multimodal data, emotional labels, and semantic annotations. To address the complexity of video data, we propose a proposed heterogeneous knowledge transfer approach that integrates multiple modalities, such as speech, vision, and text, and leverages diverse knowledge sources, like labels, metadata, and pre-trained models. Our framework utilizes a hybrid multimodal fusion architecture that effectively combines information from various sources, including audio, image, and text, captured within the video. This framework aims to overcome the challenges in knowledge transfer, such as data imperfections, class imbalance, and semantic gaps, through a carefully designed transfer learning module. We demonstrate the efficacy of our proposed framework in video emotion attribution and summarization, showing that the inclusion of heterogeneous knowledge significantly improves model performance and interpretability. Specifically, we evaluate our framework on various benchmark datasets for video emotion recognition and compare its results with state-of-the-art models, highlighting its enhanced capability in emotion detection, contribution analysis, and summary generation.

title: Complete Dictionary Recovery over the Sphere II: Recovery by Riemannian Trust-region Method
Abstract: This paper presents a novel approach for complete dictionary recovery based on the Riemannian trust-region method, referred to as Complete Dictionary Recovery over the Sphere II (CDRS-II). Given an accurate sparse representation model with limited noise, CDRS-II recovers a dictionary that exactly matches the ground truth except for a permutation and/or a sign flip. The proposed algorithm adopts a model-based approach to benefit from the sparsity and symmetry of the dictionary while addressing the uniqueness of the solution via a low-dimensional manifold. The recovery process is further accelerated with an Riemannian trust-region method. This non-convex optimization framework enables the dictionary to be recovered with a controlled number of iterations and provides a range of theoretical and numerical guarantees on the convergence properties. The performance of the Riemannian trust-region method is empirically demonstrated with a series of simulations, both on general and highly structured dictionaries, illustrating the improved efficiency and higher success rate over state-of-the-art competitors such as CDRS-I under similar conditions. The results not only confirm the effectiveness of CDRS-II but also the adaptability of the Riemannian trust-region method to applications where convex relaxations may not suffice or fail to converge.

title: Separation Surfaces in the Spectral TV Domain for Texture Decomposition
Abstract: Texture decomposition is a vital task in the field of computer vision and image processing, enabling applications such as object detection, image segmentation, and feature extraction. However, the challenge of decomposing textured images into their basic components remains an open problem. This paper proposes a novel approach to texture decomposition by leveraging separation surfaces in the spectral Total Variation (TV) domain. The underlying hypothesis is that textures can be represented as a superposition of simple texture components, each corresponding to a specific separation surface. The key innovation lies in the introduction of a novel potential function that enables the explicit modeling of separation surfaces in the spectral domain. The potential function, tailored to the characteristics of each texture component, is integrated within a variational framework to formulate an optimization problem. The resulting optimization problem is then solved using a tailored splitting algorithm, leveraging the structure of the TV regularization term. This approach provides an efficient and scalable way to separate textures from their backgrounds, while also enabling the processing of complex textures with multiple components. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed framework, showcasing its ability to achieve state-of-the-art results in texture decomposition tasks.
