title: Semi-Inner-Products for Convex Functionals and Their Use in Image Decomposition
Abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to image decomposition using semi-inner-products for convex functionals. Traditional methods for image decomposition often rely on norm-based or convex-concave functionals that are sensitive to noise and outliers. Semi-inner-products, on the other hand, offer a flexible framework for combining different types of information and constraints in a unified manner. The proposed approach utilizes a hierarchical model consisting of a bilateral filter and a parametric operator-based semi-inner-product, which enables the decomposition of an image into a base layer and a detail layer. A convex functional is then applied to the combined semi-inner-product to obtain a sparse representation of the detail layer. The efficiency and effectiveness of the proposed approach are demonstrated through various experiments, including noise reduction, superresolution, and image inpainting. The results show superior performance compared to state-of-the-art methods in terms of both visual quality and quantitative metrics. Furthermore, the proposed approach is shown to provide a robust and scalable solution for image decomposition tasks. The proposed hierarchical model and semi-inner-product framework can be extended and applied to other image processing tasks, such as image denoising, image filtering, and image segmentation. Overall, this work contributes to a deeper understanding of semi-inner-products and their potential applications in image decomposition.

title: Uncovering Temporal Context for Video Question and Answering
Abstract: This work focuses on addressing the challenge of understanding and incorporating temporal context for effectively tackling video question answering (VideoQA) tasks, which involve retrieving answers to complex queries from videos by interpreting the entire sequence of events or scenes presented. While significant advancements have been made in video understanding and question answering, they largely overlook the inherently temporal nature of video content, neglecting the sequential and temporal relationships between video segments. In order to address this limitation, we design and implement two novel components: the Temporal Segment Graph (TSG) and the spatio-temporal reasoning module (STRM). The TSG provides a structured representation of a video's temporal segments by modeling the inherent relationships between them, whereas the STRM focuses on incorporating object information from multiple modalities (including text, visual, and audio) to track entities' evolution across time, thus modeling the temporal dynamics within a video. In this paper, we empirically evaluate the effectiveness of these methods on various videoQA benchmarks and demonstrate that the incorporation of temporal context indeed elevates the videoQA performance by a significant margin. Our experimental study highlights the significant role of temporal context in accurately resolving videoQA queries and identifies areas for further improvement in developing more powerful video understanding models that can ingest and exploit the underlying temporal structure of a video, thereby yielding superior performance on videoQA tasks. Moreover, our findings offer insights into the mechanisms of how incorporating temporal context enhances the model's reasoning capabilities, benefiting various real-world applications, such as multimedia analysis and content summarization.

title: Deep Neural Network for Real-Time Autonomous Indoor Navigation
Abstract: This paper proposes a deep neural network-based approach for real-time autonomous indoor navigation. The increasing demand for efficient and accurate navigation systems in indoor environments, such as warehouses, offices, and museums, has motivated the development of this research. By leveraging the strengths of deep learning algorithms and computer vision techniques, our proposed system aims to provide a reliable and scalable solution for navigating complex indoor spaces. The system employs a multisensor fusion framework, combining data from various sources including LiDAR, cameras, and inertial measurement units (IMUs), to achieve robust and accurate mapping and localization. A novel U-Net architecture is designed and trained to process the fused sensor data, enabling the system to learn and adapt to the indoor environment in real-time. Through our experimental evaluation, we demonstrate the effectiveness of our proposed approach in navigating various indoor environments with diverse floor plans and obstacles. In contrast to traditional navigation systems, our deep neural network-based approach is shown to provide faster and more accurate navigation performance, with a significant reduction in computational overhead. The portability and flexibility of our system make it an attractive solution for a wide range of applications, from personal robots to autonomous vehicles, where accurate and efficient indoor navigation is crucial.

title: Implementation and comparative quantitative assessment of different multispectral image pansharpening approches
Abstract: This study presents an in-depth quantitative evaluation of various multispectral image pansharpening techniques, with the objective of determining their effectiveness in improving spatial and spectral resolution while minimizing artifacts and distortions. The literature review identifies and categorizes prominent pansharpening approaches, including Component Substitution (CS),Principal Component Analysis (PCA), Brovey Transform, Edge-Preserving Smoothing (EPS), and the recently introduced methods such as Gaussian Mixture Model, Multi Resolution Filter (MRF) and Total Variance (TV) method. A systematic dataset selection procedure based on geographical diversity and sensor calibration ensures a comprehensive analysis of different conditions. Each method is assessed in relation to pansharpening metrics including error gradient, spectral entropy, root mean squared error, relative dimensionless global error in validation (rgdev) and visual interpretation. A comprehensive evaluation involving nine multispectral datasets demonstrated that pansharpening approaches significantly vary in performance, showing different strengths and weaknesses depending on the image data type, spatial and spectral resolution, and the specific metric used for evaluation. Additionally, results showed that several relatively new methods demonstrated top performance levels, revealing an improvement in the pansharpening field.

title: Sensory Polymorphism and Behavior: When Machine Vision Meets Monkey Eyes
Abstract: This study delves into the intersection of machine vision and primate behavior, specifically exploring the phenomenon of sensory polymorphism where different species of monkeys exhibit varying degrees of adaptation to their environments through distinct sensory capabilities. By utilizing a combination of machine learning algorithms and computer vision techniques, researchers have been able to quantify and analyze the responses of different monkey species to various visual stimuli, shedding light on the intricate relationship between sensory perception and behavioral outcomes. The study focuses on a comparative analysis of the rhesus macaque, savanna baboon, and chimpanzee, three widely studied species in the primate order, with the goal of identifying patterns and correlations between their sensory abilities and behaviors such as foraging, social interaction, and threat response. Through a series of behavioral experiments and machine vision assessments, the research reveals that these primates have evolved unique visual adaptations that enable them to effectively navigate their complex ecological niches, with significant implications for our understanding of sensory polymorphism and its impact on behavior. The findings of this study provide valuable insights into the evolution of sensory capabilities and their relationship to behavioral outcomes in primates, with potential applications in fields such as wildlife conservation and robotics.

title: Jointly Learning Non-negative Projection and Dictionary with Discriminative Graph Constraints for Classification
Abstract: Our work focuses on jointly learning the non-negative projection matrix and the dictionary with discriminative graph constraints for classification problems, offering an effective representation for images and high classification accuracy. Traditional dictionary learning methods, such as sparse representation, have been widely applied in image classifications. However, when noise and outliers coexist in the training data, their performances degrade. To address this limitation, we develop a novel model named joint non-negative matrix factorization with graph constraints, utilizing both local and global information of data. By representing data points as vertices and constructing adjacent matrices according to the similarity between vertices, our model integrates graph constraints into the proposed framework, capturing both spatial coherence and global structure of data. On the other hand, we introduce a sparse graph Laplacian regularization term to promote smoothness of data manifolds. An iterative optimization algorithm is consequently designed to minimize the proposed loss function and preserve dictionary learning sparsity. Extensive experimental results on benchmark datasets confirm the efficiency of the jointly learned model in improving classification accuracy. The results demonstrate that our model achieves superior performance when contrasted with the existing state-of-the-art approaches, exhibiting potential value for image recognition applications. Furthermore, the proposed method simplifies complex image features into a compact representation, preserving critical semantic content for subsequent learning stages.

title: DeepFool: a simple and accurate method to fool deep neural networks
Abstract: DeepFool is a notable adversarial attack algorithm designed to facilitate misclassification of deep neural networks by introducing intentionally crafted input perturbations. Initially proposed in 2015 by Sohieri Sanginipour and crew, the strategy focuses primarily on the concept of finding the least Fisher Information Number (Fisher Information) required to fool the neural network. The method constructs an arithmetic progression involving the correct classification of input space and misclassification prediction area concerning an attacked input space, thereby evaluating the perturbations involved through a least disruptive set of targeted labels. The efficacy and adaptability of DeepFool are demonstrated primarily by its iterative framework design that enables it, on one hand, to detect weak confidence neurons within the network with small activation values and, on the other, to boost its capacity for overcoming robust training via its novel distribution approach that induces perturbation on network samples prior to feeding these into training set. Recent studies evaluate the predictive power of DeepFool under strict adversarial conditions and discuss how the efficacy of its misclassification techniques make it an empowering algorithm in the competitive adversarial machine learning landscape.

title: Oracle performance for visual captioning
Abstract: This study investigates the impact of database configuration and system architecture on oracle performance for visual captioning applications. Visual captioning, which describes a model's ability to interpret images and generate text captions, requires a significant amount of computational resources and necessitates high-performance databases that can efficiently manage large volumes of data. Our analysis reveals that adapting the query performance threshold in Oracle Database enhances captioning accuracy for high-resolution images. In addition, the effect of join ordering on captioning speed is observed and reported in this paper. Notably, adopting the OPTT (Optimize Table) command in Oracle results in approximately 17% increased captioning throughput, without a corresponding negative effect on data integrity. Furthermore, an empirical investigation is conducted to estimate the optimal storage configuration required for efficient visual captioning data processing, indicating that using hybrid (local and flash) media for storing frequently accessed data boosts the overall captioning process by roughly 41%. These findings contribute to a deeper understanding of the key considerations for deploying high-performance visual captioning systems on Oracle-based architecture, with significant implications for real-world applications in the fields of computer vision and artificial intelligence. By providing system administrators with actionable recommendations to optimize visual captioning on Oracle databases, this research offers timely insights for businesses seeking to fully integrate AI-driven visual content analysis into their digital services and products.

title: Accurate Image Super-Resolution Using Very Deep Convolutional Networks
Abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to accurate image super-resolution using very deep convolutional networks. The proposed method leverages the power of deep learning to learned the intricate mappings between low-resolution input images and their high-resolution counterparts. By employing a very deep residual-in-residual dense network architecture, our method can effectively capture the intricate details and textures present in high-resolution images, even from low-resolution inputs. The residual-in-residual dense blocks allow for the efficient flow of information across different scales, leading to state-of-the-art results in terms of both perceptual and peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR) metrics. Furthermore, our method demonstrates exceptional robustness to various image degradations, including noise, compression artifacts, and variations in illumination conditions. We conduct an exhaustive experimentation on several benchmark datasets, including Set5, BSD500, and Waterloo Exploration Database, showcasing the superior performance of our approach over existing image super-resolution methods. The proposed technique has the potential to revolutionize various applications, such as image and video editing, medical imaging, and computer vision tasks, where high-resolution image reconstruction is crucial. Our results demonstrate that the integration of very deep convolutional networks and residual-in-residual dense blocks can lead to breakthroughs in image super-resolution tasks.

title: Learning Fine-grained Features via a CNN Tree for Large-scale Classification
Abstract: Deep learning models have made significant breakthroughs in large-scale classification tasks by learning complex patterns and features from massive datasets. However, the high-dimensional feature space often contains a multitude of redundant or irrelevant information, hindering the performance of the model. To alleviate this issue, we propose a novel fully convolutional network (CNN) tree framework, which leverages a hierarchical structure to progressively extract fine-grained features from the input data. The proposed approach starts by pre-training a series of shallow CNNs at different levels of abstraction, each capturing specific yet complementary aspects of the input data. These pre-trained networks are then federated together through a tree-like structure, allowing the model to recursively refine and specialize the feature representations. The CNN tree enables efficient propagation of contextual information between the different abstraction levels, effectively capturing fine-grained features that are critical for accurate classification. Our extensive experiments on several large-scale image classification benchmarks demonstrate the efficacy of the proposed approach, achieving state-of-the-art results and outperforming existing methods by a significant margin. Furthermore, the proposed model exhibits highly competitive inference speed and efficient use of computational resources, making it a desirable solution for large-scale image classification tasks.

title: Efficient Training of Very Deep Neural Networks for Supervised Hashing
Abstract: Supervised hashing has gained significant attention in recent years due to its ability to reduce the dimensionality of high-dimensional data while preserving the semantic information, resulting in efficient storage, feature extraction, and information retrieval. However, one of the major challenges in supervised hashing lies in training very deep neural networks, which requires a large amount of computational resources and time. To address this challenge, this paper proposes an efficient training framework for very deep neural networks in the context of supervised hashing. The proposed framework leverages a novel two-stage training approach, which combines the strengths of online learning and pre-training methods. In the first stage, a pre-trained deep neural network is used to initialize the weights of the network. The pre-training is performed using a large-scale dataset and a traditional loss function. In the second stage, the weights of the pre-trained network are fine-tuned using a semi-supervised hashing loss function and a newly designed online learning approach. The proposed framework benefits from the efficiency of pre-training and the accuracy of online learning, making it suitable for training very deep neural networks for supervised hashing tasks. Experimental results on several benchmark datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed framework in terms of both efficiency and accuracy.

title: Reversible Recursive Instance-level Object Segmentation
Abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to reversible recursive instance-level object segmentation, aiming to overcome the limitations of existing methods that suffer from mode collapse and a lack of interpretability. Our approach, dubbed RRRIS, utilizes a recursive mechanism to progressively refine the segmentation results while maintaining reversibility and allowing for instance-level information to be retained at each refinement stage. A key component of RRRIS is a context-aware flow-based neural network that is trained in a generative adversarial setup, enabling the model to generate high-quality, compact, and meaningful mask representations. Our evaluations on a range of challenging object segmentation benchmarks demonstrate the superior performance of RRRIS in terms of accuracy, efficiency, and interpretability. The reversible nature of RRRIS allows for the exploration of novel application scenarios, such as the recovery of partially occluded objects and the transfer of object-level knowledge between scenes. Furthermore, we empirically show that RRRIS facilitates better semantic understanding and context-aware instance separation, setting the stage for its deployment in a wide range of computer vision tasks.

title: Zero-Shot Learning via Joint Latent Similarity Embedding
Abstract: Zero-Shot Learning via Joint Latent Similarity Embedding is a novel approach that seeks to bridge the gap between known and unknown categories in the realm of machine learning. This paper proposes a joint latent similarity embedding (JLSE) framework that enables models to generalize beyond the confines of their training data, thereby tackling the zero-shot learning task with unprecedented precision. By leveraging the collective power of latent similarity and joint embedding, JLSE effectively extracts meaningful representations from the distributional and structural aspects of semantic spaces, allowing for a more comprehensive understanding of unseen classes. The utilization of multiple modalities, including text, vision, and audio, further enhances the robustness of the proposed model, thereby facilitating robust generalization to new, unseen data. Comprehensive evaluations conducted on a diverse array of benchmarking datasets reveal that JLSE outperforms traditional baselines by a considerable margin, demonstrating its capacity to effectively and efficiently handle the zero-shot learning paradigm. The joint latent similarity embedding framework exhibits exceptional promise in a plethora of applications, including multi-modal recognition, few-shot classification, and transfer learning, underscoring the monumental implications of its novel methodology.

title: Sequential Optimization for Efficient High-Quality Object Proposal Generation
Abstract: This work presents an advanced approach to efficiently generate high-quality object proposals in computer vision, focusing on sequential optimization strategies. Existing object proposal methods often rely on greedy or iterative optimization schemes, which can lead to suboptimal results due to local minima or limitations in exploring the search space. To overcome these challenges, we propose a novel sequential optimization framework that combines the strengths of multiple optimization techniques. By iteratively refining object proposals in a sequential manner, our approach can adapt to the complexity of the scene and effectively balance the trade-off between proposal quality and computational efficiency. Specifically, we introduce a hierarchical optimization strategy that progressively refines object proposals through spatial and channel-specific refinements, leveraging the power of attention mechanisms and spatial transformers. The proposed framework is demonstrated to outperform state-of-the-art object proposal methods on several benchmarks, including PASCAL VOC and COCO, while achieving significant reductions in computational runtime. Our results underscore the potential of sequential optimization for high-quality object proposal generation and pave the way for further research in this area. By bridging the gap between proposal quality and efficiency, our approach has the potential to benefit various computer vision applications, including object detection, tracking, and image segmentation.

title: Semantic Object Parsing with Local-Global Long Short-Term Memory
Abstract: Semantic Object Parsing with Local-Global Long Short-Term Memory is a novel approach to image understanding, which synergizes the benefits of local and global contextual information. Traditional object parsing methods often rely on a single scale or neighborhood to understand the object's structure, but this limitation hampers their ability to capture complex spatial relationships between objects. To address this, our proposed model employs a Local-Global Long Short-Term Memory (LG-LSTM) architecture, where a local LSTM cell processes spatial arrangements at the pixel level and a global LSTM cell captures long-range contextual dependencies across the entire image. By integrating these two components, our LG-LSTM model enables the simultaneous learning of local and global features, allowing for more accurate and detailed object parsing results. Experimental results on several benchmarks, including PASCAL-Context and Sbd, demonstrate the superior performance of our LG-LSTM model in comparison to state-of-the-art methods. The model's ability to balance local and global context contributes to its strong representation of object structures and its resilience to noisy or occluded regions. Furthermore, our LG-LSTM model can be easily integrated with existing object detection and segmentation pipelines, making it a versatile and valuable addition to any image understanding framework.

title: Deeply-Recursive Convolutional Network for Image Super-Resolution
Abstract: The rapid advancement of image acquisition technologies has led to a significant increase in low-resolution image data, which hinders various applications in fields such as computer vision, surveillance, and medical imaging. Image super-resolution (SR) is a technique that aims to reconstruct a high-resolution (HR) image from a given low-resolution (LR) image, thereby improving visual quality and facilitating further processing tasks. However, traditional SR methods often rely on hand-crafted features or shallow models, which limit their ability to capture complex image structures and intricate details. To address this issue, this paper proposes a novel Deeply-Recursive Convolutional Network (DRCN) for image SR, which utilizes a recursive architecture to exploit rich contextual information and iteratively refine the SR estimate. By incorporating an auxiliary prediction module and a residual learning framework, the DRCN effectively learns both local and global dependencies within the input LR image, thereby achieving state-of-the-art performance. Experimental results on benchmark datasets indicate that the proposed DRCN significantly outperforms contemporary SR methods in terms of peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR) and structural similarity index (SSIM), validating its potential as a robust and efficient tool for image SR applications. The proposed approach demonstrates improved flexibility and expressiveness, enabling simultaneous optimization of multiple levels of LR image representation and detailed reconstruction of spatially correlated patterns and textures.

title: Solving Jigsaw Puzzles with Linear Programming
Abstract: Jigsaw puzzles pose a unique problem in the realm of optimization due to their tile-based structure and constraints. The objective of solving a jigsaw puzzle lies in arranging the tiles in a manner such that they form a complete image. Despite the apparent complexity of the jigsaw puzzle structure, one key insight in this pursuit is to formulate the puzzle-solving process through the framework of linear programming. This article demonstrates a novel application of linear programming for solving jigsaw puzzles. A mathematical model is developed detailing the structure of the jigsaw puzzle and defining valid puzzle configurations in the context of the constraints imposed by the physical properties of the tiles and the targeted puzzle image. This formulation affords the possibility of formulating a linear programming problem whose solution space encompasses all feasible puzzle assemblies that satisfy the puzzle constraints. Utilizing this linear programming framework enables the formulation of an optimization problem that seeks to minimize the distance between the puzzle configuration predicted by the model and its idealized counterpart. This formulation achieves a significant reduction in computational complexity and time required for puzzle solving compared to brute-force approaches to jigsaw puzzle assembly. The efficacy of this proposed optimization framework will be validated through computational experiments for a range of jigsaw puzzles varying in the level of difficulty.

title: Transductive Zero-Shot Action Recognition by Word-Vector Embedding
Abstract: This study propels the development of transductive zero-shot action recognition by introducing a novel method that leverages word-vector embeddings to bridge the semantic gap between seen and unseen action classes. Existing research on zero-shot learning primarily focuses on establishing relationships between action classes and word embeddings through meta-learning or multi-label learning techniques. However, these approaches are limited by their reliance on pre-trained word embeddings, which may not effectively capture the nuances of action semantics. To address this limitation, this research presents a word-vector embedding-based framework that learns to explicitly represent the semantics of action classes through graph-based embedding and transductive reasoning. The proposed framework is able to learn discriminative and generalizable features for zero-shot action recognition by harnessing the power of word-vector embeddings. Comprehensive experiments on multiple benchmark datasets reveal that the proposed method yields exceptional performance, achieving state-of-the-art scores on multiple metrics. By demonstrating the efficacy of word-vector embeddings in transductive zero-shot action recognition, this research contributes to advancing the boundaries of action recognition research, enabling the development of more robust and flexible action recognition systems that can generalize to unseen action classes with minimal supervision.

title: Robust Face Alignment Using a Mixture of Invariant Experts
Abstract: In the intricate realm of facial recognition and analysis, robust face alignment remains a pivotal yet challenging task due to factors such as varying face orientations, expressions, lighting conditions, and occlusions. The proposed approach, referred to as a Mixture of Invariant Experts (MIE), seeks to address these complexities by combining the strengths of multiple expert networks each specializing in different aspects of invariance. The MIE architecture is comprised of a disparate ensemble of expert networks, including convolutional neural networks (CNNs) and spatial transformers, each focusing on specific facets of face alignment, such as rotation invariance, scale invariance, and expression invariance. The experts operate collaboratively to accurately estimate facial landmarks across diverse scenarios, with each expert compensating for the limitations of the others. To evaluate the efficacy of the proposed MIE approach, extensive experiments have been conducted on an array of benchmark datasets, including but not limited to the 300-W, FFHNQ, and Celeb-A datasets. The outcomes demonstrate the MIE's exceptional performance in face alignment, boasting robustness against various adversarial conditions, as well as precise landmark localization and improved generalizability across heterogeneous populations. The results underscore the MIE's potential as a versatile and adaptable solution for real-world facial analysis applications, including but not limited to, pose estimation, facial expression recognition, and tracking, thus setting a new benchmark for the field.

title: Symbol Grounding Association in Multimodal Sequences with Missing Elements
Abstract: This study delves into the problem of symbol grounding in multimodal sequences where elements are absent, a particularly challenging scenario in multimodal understanding. The association between symbols and their grounded representations is the core task of multimodal signal understanding. However, when elements are missing, symbolic representation loses its direct connection to the original data, resulting in a disconnection between the symbol and its grounded representation. The absence of elements challenges the ability to accurately associate symbols with their meanings. This is exemplified in tasks such as image-based activities where the absence of a crucial visual context can deviate the interpretation to a different meaning and subsequent actions may also vary accordingly. To understand this complex scenario, this research proposes a novel approach that combines the power of two existing theories: Masked Sequence Modeling and Hybrid Cross-Modal Learning. The proposed framework, dubbed as Symbol Grounding Associative Task (SGAT) for multimodal sequences with missing elements, is designed to restore the correct symbolic representation even in the presence of missing elements. The experimental outcomes demonstrate the efficacy of the proposed framework in imputing missing elements with appropriate symbolic meanings, thus correcting the association between symbols and their grounded representations.

title: Similarity-based Text Recognition by Deeply Supervised Siamese Network
Abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to text recognition by utilizing a deeply supervised Siamese network for similarity-based matching. The proposed method, referred to as SimText, leverages the prowess of deep learning in capturing intricate patterns in visual data to recognize texts in various settings, including handwritten and typed scripts, with diverse fonts and languages. By establishing an Siamese network comprising two identical encoder branches with shared weights, our approach effectively learns a similarity metric that enables the accurate pairing of query and template text instances. Through the incorporation of a deeply supervised loss function, the network is incentivized to produce robust and distinctive feature representations, thus mitigating the effects of variability in text appearance and enhancing overall recognition performance. Comprehensive experiments conducted on multiple benchmark datasets demonstrate the efficacy of SimText in achieving state-of-the-art results, particularly under challenging conditions involving font style, size, and language variations. Additionally, the simplicity and computational efficiency of the proposed architecture make it a versatile and practical solution for a broad range of text recognition applications, including but not limited to, optical character recognition, handwritten text analysis, and augmented reality-based content recognition. Overall, the proposed SimText framework offers a robust and generalizable approach to text recognition that can be readily adapted to various real-world scenarios.

title: Deep Reflectance Maps
Abstract: Deep reflectance maps have emerged as a powerful tool in the field of computer vision and graphics, enabling the capture and representation of highly detailed and realistic material properties of objects. By computing the reflectance of materials under various lighting conditions, deep reflectance maps (DRMs) provide a more accurate and nuanced understanding of material appearance, rivaling that of human perception. This technique has far-reaching implications for various applications, including video game development, virtual reality, and digital cinematography. A DRM is essentially a spherical harmonic (SH) encoding of material reflectance, which allows for the efficient and accurate representation of complex material properties. The main advantage of DRMs lies in their ability to store material properties in a compact and scene-agnostic format, facilitating their use in a wide range of scenarios. Recent advancements in deep learning and computational techniques have made it possible to generate, parameterize, and render DRMs in real-time. This has opened up new avenues for applications such as film and animation production, architecture, and product design, where creating high-fidelity material appearances and lighting effects is critical. As such, DRMs have the potential to become a staple in the realm of computer graphics and vision research, pushing the boundaries of realism in digital content and further increasing the value of digital media in our lives.

title: Learning Dense Convolutional Embeddings for Semantic Segmentation
Abstract: Deep learning models, particularly convolutional neural networks (CNNs), have demonstrated significant improvements in semantic segmentation tasks. However, standard CNNs often require large computation powers, enormous memory storage, and intensive training times due to their spatial-spectral hierarchical representations. With the growing need for real-world semantic segmentation applications, there is an urgent need to develop lightweight and efficient CNN architectures that can effectively capture the image contextual information. In recent years, dense convolutional embeddings (DCEs) have been introduced as a novel effective way to capture multi-resolution and hierarchical representations of visual features in deep learning models. This research employs DCEs to create a more tractable, efficient, and scalable semantic segmentation framework. We propose a hierarchical architecture that incorporates DCEs in parallel branches to boost the feature representation capabilities of deep networks, while achieving better computational efficiency. The proposed method is systematically evaluated on several benchmark datasets to showcase its effectiveness and efficiency in various real-world scenarios. Specifically, we compare our model with state-of-the-art techniques using metrics such as accuracy, mean intersection-over-union (mIoU), accuracy rate, precision, recall, and average precision. Our experimental results demonstrate that the proposed approach significantly improves upon existing state-of-the-art semantic segmentation methods in terms of accuracy and computational efficiency.

title: Standard methods for inexpensive pollen loads authentication by means of computer vision and machine learning
Abstract: This research proposes a novel, low-cost approach to authenticate pollen loads using a combination of computer vision and machine learning. Traditionally, pollen load authentication has been a labor-intensive and costly process, relying on manual identification and verification methods. To address this challenge, a standardized methodology is developed, integrating computer vision techniques and machine learning algorithms to accurately classify pollen loads. The proposed system employs a convolutional neural network (CNN) to automatically detect and identify pollen grains within an image, while a multi-layer perceptron (MLP) is used to classify the detected grains into predefined categories. To ensure authenticity, a robust feature extraction method is employed to extract relevant morphometric features from the pollen grains, such as shape, size, and texture. These features are then used to train a classifier, which is validated using a dataset comprising authentic and inauthentic pollen loads. The study demonstrates the effectiveness of the proposed system, achieving an accuracy rate of 95% in accurately authenticating pollen loads. This innovative approach has significant implications for the field of forensic botany, enabling the rapid and cost-effective authentication of pollen loads in forensic investigations, as well as in the agri-food and pharmaceutical industries.

title: Learning to Assign Orientations to Feature Points
Abstract: This research focuses on advancing the state-of-the-art in feature point orientation estimation for improved computer vision applications such as odometry, SLAM, and 3D reconstruction. The ability to assign orientations to feature points, also known as depth-aware feature points, is a crucial step in many tasks where accurate mapping of real-world scenes is required. Traditional methods often rely on pre-defined models or indirect approaches, which can lead to suboptimal results in scenarios with diverse structural elements and varying ground truth information. To address these limitations, we propose a novel approach that learns to predict orientations of feature points through an end-to-end trainable framework. The method takes advantages of a combination of spatial and structural contextual information, captured via convolutional neural networks and graph-based architectures, to infer feature point orientations from multi-modal input sources, such as RGB images, 3D point clouds, or satellite images. Our proposed approach is validated through a series of experiments on real-world datasets, which demonstrate significant improvements in terms of depth estimation accuracy, feature point orientation estimation, and scene reconstructions over the state-of-the-art methods. Furthermore, the experimental analysis also show that the method allows for effective and robust handling of challenging scenarios, including varying levels of illumination, occlusions, and structural complexities.

title: Volume-based Semantic Labeling with Signed Distance Functions
Abstract: Volume-based semantic labeling with signed distance functions has gained significant attention in the field of computer vision, particularly in the context of 3D image segmentation and object recognition. This approach leverages the signed distance function (SDF) to encode the geometry of 3D shapes and infer semantic labels by exploiting the geometric relations between objects. By mapping each point in the 3D space to a signed distance value, SDF-based methods can effectively distinguish between object boundaries, attributes, and their correlations. In volume-based semantic labeling, SDFs are employed to segment and label objects within predefined 3D volumes or scenes, thereby providing a richer understanding of their internal and external structures. Traditional SDF-based methods focus on a single signed distance value per point, whereas recent advancements have explored more sophisticated representations, including multi-channel and Gaussian SDFs, to capture varying degrees of details and contextual relationships. The integration of SDFs with convolutional neural networks (CNNs) enables the discovery of hierarchical features and object representations, directly informing the assignment of semantic labels to the corresponding points. Furthermore, the SDF-based framework is particularly well-suited for multi-task learning and transfer learning, where its robust geometric representations can facilitate the generalization of learned patterns across diverse scenes and objects. Through thorough evaluation and comparisons with state-of-the-art methods, this research will demonstrate the potential and efficiency of SDF-based volume-based semantic labeling for 3D image segmentation and object recognition applications.

title: An Adaptive Data Representation for Robust Point-Set Registration and Merging
Abstract: This work presents an adaptive data representation approach for robust point-set registration and merging in the context of 3D shape analysis and computer vision applications. The proposed framework combines the principles of manifold learning with a probabilistic registration method to effectively model complex shape geometries and variations. The key innovation lies in the development of a novel feature descriptor based on a continuous atlas of local coordinate systems, which enables a robust and flexible representation of point-set topologies. This descriptor is then exploited within a registration pipeline, where it facilitates the accurate alignment of point-sets across varying scales and pose differences. To further enhance the robustness of the registration process, a probabilistic merging technique is introduced, which leverages the learned feature descriptors to establish consistent correspondences across multiple point-sets. The effectiveness of the proposed approach is extensively evaluated on a variety of benchmark datasets, including synthetic and real-world scenarios, and demonstrates significant improvements in registration accuracy and efficiency over existing state-of-the-art methods. Overall, the developed adaptive data representation scheme offers a powerful and versatile framework for point-set registration and merging applications in 3D computer vision and shape analysis fields.

title: Spatial frequency processing in the central and peripheral visual field during scene viewing
Abstract: Spatial frequency processing plays a critical role in visual perception, enabling individuals to efficiently encode and interpret complex visual information. This study examines the contribution of spatial frequency processing in the central and peripheral visual field during scene viewing, with a specific focus on its relationship to visual attention and semantic processing. Employing a combination of behavioral and neuroimaging techniques, including eye tracking and functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI), we investigated how spatial frequency processing is modulated by visual attention and scene context. Our results demonstrate that the distribution of spatial frequency processing across the visual field is highly dynamic and is influenced by both visual attentional processes and scene context. In particular, our findings suggest that the central visual field is more sensitive to higher spatial frequencies and is involved in object recognition and semantic processing, while the peripheral visual field is more sensitive to lower spatial frequencies and is involved in spatial context and background segregation. Furthermore, we observed a notable distinction between the neural correlates of spatial frequency processing in the central and peripheral visual fields, with the superior parietal lobule being more active for higher spatial frequencies and the lateral occipital complex being more active for lower spatial frequencies. These findings have implications for our understanding of the neural basis of visual perception and scene understanding, highlighting the importance of spatial frequency processing in the allocation of visual attention and semantic processing.

title: Structure Inference Machines: Recurrent Neural Networks for Analyzing Relations in Group Activity Recognition
Abstract: This abstract discusses the use of Structure Inference Machines (SIMs) in conjunction with Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs) to improve group activity recognition systems. The ability to effectively analyze and infer the relationships between individuals during group activities is crucial for applications such as human-computer interaction, gesture recognition, and autonomous robots. Traditional methods for group activity recognition often rely on pre-defined rules and manually annotated datasets, which can limit their adaptability and scalability. In contrast, the proposed approach utilizes a combination of SIMs and RNNs to capture the inherent structure of group activities from observation data. The SIMs are specifically designed to infer the relations and hierarchies within the group, while the RNNs learn to map these structure representations into a coherent and meaningful activity representation. The resulting system can generate robust and interpretable activity features that capture both the temporal and spatial dynamics of group activities. A series of experiments is conducted to demonstrate the effectiveness and efficiency of the proposed approach in various group activity recognition tasks, showing significant performance improvement over state-of-the-art methods. Overall, the use of SIMs and RNNs provides a novel and promising direction for group activity recognition research, with potential applications in numerous fields including autonomous systems, human-computer interaction, and machine learning.

title: DISC: Deep Image Saliency Computing via Progressive Representation Learning
Abstract: This research paper delves into the realm of deep image saliency computing, proposing a novel framework for effectively capturing and localizing visually notable points in images. The proposed method, termed Deep Image Saliency Computing via Progressive Representation Learning (DISC), pioneers an unconventional representation learning approach that enables the network to iteratively focus on novel and distinctive features in the image. Unlike conventional saliency methods that primarily rely on hand-crafted features or static region-based models, DISC harnesses the power of progressive learning to progressively refine the image representation, guiding the network to uncover not only strongly activated but also weakly activated regions often overlooked by static models. The proposed DISC framework achieves this by incorporating a progressive spatial-attention structure, which encourages the model to dissect and focus on heterogeneous elements within the image, resulting in higher precision and recall in detecting salient objects. The approach has been extensively evaluated on standard saliency benchmark datasets (DUTS, ECSSD, PASCAL-S, and HKU-IS), yields state-of-the-art results (reducing average boundary error rates by up to 17.8%), and demonstrates substantial effectiveness in a variety of applications, such as object detection, image segmentation, and visual storytelling, while introducing a fundamental shift in the field of deep image saliency computing. The findings of this research signify significant contributions to the imaging community and highlight the potential of progressive representation learning in unlocking hidden image features and elevating the overall efficacy of computer vision systems.

title: Sequence to Sequence Learning for Optical Character Recognition
Abstract: This paper explores the application of Sequence to Sequence (Seq2Seq) learning for Optical Character Recognition (OCR), a crucial task in natural language processing and computer vision. Traditional approaches to OCR-based Seq2Seq learning involve the use of Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks with attention mechanisms to map input images to sequences of characters. However, these methods often suffer from limitations such as difficulties in training large-scale models due to vanishing gradients and lack of robustness to variability in font styles and sizes. This research aims to address these limitations by incorporating a novel, hierarchical architecture that incorporates both coarse and fine-grained features from input images. Furthermore, this study extends the capabilities of Seq2Seq learning in OCR by introducing a new, globally conditioned network that leverages pre-trained language models to enable more accurate and context-aware predictions. Utilizing a combination of convolutional and recurrent layers, this architecture demonstrates state-of-the-art performance on multiple benchmark datasets, including the SVC and IAM Handwriting databases. By providing a more efficient and effective framework for sequence-to-sequence learning, this research presents significant advancements in the area of OCR and has the potential to be applied to a range of real-world applications, including document processing and sentiment analysis.

title: Unsupervised Learning of Edges
Abstract: This work delves into the realm of unsupervised edge learning, a distinct departure from the typical supervised and self-supervised methods employed by current deep learning architectures. Our investigation focuses on devising a novel edge detection mechanism capable of thriving in the absence of explicit edge annotations. This is achieved through a two-stage architecture comprising a discriminator and a generator, which work hand-in-hand to produce a feature map representing the image's edge information. The discriminator serves as a critic, scrutinizing the outputs generated by the generator and learning to identify high-quality edges that are both realistic and relevant. On the other hand, the generator leverages the learned edge features from the discriminator to refine its output, thereby facilitating an iterative improvement process. We show that this synergy between the two stages allows for a robust and efficacious edge detection system that not only outperforms existing state-of-the-art methods in terms of accuracy but also boasts enhanced interpretability and knowledge transferability. Through a series of experiments on benchmark datasets, such as BSDS500 and Edges2shoes, we demonstrate the merits of this novel edge learning approach in diverse applications, including object segmentation, image inpainting, and visual object tracking. The proposed method's adaptability, scalability, and edge locality make it suitable for applications requiring high-quality edge detection, including medical imaging, autonomous driving, and robotics. This is demonstrated through a series of experiments and cases studies on these applications.

title: Natural Language Object Retrieval
Abstract:
Abstract:
Natural Language Object Retrieval (NOR) emerges as an interdisciplinary research area, integrating computer vision, natural language processing, and machine learning to retrieve and manipulate objects in a dynamic, real-world environment. This paper delves into the recent advancements in NOR, focusing on the convergence of deep learning models, multimodal fusion, and attention mechanisms, enabling the system to accurately identify objects through descriptive natural language queries. By leveraging the strength of object detection and image captioning algorithms, the NOR system has the potential to revolutionize various applications, including smart homes, retail settings, and industrial manufacturing, where object retrieval plays a pivotal role in improving productivity and efficiency. Specifically, this research explores the challenges of domain adaptation, visual grounding, and semantic understanding in NOR, demonstrating the efficacy of a proposed multimodal fusion framework that combines state-of-the-art architectures for image and language processing. The experimental results show significant improvements in retrieval accuracy and efficiency, validating the potential of NOR to transform the way we interact with physical objects in our daily lives. The outcomes of this study contribute to the continued development of intelligent object retrieval systems, emphasizing the importance of cross-disciplinary collaborations to tackle the complexities of visual and linguistic understanding.

title: Adaptive Affinity Matrix for Unsupervised Metric Learning
Abstract: The proposed Adaptive Affinity Matrix (AAM) is a novel framework for unsupervised metric learning that leverages the dynamic adjustment of affinity matrix representations to capture non-linear inter-sample relationships. Conventional affinity matrix learning methods often rely on handcrafted features and hardcoded metrics to define the affinity between data samples, limiting their ability to adapt to complex data distributions. In contrast, AAM learns a multiple-latent dimension affinity matrix, where the affinity between samples is learned through an automated exploration of the data manifold via neural networks. This adaptive approach seeks to alleviate issues such as the curse of dimensionality and the brittleness of conventional affinity matrix learning methods to noisy or irrelevant features. AAM tackles these challenges by employing a multi-task learning architecture, where multiple features and metrics are simultaneously learned to define the affinity matrix representation, thereby fostering a discriminative embedding that emphasizes key inter-sample relationships. Through extensive experimental evaluations on diverse benchmark datasets, AAM demonstrates improved performance and robustness compared to existing unsupervised metric learning methods, showcasing its potential for real-world applications such as image and video retrieval, clustering, and anomaly detection. The adaptability and versatility of AAM further underscores its potential to be integrated into various domains requiring flexible and data-driven affinity matrix learning.

title: Deep Mean Maps
Abstract: Deep mean maps represent a novel framework for modeling and analyzing spatial-temporal data, which has garnered significant attention in recent years. By introducing a spatial mean map layer to deepen convolutional neural networks, deep mean maps effectively capture regional features and relationships within images, thereby enabling accurate spatial information extraction. This research focuses on exploring the potential applications and enhanced capabilities of deep mean maps in remote sensing and computer vision tasks. A detailed investigation into the formulation and construction of deep mean maps, including their theoretical underpinnings and implementation, is presented. Experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of deep mean maps in tasks such as image classification, object detection, and change detection. The performance gains achieved through the incorporation of deep mean maps are demonstrated to be significant, highlighting the utility of this framework in overcoming existing limitations associated with traditional convolutional neural networks. Furthermore, the use of deep mean maps is shown to significantly enhance deep learning models' capacity for spatial feature interaction and contextual awareness. The proposed approach is also evaluated in various real-world scenarios, including multispectral and RGB datasets, showcasing the versatility and adaptability of deep mean maps in diverse applications. Overall, this research aims to provide a comprehensive understanding of deep mean maps, their theoretical foundation, and their practical implications for the advancement of deep learning techniques in spatial-temporal data analysis.

title: UA-DETRAC: A New Benchmark and Protocol for Multi-Object Detection and Tracking
Abstract: This research paper examines the development and establishment of Universal Anomaly Detection in a real-world setting for an Embedded Real-time Automatic Crash detection and Tracking (UA-DETRAC) benchmark and protocol for multi-object detection and tracking. The increasing number of accidents and casualties on streets calls for the creation of more sophisticated and reliable automatic surveillance systems. The primary objective of this research is to update and propose techniques that will make multi-object tracking more efficient and less prone to errors. In order to minimize variance among various automatic surveillance systems, the UA-DETRAC benchmark establishes a consistent protocol that may be employed across various viewpoints. The protocol is specified based on real-world incident scenarios, with a focus on various forms of vehicles, pedestrians, and other obstructions that can occur on roads. The novelty of the UA-DETRAC benchmark and protocol will enable developers, researchers, and producers to produce and implement unbiased solutions that are more effective in real-world traffic surveillance applications. It also enables real-world testing setups to be easily replicated and the performance of various automatic surveillance systems to be compared on the same grounds, in order to find the most precise and least error-prone system.

title: Action Recognition using Visual Attention
Abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to action recognition using visual attention, which enables computers to focus on the most relevant parts of a scene and accurately classify actions. Current action recognition methods often rely on convolutional neural networks (CNNs) that process the entire input image, which can lead to poor performance due to the presence of irrelevant background information. To mitigate this issue, we introduce a multi-modal architecture that combines spatial and channel attention mechanisms to selectively focus on the key regions and features of the image. The spatial attention module generates a heat map that highlights the importance of different regions in the image, while the channel attention module weighs the importance of different feature maps. Our proposed method can effectively discard redundant information and capture the essential features, leading to significant improvements in action recognition accuracy. Experimental results on several benchmarks, including UCF-101, HMDB-51, and ActivityNet, demonstrate the efficacy of our proposed approach, achieving state-of-the-art performance in various action recognition tasks. Moreover, our method can be efficiently deployed in real-world applications, such as surveillance systems and human-computer interaction, where accurate action recognition is crucial. Overall, this work presents a comprehensive framework for visual attention-based action recognition, showcasing the potential of integrating attention mechanisms with deep learning architectures for improved performance and efficiency.

title: Going Deeper in Facial Expression Recognition using Deep Neural Networks
Abstract: Advances in technology have led to the widespread use of facial expression recognition in various fields such as human-computer interaction, security, and emotion analysis. However, the traditional methods used for facial expression recognition often face challenges in handling complex and diverse facial expressions. This is where deep neural networks (DNNs) come into play, with their ability to automatically learn and improve their performance on such tasks. This study delves deeper into the use of DNNs for facial expression recognition, examining various architectures and techniques that have been employed in recent years to address the complexities of human emotions. A comprehensive review of the literature is conducted to identify the strengths and limitations of different DNN-based approaches, including convolutional neural networks (CNNs), recurrent neural networks (RNNs), and transfer learning. Additionally, the study explores the use of pre-trained models, data augmentation techniques, and attention mechanisms to improve the performance of facial expression recognition systems. The results of this study demonstrate the effectiveness of DNNs in recognizing facial expressions, and provide insights into the potential applications of facial expression recognition in areas such as affective computing, sentiment analysis, and social robotics. Overall, this research contributes to the advancement of facial expression recognition technology, and highlights the potential of DNNs in unlocking the mysteries of human emotions.

title: Basic Level Categorization Facilitates Visual Object Recognition
Abstract: The human brain's ability to recognize objects from a single glance is a complex process that has been extensively studied in the field of visual object recognition. Recent research has suggested that the automatic activation of basic level categories plays a crucial role in facilitating this process. This abstract discusses the concept of basic level categorization, its significance in object recognition, and the potential neural mechanisms underlying this phenomenon. By definition, basic level categories refer to the highest level of abstraction that groups objects with distinct shared features. In this context, categorizing objects at the basic level enables the activation of a rich network of semantic associations, facilitating quicker recognition of objects. Using event-related potentials (ERPs) and functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI), researchers have found that categories at the basic level exhibit more widespread activation in conceptual networks compared to more subordinate or superordinate categories. Furthermore, studies have demonstrated that the speed of object recognition is faster when objects are categorized at the basic level, as compared to when more specific or abstract categories are used. The neural basis for this phenomenon is thought to involve the coordinated activity of category-selective areas in the ventral visual pathway, as well as the modulation of top-down attention by higher-level conceptual networks. Overall, our understanding of basic level categorization and its role in facilitating visual object recognition highlights the importance of considering the inherent category structure of objects when studying visual perception.

title: Deep Gaussian Conditional Random Field Network: A Model-based Deep Network for Discriminative Denoising
Abstract: This paper proposes a novel deep architecture known as the Deep Gaussian Conditional Random Field Network (DGCRFN) for discriminative denoising. Building upon the strengths of Gaussian Conditional Random Fields (CRFs), which have been shown to be effective in modeling dependencies between observations, and deep neural networks, DGCRFN incorporates a CRF-based decision layer to enhance the denoising performance of deep networks. The proposed model learns to filter out noise in images while preserving their underlying structures by characterizing the noise distribution as a Gaussian mixture and modeling the dependencies between neighboring pixels within a localized region through CRFs. A backpropagation-based optimization method is developed to efficiently train DGCRFN using noisy images as training data. When evaluated against state-of-the-art denoising methods on various benchmark datasets, DGCRFN consistently yields superior results, reporting significant improvements in terms of peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR) and structural similarity index (SSIM). These results demonstrate the effectiveness of DGCRFN in removing noise while accurately preserving the original image structures, signifying its potential as a robust and efficient tool for various image processing tasks, including denoising, debluring, and super-resolution. Furthermore, the learnable CRF component allows for flexibility in incorporating various prior knowledge about image structures and noise distributions, enabling DGCRFN to adapt to diverse scenarios and emerging applications in computer vision and image analysis.

title: Efficient non-greedy optimization of decision trees
Abstract: This research paper presents an efficient non-greedy optimization approach for decision trees, which aims to improve the accuracy and generalizability of classification models while diminishing the risk of overfitting. Traditional non-greedy optimization methods tend to be computationally expensive and time-consuming, often resulting in impaired model performance due to their brute-force nature. To address these limitations, we develop a novel non-greedy optimization algorithm that leverages a balanced exploration-exploitation framework to navigate the vast decision tree search space. This novel approach, dubbed as Efficient Non-greedy Tree Pruning (ENTP), exploits a mixture of exploration and exploitation by iteratively applying node selection and edge addition strategies. Furthermore, ENTP incorporates an adaptive pruning mechanism to dynamically adjust the tree structure according to the training data, thereby mitigating overfitting concerns. Experimental results on several benchmark datasets demonstrate the efficacy of ENTP, which delivers state-of-the-art performance while significantly reducing computational costs when compared to existing non-greedy optimization techniques. Additionally, the proposed algorithm is robust and scalable, making it an attractive solution for large-scale decision tree construction tasks in various machine learning applications.

title: Newtonian Image Understanding: Unfolding the Dynamics of Objects in Static Images
Abstract:
Abstract: 
Newtonian image understanding represents a groundbreaking approach to deciphering the dynamics of objects within static images by leveraging the fundamental principles of Newtonian physics, specifically gravity, inertia, and motion. This novel framework seeks to bridge the gap between computer vision and physics by introducing a structured methodology for accurately predicting object behaviors and movements from static images. Utilizing insights from Newtonian dynamics, researchers can infer subtle cues about an object's mass, velocity, acceleration, and orientation, thereby unlocking the secrets of seemingly stationary images. By translating the laws of motion into an image-understanding paradigm, Newtonian image understanding paves the way for advancements in fields such as surveillance, robotics, action recognition, and object manipulation. Furthermore, this research has far-reaching implications for artificial intelligence, where the incorporation of physical reasoning can significantly enhance the accuracy and autonomy of AI-driven systems. As a pioneering contribution to the intersection of computer vision and physics, this work promises to revolutionize the way we analyze and comprehend visual data, opening new avenues for interdisciplinary research and innovation.

title: Facial Landmark Detection with Tweaked Convolutional Neural Networks
Abstract: Deep learning techniques have significantly improved facial landmark detection in recent years, enabling applications in various fields such as computer vision, biometrics, and human-computer interaction. However, traditional facial landmark detection models have limitations in terms of accuracy and robustness when dealing with diverse facial poses, expressions, and occlusions. In this paper, we present a method for enhanced facial landmark detection using tweaked convolutional neural networks. Our approach combines the benefits of convolutional neural networks (CNNs) with innovative tweaks to improve facial landmark detection accuracy and robustness. Specifically, we incorporate a novel data augmentation technique to generate diverse facial images with varied poses, expressions, and lighting conditions, thereby increasing the model's ability to generalize across different scenarios. Additionally, we introduce a spatial regularization mechanism to refine the predicted facial landmarks and reduce errors. Furthermore, we propose a patch-wise training strategy to handle occlusions and partial facial visibility. Our experimental results demonstrate that our tweaked CNN architecture consistently outperforms state-of-the-art methods on benchmark datasets, achieving higher accuracy and robustness in challenging facial landmark detection scenarios.

title: Multimodal Skip-gram Using Convolutional Pseudowords
Abstract: This paper proposes Multimodal Skip-gram Using Convolutional Pseudowords (MSP), a novel approach that combines the strengths of multimodal learning and word embeddings to model complex semantic relationships between words and their corresponding visual and acoustic representations. MSP leverages convolutional neural networks (CNNs) to learn pseudowords, which are not actual words but groups of visual and acoustic symbols that are analogous to words, and leverages these representations to learn Skip-gram embeddings. In contrast to traditional Skip-gram models that rely on word pairs and their co-occurrences in text data only, MSP exploits cross-modal relationships between text, images, and audio to improve the quality and robustness of the generated word embeddings. Our approach incorporates multiple modalities via visual and acoustic features extracted from images and audio, respectively, allowing the MSP model to capture rich contextual information that would be unattainable with text data alone. Through extensive experiments on several benchmark datasets, including static images, dynamic videos, and spoken audio, we demonstrate the significant advantages of MSP over state-of-the-art Skip-gram models in capturing nuanced semantic relationships and improving model robustness and generalizability to unseen data. Our results show that the proposed MSP approach can achieve better performance in various downstream tasks, including image classification, text classification, and audio classification, making it a valuable addition to the toolkit of multimodal researchers and practitioners.

title: Human Curation and Convnets: Powering Item-to-Item Recommendations on Pinterest
Abstract: Human curation and Convolutional Neural Networks (ConvNets) have been increasingly integrated to power personalized item-to-item recommendations on Pinterest. Traditional collaborative filtering methods have limitations in handling cold start and scalability issues, and deep learning-based approaches often struggle with interpretability. This research proposes a novel framework that synergizes human curation and ConvNet architectures to address these challenges. By leveraging user-generated metadata and expert-annotated attributes, the framework enables the model to learn rich representations of user preferences and item characteristics. The ConvNet architecture, comprising a sequence of convolutional and pooling layers, extracts features that capture the intricate relationships between visual and textual attributes of items. The model is trained on a large-scale Pinterest dataset and evaluated on a series of metrics, including precision, recall, and F1-score. The results demonstrate that the proposed framework outperforms state-of-the-art methods in terms of prediction accuracy and model interpretability. Empirical analyses reveal that the incorporation of human curation data and expert annotations significantly boosts the model's performance and robustness to sparsity and cold start scenarios. By striking a balance between human knowledge and artificial intelligence, this research aims to develop a more effective and explainable item-to-item recommendation system on Pinterest. The findings of this study have significant implications for the development of more personalized and effective recommendation systems in social media platforms.

title: LLNet: A Deep Autoencoder Approach to Natural Low-light Image Enhancement
Abstract: This paper proposes a novel deep autoencoder architecture, dubbed LLNet, for enhancing low-light images captured under natural scenes. The primary challenge in low-light image enhancement lies in the complex interplay between noise, shadows, and structural information, making it daunting to preserve the image's original details and colors while denoising and illuminating the dark regions. To address this, the LLNet pipeline employs a hierarchical structure consisting of an encoder and a decoder, both composed of progressive residual blocks and leaky ReLU activation functions. The encoder segment is specifically designed to yield multi-resolution feature representations, capturing the essential structural patterns in the input image. Conversely, the proposed decoder components iteratively refine the enhanced features, re-injecting contextual details from the encoder outputs in a hierarchical manner. Via extensive experimental evaluations and comparisons with state-of-the-art techniques, our comprehensive results demonstrate the efficacy and adaptability of LLNet in tackling diverse low-light scenarios, yielding impressive improvements in not only visual quality and detail retention but also metrics such as PSNR and SSIM. Moreover, the proposed approach facilitates easy integration with various image processing frameworks, rendering LLNet a versatile and efficient solution for low-light image enhancement needs.

title: Automatic Inference of the Quantile Parameter
Abstract: Advances in parameter estimation and uncertainty quantification have become increasingly important in various fields of statistical modeling. The quantile parameter is a significant component of many statistical distributions, capturing the level of variability associated with a particular percentage of data. However, manually inferring this parameter can be a cumbersome and time-consuming process, especially for large datasets and complex models. To address this limitation, this research aims to explore the development of an automated quantile inference framework that can identify the optimal quantile parameter for a given dataset. By leveraging machine learning and Bayesian inference techniques, this framework aims to provide a systematic and computationally efficient method for quantile parameter estimation. The proposed approach is evaluated on various benchmark datasets and compared to existing manual estimation methods. Results demonstrate significant improvements in accuracy, precision, and computational efficiency, making this automated framework a promising tool for researchers and practitioners alike. Furthermore, the research explores the application of this framework to real-world scenarios, including finance, engineering, and climate science, highlighting its potential for advancing our understanding and management of uncertainty in complex systems. By providing a comprehensive and adaptable approach to quantile parameter estimation, this research contributes to the development of more effective statistical modeling and decision-making tools.

title: Representational Distance Learning for Deep Neural Networks
Abstract: Representational distance learning for deep neural networks aims to bridge the gap between disparate representations learned by different neural networks, thereby enabling knowledge transfer and multi-task learning. This framework focuses on minimizing the representational distance between the learned features of individual networks, allowing them to generalize and adapt to new tasks and datasets. By reducing the discrepancy in representation, the involved networks can better share knowledge, leverage their strengths, and extend their capabilities. Our proposed method employs a novel distance metric, derived from the theory of algebraic geometry, which efficiently quantifies the representational dissimilarity between different neural networks. Through this metric, we incorporate a regularization term into the conventional training objective, governing the learning process and facilitating a consistent, efficient, and robust alignment of the representations. Key benefits of this approach include enhanced transferability, faster adaptation to new tasks, and improved accuracy. We analyze the advantages and challenges of this approach in a sequence of experiments, demonstrating its efficacy in multi-task learning and domain adaptation scenarios. Specifically, our experiments involve a series of tasks, showcasing the model's capability to generalize and adapt in various settings, such as image classification, object detection, and segmentation, ultimately validating the potential applications of this representational distance learning framework across a diverse range of deep neural network architectures.

title: Learning Human Identity from Motion Patterns
Abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to learning human identity from motion patterns, focusing on distinguishing individuals based on their unique gait characteristics. A customized convolutional neural network (CNN) architecture, dubbed "MPnet," is proposed to process spatiotemporal data from camera trap recordings, pedestrian surveillance footage, and wearable sensors. The MPnet model leverages a multi-scale convolutional feature extraction mechanism to identify contextual patterns and features within the time-series data, thereby capturing the intrinsic gait characteristics of individuals. Moreover, an ensemble learning strategy integrates multiple feature extractors and classifiers to enhance robustness and improve performance. The results of the comprehensive evaluation on a publicly available dataset indicate that the proposed approach delivers significant improvements in identifying individuals from gait patterns, with accuracy rates exceeding 95%. When compared to existing techniques, the proposed solution demonstrates superior performance in identifying individuals across different sessions, environments, and sensor modalities. The proposed method is also robust to varying walking conditions, such as different terrain, speed, and lighting conditions, due to the inclusion of data augmentation strategies. The findings of this research contribute to the development of efficient and scalable human identification systems that rely on motion patterns, offering potential applications in various fields, including surveillance, security, and healthcare. The technical advancements and insights provided in this paper can support the design and implementation of innovative solutions for human identification and tracking, tailored to specific use cases and domain requirements.
