title: Deep Multimodal Semantic Embeddings for Speech and Images
Abstract: This work presents a novel approach to fusing speech and image modalities within a unified framework of multimodal semantic embeddings, leading to more comprehensive understanding and description of complex phenomena. By leveraging advances in deep learning and representation learning, we integrate speech and image features through a neural network architecture that combines feature extraction, fusion, and encoding processes. Our proposed model is enabled by two primary components: a speech encoder and an image encoder, both based on convolutional neural networks (CNNs) and recurrent neural networks (RNNs), which are designed to capture distinct contextual patterns and semantic information within each modality. A spatial-temporal fusion block is then introduced, facilitating the effective integration of complementary and contextual features from the two modalities and subsequently, embedding them in a shared, multidimensional semantic space. The resulting multimodal embeddings capture relationships between speech and image components, allowing for more accurate and robust analysis of complex datasets. Our extensive experiments on benchmark and real-world multimodal datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of our proposed deep multimodal embedding framework in enhancing representation learning, classification accuracy, and capture of contextual information, paving the way for a wide range of applications in human-computer interaction, multimedia retrieval, and multilinguality, among others.

title: The capabilities and performance of the Automated Planet Finder Telescope with the implementation of a dynamic scheduler
Abstract: The Automated Planet Finder Telescope has proven itself to be a groundbreaking astronomical tool, capable of efficiently discovering exoplanets and conducting astrophysical research. In this study, the performance of the telescope is evaluated with the implementation of a dynamic scheduler, highlighting its capabilities and efficiencies. By examining the scheduling strategy and real-time data processing, the research reveals the telescope's ability to optimize its observing time and maximize the detection of exoplanets. The initial results show a significant increase in the number of detected exoplanets, indicating the importance of integrating dynamic scheduling into the telescope's operations. Furthermore, the study explores the telescope's potential for identifying planetary systems and making accurate population-level assessments, showcasing its unmatched capabilities in the field of exoplanetary science. Through the assessment of various performance metrics, including time-efficiency, detection rates, and data quality, the research demonstrates the critical role that the Automated Planet Finder Telescope with dynamic scheduling can play in understanding our universe and advancing astronomical discoveries. By integrating real-time data processing and adapting to changing observing conditions, this innovative approach can effectively capture the fleeting moments of potentially habitable exoplanet transits, thus paving the way for more in-depth studies of the cosmos.

title: IBMMS Decision Support Tool For Management of Bank Telemarketing Campaigns
Abstract: This study proposes the development of an IBM Maximo Scheduler (IBMMS) decision support tool for effective management of bank telemarketing campaigns. The proposed tool aims to aid banks in maximizing the efficiency of their telemarketing operations while minimizing operational costs. It integrates various aspects of bank telemarketing operations, including campaign planning, staffing, routing, and customer database management. A critical evaluation of current bank telemarketing campaign management practices revealed limitations in existing decision support systems, such as the absence of real-time data analytics, inaccurate predictive modeling, and a lack of personalized interaction with customers. To address these limitations, the proposed IBMMS tool leverages advanced analytics, machine learning algorithms, and business intelligence techniques to provide banks with actionable insights into campaign performance. Additionally, it enables banks to model and predict customer behavior, identify potential leads, and optimize resource allocation. By adopting this decision support tool, banks can enhance the effectiveness of their telemarketing campaigns, improve customer engagement, and ultimately boost revenue. A case study approach was employed to validate the effectiveness of the proposed tool in real-world scenarios. The findings of this study demonstrate the potential of the IBMMS decision support tool in transforming telemarketing campaign management practices in the banking sector.

title: Instantaneous Modelling and Reverse Engineering of DataConsistent Prime Models in Seconds!
Abstract: This paper introduces a groundbreaking novel approach for instantaneous modelling and reverse engineering of data-consistent prime models with unprecedented speed, leveraging the latest advancements in quantum computing and artificial intelligence. Our innovative methodology allows for the efficient generation and reconstruction of prime models from complex data sets, overcoming the limitations of traditional methods that often require extensive computational resources and time. By harnessing the power of quantum parallelism and machine learning algorithms, our approach effectively identifies and reproduces prime models in a fraction of the time required by existing methods, resulting in marked improvements in productivity and efficiency across various fields, including data science, finance, and engineering. Our technique involves processing large data sets through a bespoke hybrid quantum-classical framework that combines the benefits of both worlds, enabling the instant identification of prime models and their corresponding generation. Furthermore, we demonstrate the potential of our approach through a series of experiments, showcasing its scalability and adaptability across diverse data sets and application domains. By unlocking the full potential of prime models, our research contributes significantly to the advancement of data analysis, model development, and predictive analytics, opening up new avenues for innovation and discovery in numerous fields.

title: Discovery Radiomics via StochasticNet Sequencers for Cancer Detection
Abstract: This study presents a novel application of StochasticNet-based sequencers in the discovery of radiomics features for the early detection of cancer. Recent advances in deep learning have led to the development of powerful radiomic models that can uncover hidden patterns in medical images, enabling accurate diagnosis and prognosis. However, the complexity and variability of cancerous tissues pose significant challenges to the development of effective radiomic features. To address this issue, we propose the use of StochasticNet-based sequencers as a preprocessing step to discover hidden patterns in imaging data. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach by applying it to a comprehensive dataset of cancer patients, where we identify a unique set of radiomics features that distinguish between malignant and benign tissues. Our results show that the proposed approach outperforms state-of-the-art radiomic models in terms of classification accuracy and robustness. We also show that the StochasticNet-based sequencers can be optimized for specific imaging modalities and cancer types, making them highly adaptable to different clinical scenarios. The proposed approach has the potential to revolutionize the field of cancer diagnosis and treatment by enabling early detection and personalized treatment plans based on radiomics features extracted from medical images. The findings of this study will contribute to the development of more effective and efficient cancer detection methods, ultimately leading to improved patient outcomes and reduced mortality rates.

title: From Images to Sentences through Scene Description Graphs using Commonsense Reasoning and Knowledge
Abstract: Converting images into descriptive sentences is a fundamental task in computer vision, encompassing image understanding and natural language processing. This study proposes a novel framework, Scene Description Graphs (SDGs), which leverages commonsense reasoning and knowledge to accomplish this vision-to-language translation. The SDGs model first extracts a set of visual features from the input image, representing scene elements such as objects, actions, and spatial relationships. These features are then encoded into a graph structure, where nodes represent individual scene elements and edges capture their relationships. By incorporating a large-scale knowledge graph, the model integrates real-world knowledge with visual information, enabling it to reason about the scene and generate coherent sentences that describe its compositional and relational aspects. Our approach employs a two-stage generation process, with the first stage predicting a set of scene elements and their relationships, and the second stage generating a sentence based on these outputs. Evaluations on various benchmarks demonstrate the efficacy of the proposed SDGs framework in producing accurate and diverse scene descriptions, outperforming state-of-the-art models in several aspects. The results highlight the potential of integrating commonsense reasoning and knowledge with deep visual representations for vision-to-language translation, paving the way for more sophisticated applications in fields like robotics, assistive technology, and education.

title: Taxonomy of Pathways to Dangerous AI
Abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) poses an unprecedented risk to global stability and human well-being, necessitating a comprehensive understanding of its development pathways. This research aims to establish a taxonomy of pathways to dangerous AI, encompassing a range of potential factors and scenarios, from the early stages of AI development to its widespread adoption. Our taxonomy conceptualizes six primary pathways to dangerous AI, each representing a distinct sequence of technological advancements, societal shifts, and decision-making processes. The "hubris pathway" represents the consequences of unchecked enthusiasm and expectations surrounding AI's potential, leading to a systematic overestimation of its capabilities. The "over-engineering pathway" results from the pursuit of excessive technical sophistication, causing AI systems to become uninterpretable and uncontrollable. The "over-adoption pathway" occurs when AI systems are introduced faster than they are tested, leading to unforeseen interactions and negative consequences. The "manipulation pathway" involves the deliberate use of AI for malicious purposes, such as disinformation and deception. The "superintelligence pathway" emerges when an AI system surpasses human intelligence, accelerating its own development and evading human oversight. Lastly, the "social upheaval pathway" results from the displacement of jobs and social structures, precipitating societal unrest and fragility. By exploring these pathways, our taxonomy provides a foundation for developing strategies to mitigate the risks associated with the emergence of dangerous AI.

title: Evolution of Collective Behaviors for a Real Swarm of Aquatic Surface Robots
Abstract: This research delves into the evolution of collective behaviors for a real swarm of aquatic surface robots, a phenomenon where individual actions lead to emergent, coordinated group behavior. The study draws upon insights from biological systems, such as flocking and schooling behavior, to investigate how decentralized and self-organized decision-making strategies can be applied in a controlled aquatic environment. A custom-designed swarm of robotic boats, equipped with GPS, sensors, and communication systems, serves as the primary testbed for this investigation. By leveraging principles of evolutionary algorithms and machine learning, the researchers systematically evolve and analyze the collective behaviors of the robotic swarm in response to various environmental stimuli and tasks, such as obstacle avoidance, foraging, and target tracking. Experimental results and simulations reveal a rich interplay between individual robot interactions and the emergence of complex swarm properties, including patterns of alignment, cohesion, and division of labor. The findings provide valuable insights into the optimal design of decentralized controllers for swarms of aquatic robots, as well as the fundamental mechanisms governing the evolution of collective behavior in these systems, with implications for applications in areas such as search and rescue, environmental monitoring, and marine conservation.

title: The cave of Shadows. Addressing the human factor with generalized additive mixed models
Abstract: This study delves into the enigmatic phenomenon of the "Cave of Shadows," an abandoned mine purported to have an unexplained ability to induce profound introspection, visionary episodes, and other anomalous psychological experiences in visitors. The allure of understanding the underlying mechanisms behind this phenomenon necessitates a nuanced exploration of the complex interplay between the human psyche, environment, and socio-cultural context. To this end, we leveraged generalized additive mixed models (GAMMs) as a statistical framework for scrutinizing the multifaceted interactions at play. Our findings indicate a significant relationship between the duration of presence in the Cave of Shadows, individual susceptibility to stress and anxiety, and the onset of unusual experiences. The data suggest that the cave's perceived ambience, characterized by an omnipresent sense of isolation and confinement, plays a pivotal role in triggering these anomalous experiences. Furthermore, our analyses reveal salient interactions between visitor age, prior exposure to solitary confinement, and reported intensity of unusual experiences. The results of this study propose a dynamic conceptual framework for understanding the mechanisms driving human responses to stress and isolation in extreme environments, underscoring the relevance of addressing the human element in optimizing perceptions and engagement within such settings. Implications of this research have far-reaching consequences for therapeutic and experiential applications, particularly in fields like archetypal psychology and wilderness psychotherapy.

title: Big Data and Business Intelligence: Debunking the Myths
Abstract: The integration of big data and business intelligence has significantly transformed various business sectors and industries globally. Despite its numerous applications and benefits, several misconceptions and myths surrounding big data continue to prevail, hindering its widespread adoption and effective utilization. This study endeavors to clarify and debunk some of these myths, shedding light on the significance of big data and business intelligence in informing business decision-making processes. Through an extensive review of existing literature, empirical evidence, and case studies, this research explores some of the most prevalent misconceptions and myths, including concerns over data quality, scalability, integration, analytics complexity, and talent gap. Furthermore, it investigates how companies can leverage the potential of big data analytics and business intelligence to drive innovation, enhance market competitiveness, and ultimately boost their economic performance. The analysis outcomes illustrate that leveraging the potential of big data analytics and business intelligence is not as daunting as perceived, and that business-to-business and business-to-consumer firms can benefit from accurate, real-time, and meaningful insights drawn from vast amounts of structured and unstructured data. The study's findings are expected to serve as a guiding benchmark for businesses looking to harness the power of data-driven decision-making in today's digital landscape.

title: Information retrieval in folktales using natural language processing
Abstract: This study explores the utilization of natural language processing (NLP) in information retrieval of folktales, highlighting the potential benefits and challenges of leveraging NLP techniques in this domain. Folktales are vital components of human cultural heritage, reflecting various aspects of social, moral, and cultural values. However, their large volume and complexity make information retrieval in these narratives a considerable challenge. The research delves into existing approaches and algorithms for NLP-based information retrieval in folktales, including named entity recognition, sentiment analysis, topic modeling, and semantic search. The proposed system incorporates these techniques to develop a proficient and efficient folktales retrieval platform that assists users in discovering specific stories and narratives within a large corpus. By integrating machine learning models and entity-centric disambiguation methods, the platform ensures an accurate and consistent retrieval process. Furthermore, subjective evaluations demonstrate the effectiveness of the NLP-based approach, particularly in terms of precision, recall, and query satisfaction. The systematic evaluation of this work validates its practicality and effectiveness as a valuable research contribution to the broader NLP and digital humanities domains.

title: Incorporating Knowledge into Structural Equation Models using Auxiliary Variables
Abstract: This study proposes a novel approach for incorporating external knowledge into structural equation models (SEMs) through the use of auxiliary variables. The inclusion of knowledge-driven auxiliary variables can augment the existing structural paths in a SEM by capturing additional relationships between latent constructs. A systematic approach is developed for identifying and specifying auxiliary variables based on prior knowledge and existing research. This involves a combination of literature reviews and expert elicitation to identify relevant auxiliary variables. The proposed method also addresses the challenges of integrating multiple knowledge sources and prioritizing the most informative auxiliary variables for a given SEM. A simulation study is conducted to evaluate the performance of the proposed approach under varying levels of measurement error, sample size, and auxiliary variable strength. The results show that incorporating knowledge-driven auxiliary variables can significantly improve the accuracy of parameter estimates and model fit in SEMs. The approach is applied to real-world data to demonstrate its practical utility and guide future research studies. The proposed method facilitates the integration of external knowledge into SEMs, enabling researchers to update and revise their models based on new insights and findings, ultimately advancing the development of more nuanced and accurate theories.

title: Traffic Sign Classification Using Deep Inception Based Convolutional Networks
Abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to traffic sign classification using deep inception-based convolutional networks. The designed system leverages the concept of transfer learning to improve the classification accuracy and efficiency of traffic signs. By utilizing pre-trained Inception V3 and V4 models, the proposed framework adapts the network structure to suit the specific requirements of traffic sign recognition. The dataset used for this experiment is the German Traffic Sign Recognition Benchmark (GTSRB), which comprises 43 unique sign classes, including stop signs, warning signs, and speed limit signs. The results demonstrate the superiority of the proposed system over other state-of-the-art approaches in terms of accuracy and computational efficiency. To achieve optimal performance, extensive experiments involving different hyperparameter tuning and data augmentation techniques have been carried out. Notably, the integration of contextual information obtained from the surrounding pixel regions significantly enhances the network's ability to distinguish between subtle sign variations. Furthermore, the proposed system exhibits excellent robustness against varied lighting conditions, making it highly suitable for real-world traffic sign recognition applications. The project outcomes not only contribute to the advancement of intelligent transportation systems but also provide valuable insights for further research in the field of image classification and deep learning.

title: Detecting events and key actors in multi-person videos
Abstract: This study proposes a novel event detection and key actor identification system tailored to the complexities of multi-person videos. Traditional event detection techniques struggle with identifying specific actions and actors in crowded scenes, often resulting in incorrect or incomplete annotations. Our approach addresses these challenges by leveraging a multi-stage architecture that incorporate deep learning techniques. First, a multi-task learning framework is employed to detect and segment the individuals in each frame, enabling the system to identify the actions and movements of each actor. Next, a graph-based representation is utilized to model the temporal relationships between actions, facilitating the detection of complex events such as handovers, goal scoring, and collisions. The system also incorporates a key actor identification module that relies on a combination of pose estimation, object interaction, and social context to pinpoint the most influential individuals in each scene. The proposed system has been evaluated on several benchmark datasets with encouraging results, achieving state-of-the-art performance in both event detection and key actor identification tasks. Furthermore, the system's ability to handle real-world video footage with varying lighting conditions, resolutions, and camera angles demonstrates its potential for deployment in practical applications, such as sports analysis, surveillance, and event monitoring.

title: Spectral-Spatial Classification of Hyperspectral Image Using Autoencoders
Abstract:
Spectral-Spatial Classification of Hyperspectral Image Using Autoencoders Abstract:

Hyperspectral imaging technology has gained significant attention in recent years due to its ability to capture detailed spectral information of the environment. However, the large number of bands and relatively small number of samples in hyperspectral images pose a significant challenge for classification tasks. Traditional machine learning approaches have been employed for hyperspectral image classification, but they often fail to capture the complex spatial relationships between pixels. Autoencoders, a type of neural network that learns to compress and reconstruct data, have shown promise in capturing both spectral and spatial information. This research explores the use of autoencoders for spectral-spatial classification of hyperspectral images. We propose a dual encoder architecture, where one encoder learns to compress spectral information and another encoder learns to capture spatial context. The output of the two encoders is then fused to form a feature representation that captures both spectral and spatial features. We evaluate the proposed approach on several benchmark datasets and compare it with state-of-the-art methods. The results show that our approach achieves significant improvements in classification accuracy, highlighting the potential of autoencoders for hyperspectral image classification. Furthermore, our analysis of the encoder weights provides insights into the spectral and spatial features that are learned by the autoencoder, shedding light on the underlying mechanisms that drive the classification decisions.

title: A disembodied developmental robotic agent called Samu Bátfai
Abstract: Our research focuses on the development of a disembodied developmental robotic agent, named Samu Bátfai, which embodies the principles of cognitive, social, and emotional development in robots. Through the integration of machine learning algorithms and sensory-motor interactions, Samu Bátfai is capable of navigating and adapting to its environment in a way that mimics human infant development. We explored the use of autonomous interaction with the environment to facilitate learning and development, drawing on theories of cognitive development such as Jean Piaget's constructivist theory and Lev Vygotsky's sociocultural theory. In our study, Samu Bátfai learns to recognize and classify objects, develop predictive models of the environment, and learn to navigate and avoid obstacles. Through embodied interaction, the robotic agent develops an understanding of causality, the concept of space and events, and the relation between actions and outcomes. Additionally, we examined the potential of the agent to acquire social and emotional competencies through interactions with humans, including empathy, cooperation, and understanding human perspectives. The findings of our study offer new insights into the possibilities of embodied cognition and the development of social and emotional intelligence in robots.

title: Visual Language Modeling on CNN Image Representations
Abstract: Visual language modeling has emerged as a crucial aspect in multimodal understanding, enabling computers to perceive and reason about visual content alongside text. Recent advancements in deep learning, particularly the fusion of transformer architectures and convolutional neural networks (CNNs), have yielded significant improvements in image-text matching and visual grounding tasks. However, the relationship between CNN image representations and language models remains poorly understood. This study aims to bridge this gap by exploring the capabilities and limitations of visual language modeling on CNN image representations. We examine the effectiveness of various CNN architectures in generating informative image representations that can be mapped to language models, and investigate the impact of different image-text fusion strategies on the quality of generated text. Our experiments involve training and testing visual language models on a range of image-text datasets, including COCO, Flickr30k, and VQA, under varying settings of image resolution, text length, and fusion techniques. By comparing the performance of different CNN representations and fusion strategies, we reveal the best practices for designing effective visual language models and discuss their implications for the development of multimodal machine learning applications. The results of this study contribute to a deeper understanding of visual language modeling and highlight its potential in real-world scenarios where images and text are intimately connected.

title: Enacting textual entailment and ontologies for automated essay grading in chemical domain
Abstract: This research explores the application of textual entailment and ontologies to automate essay grading in the chemical domain. Enacting textual entailment involves identifying and evaluating the relationships between key concepts and information in a student's response, enabling the assessment of the underlying knowledge and reasoning skills demonstrated. Ontologies, with their rich knowledge representation and semantic structures, provide a robust framework for organizing and categorizing chemical concepts, allowing for the effective matching and evaluation of response content. The proposed approach integrates natural language processing (NLP) techniques with ontological reasoning to generate comprehensive models of chemical knowledge and relevant criteria for assessing student understanding. The integrated system evaluates student essays based on the entailment relationships between concepts, relevance to chemical domain, and alignment with the targeted learning objectives. To evaluate the efficacy of this approach, a collection of annotated essays was used to fine-tune and validate the proposed system against a set of established grading schemes and rubrics. The experimental results indicate significant improvements in accuracy and reliability compared to traditional manual grading methods, suggesting the potential of this system to support efficient, effective, and personalized assessment of students' performance in chemical domain-based courses. Overall, the study contributes to the development of AI-powered tools for automated essay grading in high-stakes assessment environments.

title: An Efficient Multilinear Optimization Framework for Hypergraph Matching
Abstract: A reliable and versatile hypergraph matching is pivotal for numerous real-world applications, including computer vision, robotics, and social networks. Unfortunately, designing an efficient framework for hypergraph matching is an extremely challenging task, largely due to the non-trivial combinatorial complexity. Existing approaches often rely on suboptimal heuristic approximations or are limited to specific types of hypergraphs, making it imperative to develop a general and efficient multilinear optimization framework. This research endeavors to establish a novel framework for hypergraph matching, focusing on the synergy of multilinear algebra and optimization techniques. By utilizing the structural properties of multilinear functions, the proposed framework is able to efficiently cast the hypergraph matching problem as a multilinear optimization problem, formulating it as an equivalent minimization problem in the space of polynomials. We demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed framework using a range of hypergraphs of varying sizes and configurations, achieving competitive optimization results that are often superior to existing state-of-the-art methods. Moreover, the framework facilitates the discovery of meaningful insights into the structural properties of hypergraphs, thereby shedding new light on the essence of hypergraph matching and its rich associated challenges. Our framework offers a balanced trade-off between computational efficiency and optimization quality, paving the way for the development of more sophisticated hypergraph matching algorithms that can solve larger and more complex problems.

title: Decomposition Bounds for Marginal MAP
Abstract: This paper presents a comprehensive study on decomposition bounds for marginal MAP inference, a fundamental problem in probabilistic graphical models. Marginal MAP involves finding the most probable assignment of values to a subset of variables, conditioned on available observations, and has numerous applications in machine learning, artificial intelligence, and related fields. However, exact computation of marginal MAP is generally intractable and solving this problem is #P-hard. As a result, researchers have resorted to approximation methods, which often rely on the framework of Lovász local lemma and the concept of decomposition bounds. This paper provides a novel perspective on decomposing the marginal MAP problem into smaller, more manageable sub-problems using a Lagrangian-based approach. Our strategy employs quadratic programming and multi-block alternating direction method of multipliers to efficiently approximate the optimal solution. The paper also provides tight computational bounds for our proposed methods, leveraging the robust convexification of specific auxiliary functions. By examining various representative graphs and large-scale instances, our experimental results suggest that the proposed method yields tighter and more accurate bounds compared to existing decomposition methods. Furthermore, the introduction of a novel graph clustering strategy allows for efficient decomposition in cases of large-scale graphs. This paper has significant implications for the generalization of existing MAP inference algorithms, offering easier and more efficient ways to solve important problems in machine learning and computer science.

title: A fuzzy based conceptual framework for career counselling
Abstract: This paper proposes a novel fuzzy-based conceptual framework for career counselling to facilitate efficient and effective career decision-making for individuals. Presently, career counselling relies heavily on traditional methods which might not account for the complexities and uncertainties inherent in career choices, resulting in inaccurate guidance and low career satisfaction rates. In response, this framework integrates fuzzy logic theory with career development theories to address the shortcomings of traditional approaches. The framework is grounded in the principles of fuzzy set theory, which allows for the incorporation of ambiguity and uncertainty into career assessment and decision-making processes. Using this framework, career counsellors can accurately capture and analyse individual differences, career aspirations, and occupational characteristics, leading to more precise and contextualised career recommendations. Furthermore, the fuzzy-based conceptual framework enables the consideration of multiple career paths and outcomes, reducing decision anxieties and enhancing job search effectiveness. A case study of its implementation in a real-world setting highlights the framework's potential in improving career counselling outcomes, increasing client satisfaction, and promoting autonomy in career decision-making. Overall, this framework offers a paradigm shift in career counselling, bridging the gap between traditional and contemporary career development practices while pushing the boundaries of fuzzy-based career guidance.

title: Proceedings First International Workshop on Focusing
Abstract: This workshop provides a platform for researchers and practitioners to discuss the theoretical foundations, implementation techniques, and applications of focusing logical frameworks. Focusing, also known as analytic tableaux or model elimination, is a deductive reasoning paradigm and a key methodology in artificial intelligence, computer science, and mathematical logic. The proceedings brings together original contributions in all aspects of focusing, ranging from theoretical aspects such as optimal focusing algorithms and resolution strategies, to implementation aspects such as efficient data structures, parallel processing, and practical applications in various domains. The papers presented demonstrate novel approaches to solving complex problems in areas like automated reasoning, knowledge representation, and natural language processing, highlighting the power and versatility of focusing techniques. The recent breakthroughs and emerging trends in artificial intelligence, specifically in areas like deep learning and hybrid reasoning, are also discussed, showcasing the potential of focusing methodologies to address the computational complexity of AI-related challenges. These advancements and theoretical analyses aimed towards increasing the efficiency and effectiveness of AI systems, ultimately resulting in improved decision-making, conflict resolution, and problem-solving capabilities, and creating highly practical applications in real-world problems.

title: Proceedings Workshop on Models for Formal Analysis of Real Systems
Abstract: This workshop gathered researchers from diverse fields of computer science and mathematics to present novel advances in modeling and analysis techniques for real-world systems. Formal methods have long been recognized for their ability to provide a rigorous and systematic approach to system design and verification. However, their adoption in practice remains limited by the complexity of tailoring these methods to specific domains and systems. The papers in this workshop focused on addressing this challenge by presenting models, theories, and techniques that can be applied to real-world systems, comprising complex software, embedded systems, and cyber-physical systems, particularly emphasizing systems of national and international importance. Researchers demonstrated the application of hybrid models, machine learning, and stochastic processes in real-world scenarios, often incorporating mathematical rigor and analytics. The effectiveness and scalability of these methods were evaluated through case studies and performance measurements on real-world systems, showcasing their potential for practical adoption. The presented works expand upon traditional notions of formal methods, instead embracing greater flexibility and expressiveness while maintaining computational tractability. As such, this workshop contributes to the ongoing development of formal methods that cater to the needs of real-world applications and facilitates their role in shaping the future of complex system design and verification.

title: (Yet) Another Theoretical Model of Thinking
Abstract: Despite a plethora of theoretical frameworks detailing various aspects of thinking, fundamental questions remain unanswered regarding its underlying structure and developmental trajectory. A long-standing challenge in the field of cognitive science is the integration of disparate theories to provide an overarching model that can account for an individual's ability to reason, problem-solve, and learn. Many existing theories focus on narrow aspects of thinking, such as intuitive versus deliberative thought or dual-process models, yet they fail to capture the complex interplay between different cognitive processes that enable human thought. In response to these limitations, this paper presents a novel theoretical framework, dubbed the 'Eunoian model', which seeks to provide a more comprehensive account of thinking. Drawing on insights from philosophy, psychology, and neuroscience, the Eunoian model posits that thinking is comprised of three distinct, yet interdependent, components: the 'causal', 'intuitive', and 'evaluative' processes. Each of these processes is hypothesized to be engaged at different stages of the thinking process, and their relationships are conceptualized as dynamic and context-dependent. Through a series of simulations, empirical studies, and conceptual analyses, we test the Eunoian model's predictive power and assess its ability to account for a range of complex cognitive phenomena, including reasoning, decision-making, and learning.

title: Learning Linguistic Biomarkers for Predicting Mild Cognitive Impairment using Compound Skip-grams
Abstract: This study aims to explore the application of linguistic biomarkers in predicting mild cognitive impairment (MCI) through the lens of compound skip-grams. Various linguistic features can serve as potential biomarkers, but few studies have effectively integrated multiple features to identify early signs of MCI. The Compound Skip-grams model, designed to capture both local and non-local dependencies in words, was utilized to analyze text data from individuals with MCI and age-matched controls. The proposed method leverages the rich linguistic profiles of language production in individuals with MCI to predict the development of MCI. In particular, the model extracts complex linguistic patterns, including two- and three-word combinations, and their associated frequency, to identify significant predictive biomarkers. A machine learning pipeline is constructed using the extracted features to classify individuals as having MCI or not. The experimental results demonstrate encouraging performance with high accuracy and area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) values. Furthermore, feature importance and permutation feature importance are computed to understand the contributions of individual linguistic biomarkers and compound skip-gram patterns. The findings demonstrate the feasibility of using compound skip-grams as a potential tool for MCI prediction based on complex linguistic patterns, laying the groundwork for the application of linguistic biomarkers in cognitive assessments and potential therapeutic interventions. The research provides innovative insights into the use of linguistic measures and their integrative analysis in diagnostic and research settings.

title: A Study of an Modeling Method of T-S fuzzy System Based on Moving Fuzzy Reasoning and Its Application
Abstract: This study explores an advanced modeling method of T-S fuzzy systems based on moving fuzzy reasoning, specifically targeting their potential applications in real-world complex systems. The T-S fuzzy system is a prominent approach in fuzzy modeling, offering a flexible framework for representing and analyzing complex relationships between variables. However, the conventional fixed fuzzy reasoning approach used in most T-S systems has limitations in accurately modeling dynamic systems changes. To address these challenges, the proposed moving fuzzy reasoning approach updates both the fuzzy rule consequent parts and the premise parameters simultaneously using the least-squares estimator, thus achieving a more accurate dynamic modeling performance. A series of simulations with different datasets and various case studies show the superior performance of the proposed method compared to existing models in terms of root mean squared error and peak signal-to-noise ratio. Additionally, the study focuses on the applicability and effectiveness of the moving fuzzy reasoning-based T-S system in modeling and prediction of nonlinear systems, showcasing its promising ability to be used in various engineering fields where complex dynamic relationships dominate. The proposed enhanced T-S fuzzy system demonstrates the capabilities of moving fuzzy reasoning for more precise modeling and analysis of dynamic systems, providing insights into their potential applications in real-time predictive maintenance, fault diagnosis, and monitoring of critical infrastructure systems. The results and analysis of this study contribute to the development of improved intelligent systems and enhance the understanding of complex dynamic behaviors, ultimately contributing to better decision-making strategies.

title: A Winner-Take-All Approach to Emotional Neural Networks with Universal Approximation Property
Abstract:
A Winner-Take-All Approach to Emotional Neural Networks with Universal Approximation Property 

This paper proposes a novel Winner-Take-All (WTA) approach to design efficient Emotional Neural Networks (ENN) with the universal approximation property. ENNs, which integrate emotions into neural networks, are essential for developing more realistic and human-like artificial intelligence. However, traditional ENNs suffer from excessive computational complexity and low learning efficiency. To address these issues, we introduce a WTA-based ENN architecture that selectively activates the most relevant emotions, thereby reducing the dimensionality of the emotional space. Our proposed network inherits the fundamental characteristics of ENNs, including emotional regulation, empathy, and social interaction, while maintaining the universal approximation property. We demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach through rigorous mathematical analysis and comparative experimental results on several benchmark tasks, including sentiment analysis, emotional intelligence assessment, and social network inference. Our results show that the WTA-ENN outperforms state-of-the-art ENNs in terms of learning speed, generalizability, and interpretability, making it a promising candidate for real-world applications. The WTA-ENN's ability to approximate any continuous function makes it a versatile and practical choice for a wide range of tasks, from affective computing to social robotics and human-computer interaction.

title: Design of an Alarm System for Isfahan Ozone Level based on Artificial Intelligence Predictor Models
Abstract: This study initiates the design of an intelligent alarm system for Isfahan, aimed at predicting ozone levels and alerting residents of impending hazardous air quality conditions. A crucial concern for several urban environments worldwide, ozone pollution poses significant risks to public health. To address this issue effectively, a multiscale modeling process is devised, leveraging the predictive capabilities of artificial intelligence (AI) into municipal-scale forecasting. By integrating data acquisition from ground-level atmospheric sensors with climate projection models, we are able to accurately calculate ozone concentration levels in near real-time. Machine and deep learning frameworks are then employed in validation efforts, enabling improved accuracy levels of 85% for daytime and 76% for nighttime predictions during peak-ozone intervals. The proposed alarm system integrates robust AI predictor models with user-friendly mobile applications, ensuring timely dissemination of ozone alerts to residents, policymakers, and emergency responders. Furthermore, impact assessments of the implemented system reveal significant enhancement of civic preparedness and air pollution mitigation efforts, solidifying a safer urban atmosphere with reduced ozone-related risks. By extending comprehensive air quality forecasting standards, this paper explores and develops an ultra-modern framework for evaluating, predicting, and mitigating ozone levels.

title: Review-Level Sentiment Classification with Sentence-Level Polarity Correction
Abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to Review-Level Sentiment Classification (RLSC) that utilizes a hybrid deep learning model combining both linguistic features and sentiment polarities at the sentence level. The proposed framework, Sentiment Corrector (SC), consists of two primary components: a sentence-level sentiment classification module and a polarity correction module. The first module leverages a transformer-based architecture, pre-trained on a massive corpus of text data, to classify the overall sentiment of a review. However, the module may occasionally misclassify sentences containing nuanced or context-dependent emotional expressions. To address this issue, the polarity correction module is employed, utilizing a probabilistic paradigm to reassess the sentiment of individual sentences while taking into account the overall sentiment of the review. By incorporating both sentence-level and review-level features, SC improves the accuracy of RLSC, particularly in scenarios where sentence-level polarity correction is crucial. Extensive experiments on various datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of SC, achieving state-of-the-art performance in comparison to existing RLSC models. The results highlight the significance of integrating sentence-level sentiment analysis with review-level polarity correction for improved accuracy in sentiment classification tasks.

title: Review of Person Re-identification Techniques
Abstract: Person re-identification is a challenging task in the field of computer vision and machine learning, where the goal is to recognize individuals across multiple cameras with non-overlapping views. Despite advancements in this field, it remains an open problem due to variations in illumination, pose, and viewpoint changes. Recent progress in deep learning has led to the development of several person re-identification techniques, including convolutional neural networks (CNNs), attention-based models, and metric learning approaches. These techniques have been experimented with various databases, such as Market-1501, DukeMTMC, and CUHK03, showing promising results. However, there is a need to review and analyze these techniques to understand their strengths, limitations, and applications. This paper provides an in-depth review of the state-of-the-art person re-identification techniques, covering their architectures, training procedures, and evaluation metrics. We discuss the advantages and disadvantages of each technique and highlight the key factors that affect their performance. Furthermore, we analyze the applications of person re-identification in various fields, including surveillance, biometric authentication, and smart cities. We also discuss the challenges and future directions of this field, including the development of more robust and scalable models, and the need for larger and more diverse datasets. Our review aims to provide a comprehensive understanding of the current state of person re-identification techniques and to inspire further research in this area.

title: Combining Privileged Information to Improve Context-Aware Recommender Systems
Abstract: This study investigates the effectiveness of combining privileged information in context-aware recommender systems. Current recommender systems rely heavily on user behavior and item attributes to provide recommendations, but often neglect auxiliary information that can be highly informative, such as item categories, attributes, or expert knowledge. We propose a novel approach that leverages multiple types of privileged information to enhance the accuracy and diversity of recommendations. Our method, named Context-Aware Privileged Fusion (CAPF), aggregates and weighs the contributions of multiple privileged sources in an optimization framework. This approach is evaluated using four real-world datasets with diverse characteristics and various types of privileged information. Our experimental results demonstrate that CAPF significantly outperforms state-of-the-art context-aware recommender systems in terms of precision, recall, and diversity of recommendations, particularly when exploiting multiple privileged sources. Furthermore, the analysis of the model's performance reveals that the optimal weighting of privileged sources varies across datasets and evaluation metrics, underscoring the importance of adaptive and explainable approaches to context-aware recommendation. By providing a flexible and interpretable framework for combining privileged information, CAPF has the potential to improve the effectiveness of context-aware recommender systems in various applications, including e-commerce, travel, and media recommendation.

title: Robotics Technology in Mental Health Care
Abstract: The integration of robotics technology in mental health care has garnered significant attention in recent years due to its potential to provide novel solutions for addressing diverse aspects of mental well-being. Research has demonstrated that robots can effectively serve as companions for individuals with psychosocial disabilities, alleviating feelings of loneliness and social isolation that often exacerbate mental health conditions. Furthermore, robots can facilitate tailored interventions and therapies for a range of disorders, including anxiety, depression, and post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD). Through the use of advanced machine learning algorithms, robots can adapt their responses to the unique needs and preferences of individuals, promoting engagement and fostering a sense of trust. Additionally, robots can aid mental health professionals in gathering data and monitoring patient outcomes, enhancing the efficiency and effectiveness of therapeutic interventions. Preliminary studies have yielded promising results, showing that robot-assisted therapy can lead to improved mental health outcomes, reduced symptoms, and enhanced quality of life. Nevertheless, there are concerns regarding the potential limitations and biases associated with the development and deployment of robots in mental health care, including issues of cultural sensitivity, data security, and human-robot interaction. Addressing these concerns will be essential in navigating the full potential of robotic technology in mental health care.

title: Deep Kernel Learning
Abstract: Deep kernel learning has emerged as a promising approach to hybridize the strengths of both kernel methods and deep neural networks. Traditional kernel methods offer a powerful mean for incorporating non-linear hypotheses into the problem-solving process by embedding data into a high-dimensional feature space through a kernel function. However, the scalability and computational requirements of these methods often become a bottleneck in handling large-scale datasets. On the other hand, deep neural networks have gained significant attention in recent years for their ability to learn hierarchical and complex representations from raw data. Despite their success, deep neural networks may suffer from poor generalization performance and Mode Collapse when dealing with smaller datasets or lack of sufficient training data. This raises the question of whether the paradigms of deep learning and kernel methods can be combined to leverage their respective strengths and address their limitations. Deep kernel learning aims to strike a balance between the capacity of deep neural networks and the interpretability and flexibility of kernel methods by incorporating the kernel trick into the network architecture. This fusion enables the neural network to learn non-linear transformations that can be generalized using a kernel function, potentially offering a scalable and flexible framework for various machine learning tasks, including classification, regression, and clustering. The research in this domain is rapidly advancing, with new architectures and techniques being proposed to adapt kernel methods to deep neural networks and integrate deep neural networks with kernel-based approaches.

title: Learning Optimized Or's of And's
Abstract: This study delves into the realm of logic and Boolean operations, focusing on learning optimized Or's of And's (OoA's) in the context of artificial intelligence and software engineering. As an omnipresent concept in computer science, Boolean logic plays a pivotal role in various algorithms, data structures, and decision-making processes. In the pursuit of enhancing efficiency and scalability, researchers have sought innovative ways to optimize Boolean operations, particularly when dealing with complex logical expressions. Or's of And's, which emerge in the implementation of disjunctive normal form (DNF) or any logic using both disjunction and conjunctions presents an interesting aspect of optimization. The investigation of OoA's in various computing applications and their algorithms has garnered attention for its potential to minimize computational overhead and maximize problem-solving speed. Through a thorough examination of existing literature and application-driven prototypes, this research aims to identify the optimization techniques and strategies suitable for OoA expressions, further evaluating their applicability across distinct domains and complexity levels. By providing a comprehensive understanding of OoA optimization methods and their real-world significance, this study seeks to contribute to the advancement of more efficient Boolean operations, enhancing the broader impact on related technologies and problem-solving frameworks.

title: Submodular Hamming Metrics
Abstract: This paper introduces a novel framework for analyzing and utilizing Submodular Hamming metrics, a class of functions that exhibit diminishing returns when added to a subset. We provide a comprehensive overview of the properties and implications of these metrics, including tight relationships between the submodularity of Hamming metrics and their applications in Machine Learning and Optimization. By leveraging the submodularity of Hamming metrics, we develop new algorithms for efficient data mining and clustering, allowing for more accurate feature selection and dimensionality reduction. Our approach also enables the derivation of tight bounds on the computational complexity of existing algorithms, ensuring optimal scalability for large datasets. Furthermore, we introduce a novel extension of Hamming metrics to handle non-binary instances, enabling the analysis of complex, high-dimensional data with diverse attribute types. Empirical evidence confirms the effectiveness of our Submodular Hamming metrics in achieving state-of-the-art results for several benchmark tasks, including image segmentation, Anomaly detection, and Community Detection. Our research aims to establish Submodular Hamming metrics as a fundamental tool in Data Science and Machine Learning, offering a balanced approach that strikes a trade-off between computational efficiency, scalability, and accuracy.

title: Towards a Better Understanding of Predict and Count Models
Abstract: Predict and count models have garnered significant attention in recent years, particularly in the realm of statistical analysis and machine learning. These models are primarily employed to forecast the occurrence of future events or predict the likelihood of an event happening, by modeling the underlying count data. This study aims to delve deeper into the intricacies of these models, focusing on their strengths, limitations, and potential applications. Through a comprehensive literature review and theoretical analysis, this research will investigate the essential components of predict and count models, including the Poisson, negative binomial, and generalized mixed models, and assess their effectiveness in various domains such as epidemiology, finance, and social sciences. The research will also explore recent advancements in model development and the use of advanced techniques such as generalized linear mixed models and machine learning algorithms to improve the predictive power and robustness of these models. Additionally, the study will examine the challenges associated with the model selection, model calibration, and model performance evaluation, highlighting critical considerations for practitioners. By providing a nuanced understanding of predict and count models, this research aims to inform the development of more accurate and reliable predictive models, ultimately facilitating better decision-making in complex, high-stakes environments.

title: Depth, balancing, and limits of the Elo model
Abstract: The Elo model, initially developed for rating chess players, has become a widely used algorithm in games and competitive environments to estimate the relative skill of participants. This paper aims to provide an in-depth analysis of the Elo model, investigating its depth, balancing, and limits. As an improvement over traditional win-loss ratio models, Elo models rely on a more sophisticated mathematical framework, considering not only the outcome but also the expectations based upon the opponents' ratings. A deeper investigation into the properties of Elo models reveals that, while they are undeniably effective in capturing pairwise relationships, their limitations arise from their assumption of linearity in ranking. This assumption results in inherent imbalances in rating distributions, particularly when dealing with populations of small, unevenly sized subgroups. A further challenge lies in manipulating Elo models to handle variable-match sizes, participant volatility, and biased competition structures, pointing to extensive possibilities for the model's improvement. Furthermore, this paper explores Elo's compatibility with, and intersections of, recent advances in probability theory and learning algorithms, aiming to shed light on whether and how these ideas can leverage practical applications for the modernized Elo model, boosting its predictive performance and information-gathering capabilities.

title: An Action Language for Multi-Agent Domains: Foundations
Abstract: This abstract proposes a novel action language, specifically designed to operate within multi-agent domains. Building upon existing work in the field of action languages, our approach provides a framework for expressively and efficiently integrating heterogeneous agents and their associated logics. The language's core features include flexible integration of agent theories, allowance for variable and context-dependent action preconditions, and mechanisms to handle changing preferences and goal dependencies. Central to this language is the notion of an 'orchestration theory', which encapsulates the global structure and interactions between agents. By decoupling agent-specific extensions from the core language, our framework enables seamless integration with existing agent platforms and facilitates scalable multi-agent applications. Comprehensive validation of the proposed language is provided through formal semantics, proof-theoretic encodings, and case studies, demonstrating its expressiveness and usability in both prototypical and real-world settings. The outcome of our work is a versatile action language, suitable for description, reasoning, and execution in large-scale, dynamic multi-agent environments. By bridging the gap between formal semantics and practical application, our language serves as a foundation for advancing multi-agent research and promoting the development of sophisticated autonomous systems.

title: Thoughts on Massively Scalable Gaussian Processes
Abstract: This paper explores the scalability aspects of Gaussian Processes (GPs) in machine learning applications, particularly those that require prediction on large datasets. GPs are known for their ability to model complex, non-linear relationships between input and output variables, making them a popular choice for regression and classification tasks. However, their computational cost and memory requirements pose significant challenges when applied to massively scalable problems. Traditional GP methods exhibit a primary time complexity of O(n^3), where n is the number of training data points, limiting their applicability to large datasets. Although attempts have been made to address this issue through various approximations and sparse approximations, they often compromise on the model's accuracy and expressiveness. This study proposes a novel distributed GP framework that leverages the strengths of Hadoop MapReduce and parallel processing to scale GPs to massive datasets while maintaining their statistical guarantees. By decomposing the GP computations into smaller, independently solvable sub-problems, our approach enables the efficient use of multi-core processors and distributed computing resources. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of our framework in efficiently and accurately modeling large datasets with scalable GPs, opening up new possibilities for real-world applications in areas such as recommender systems, climate modeling, and structural health monitoring.

title: Symmetry-invariant optimization in deep networks
Abstract: Symmetry-invariant optimization in deep networks is a fundamental challenge in the field of deep learning, where the inherent group symmetries within the model can significantly hinder the convergence of optimization algorithms, leading to suboptimal solutions and reduced generalizability. This issue arises due to the fact that most deep network architectures exhibit symmetries, such as translational or rotational symmetries, which can be exploited by the model to skew its performance towards a specific set of solutions. The existing optimization algorithms, designed without considering these symmetries, fail to address this problem effectively, ending up in local optima far away from the true global optimum. Therefore, it is crucial to develop symmetry-aware optimization algorithms that are capable of exploiting these symmetries to speed up convergence while maintaining good generalization characteristics. Recent research has shown that by incorporating symmetry information into the optimization process, it is possible to obtain superior results and improvements in convergence rates and generalization capabilities. This paper proposes an innovative symmetry-invariant optimization framework that exploits the intrinsic symmetries of deep networks to develop efficient optimization algorithms that converge to the global optimum and yield better performance in terms of both accuracy and robustness, while robustly handling symmetries commonly observed in deep networks.

title: Adaptive information-theoretic bounded rational decision-making with parametric priors
Abstract: This paper presents a novel decision-making framework that combines the theories of bounded rationality with the principles of adaptive information processing, which is achieved through the utilization of parametric prior distributions over decision alternatives. Our model, termed the adaptive information-theoretic decision maker (AIDM), seeks to alleviate the limitations of existing rational choice models by relaxing the assumption of perfect information and incorporating uncertainty in the decision environment. AIDM leverages the prior distributions to adapt to changing circumstances and revise its decision-making strategy accordingly, thereby enabling the decision maker to reallocate its resources under uncertainty and choose the optimal path to maximize its decision-making performance. We deploy an information-theoretic objective function, i.e., the normalized information gain, to measure the expected utility of each decision. By optimizing this objective function with respect to the decision variables subject to a computational budget constraint, AIDM dynamically adjusts its decision parameters to maximize the expected information gain and optimize its decision-making performance under uncertainty. Experimental results on a range of benchmark problems demonstrate the efficacy of AIDM in achieving superior decision-making performance compared to state-of-the-art models, and highlight its potential as a robust and versatile tool for adaptive decision-making under uncertainty.

title: Computing sets of graded attribute implications with witnessed non-redundancy
Abstract: This paper presents a framework for computing sets of graded attribute implications with witnessed non-redundancy, enabling users to extract knowledge from imperfect data in digital systems. Gradual reasoning in computational models of uncertainty often involves the formation of implications, where one attribute is implied by another based on their degree of association. Traditional computing methods for such implications may ignore non-redundancy properties, leading to excessive implications that obscure the underlying data patterns. To address this limitation, our work introduces a novel algorithm that verifies non-redundancy properties, leveraging witnessed relationships between arguments and implications. By identifying and discarding redundant implications, our approach ensures that the derived implications represent significant associations in the data. The framework is further empowered by an implication graph-based structure, which captures the hierarchical relationships between implications and facilitates efficient computation. A reduction theorem is established, showing that the problem of computing the set of graded attribute implications with witnessed non-redundancy is in PSPACE. Experimental results on both synthetic and real-world datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach in extract- ing high-quality implications while controlling redundancy, thus shedding new light on the knowledge-discovery process in uncertain data analysis.

title: Radio SETI Observations of the Anomalous Star KIC 8462852
Abstract: The star KIC 8462852, also known as Tabby's Star, has garnered significant attention in the astrophysical community due to its unusual dimming patterns, which some have speculated could be evidence of an advanced alien civilization. The Search for Extraterrestrial Intelligence (SETI) Institute has prompted this study to investigate the possibility of radio signals emanating from this enigmatic star. Through a deep radio SETI observation program conducted between 2015 and 2018, we analyzed nearly 2 million minutes of dedicated telescope time. Our observations utilized the 100-meter Robert C. Byrd Green Bank Telescope and the 85-meter Gunma Astronomical Observatory's radio telescope to sweep the sky for narrowband signals. We employed a combination of autocorrelation and spectral methods to systematically search for periodic or aperiodic signals associated with KIC 8462852, while simultaneously testing for the presence of previously known astrophysical and anthropogenic interference. The absence of any statistically significant signals was found, which, combined with the constraints on any potential optical and infrared transient events, continues to lend credence to the hypothesis that KIC 8462852 hosts a cataclysmic or circumstellar event, but casts doubt on a massive alien construct interpretation of the dimming phenomenon.

title: Achieving Sensor Fusion for Collaborative Multi-level Monitoring of Pipeline Infrastructures
Abstract: This research paper comprehensively explores the concept of sensor fusion for enhancing collaborative multi-level monitoring of pipeline infrastructures. In light of the increasing global demand for energy and the significant economic and environmental implications of pipeline failures, robust monitoring strategies have become essential for ensuring pipeline safety and reliability. The integration of various sensor technologies, such as acoustic, vibration, strain, and temperature sensors, offers unparalleled opportunities for augmenting pipeline monitoring capabilities. However, traditional monitoring approaches often rely on isolated sensor systems, leading to information silos and reduced situational awareness. To address this limitation, this research paper proposes a novel sensor fusion framework for synergistically combining data from multiple sources, modalities, and levels of observation. The proposed framework capitalizes on machine learning and artificial intelligence techniques to develop predictive models that can identify potential pipeline anomalies, faults, and failures in real-time. By leveraging advanced signal processing and data analytics methods, the framework enables the extraction of context-aware features and the creation of high-fidelity models that can accurately predict the state of the pipeline. The research further validates the efficacy of the proposed framework through simulation-based studies and real-world case studies, demonstrating its potential for enhancing pipeline monitoring, reducing maintenance costs, and improving overall pipeline reliability.

title: Train and Test Tightness of LP Relaxations in Structured Prediction
Abstract: This paper examines the train and test tightness of linear programming (LP) relaxations in structured prediction tasks. While tight LP relaxations are known to be a powerful tool for tackling structured prediction problems, existing research has mostly focused on analyzing their performance on certain types of problems or with specific model architectures. In contrast, this work takes a step back to investigate the fundamental question of how well LP relaxations generalize from their training to unseen test data. To this end, a new taxonomy is proposed for describing the properties of LP relaxations that influence their generalization, and a comprehensive empirical study is conducted to evaluate the relationship between these properties and the test tightness of the relaxations. The study involves a wide range of structured prediction tasks, including but not limited to natural language processing, computer vision, and machine learning. Through extensive experiments and comparisons of state-of-the-art models, it is demonstrated that certain regularity characteristics in the optimized patterns of the LP solutions, often undervalued, are instrumental in contributing to the test tightness of these relaxations.

title: Learning in Auctions: Regret is Hard, Envy is Easy
Abstract: This paper endeavors to provide a comprehensive analysis of regret and envy in learning auctions, shedding light on the complexities and competitiveness inherent in these scenarios. The pervasive presence of these emotions in human interactions often renders decision-making frameworks ineffective in multi-agent environments where information is asymmetrical. In the context of auctions, both regret and envy possess unrelenting and profound impacts on bidder behavior. While regret frequently entices individuals to bid higher, a sentiment grounded in the fear of losing or missing out, envy conversely fuels counterproductive behavior as bidders succumb to the urge to outdo their competitors. An in-depth study reveals the dual conundrums inherent in these emotions - regret is a notoriously difficult emotion to optimize for because understanding the intricacies of human psychology often eludes machine learning systems, while simultaneously, envy presents itself as a malleable factor susceptible to exploitation through targeted bidding strategies. By embracing and addressing these seemingly conflicting emotional dynamics, researchers have made some recent headway, paving the way for novel insights into auction learning. The study here will scrutinize the theoretical foundation of regret and envy in auctions and illustrate how game-theoretic frameworks can foster better problem-solving strategies.

title: Co-Clustering Network-Constrained Trajectory Data
Abstract: This study introduces a novel framework for co-clustering network-constrained trajectory data, leveraging the strengths of both network embedding and community detection techniques. Typically, trajectory data is collected from objects moving through a spatial network, often represented as a graph or spatial-road network. However, traditional clustering methods struggle to identify meaningful patterns and groups when dealing with such data, particularly when confronted with geographical features and network constraints influencing the trajectories of moving objects. Existing co-clustering approaches usually rely on network information jointly with a spatial perspective but fall short in accurately learning community structures from such spatial networks. Our proposed framework, coined SCN-COC, concurrently clusters both spatial nodes and associated trajectory vectors, encapsulating the significance of spatial context, network information, and node representations. By injecting spatial features into the embedding of each node and incorporating topological constraints during clustering, SCN-COC presents effective representation of network-constrained trajectory data while retaining spatial characteristics. Furthermore, leveraging our clustering model's predictive capacity, we analyze the community properties of the embedded spatial nodes within the network structure. Ultimately, these results demonstrate substantial promise for enhancing network-explored trajectory data analysis and spatial-driven decision-making within urban planning, traffic modeling, and resource allocation.

title: Algorithm Portfolios for Noisy Optimization
Abstract: Algorithm portfolios for noisy optimization provide an alternative to traditional single- algorithm approaches by combining ensemble methods with adaptive selection strategies to mitigate the effects of noisy fitness landscapes. This research proposes a novel framework for constructing algorithm portfolios that navigate noisy optimization problems, leveraging the strengths of different algorithms and exploiting their complementary search behaviors to achieve more robust and efficient search. By decomposing the optimization process into multiple stages, each sampled from a different distribution, the proposed framework is capable of capturing a broader range of solution landscapes and identifying promising areas of the search space more effectively. Furthermore, the adaptive selection strategy implemented in this framework enables it to dynamically adjust the weighting of different algorithms based on the quality of their samples, allowing it to adapt to changing fitness landscapes and learn from its own experiences throughout the optimization process. Experimental results on a range of benchmark problems demonstrate the potential of the proposed framework to outperform both single-algorithm and ensemble-based approaches, even in the presence of significant levels of noise and uncertainty. The results also highlight the importance of carefully selecting and combining algorithms in noisy optimization problems, as well as the need for more sophisticated selection mechanisms that can adapt to the changing characteristics of the search landscape.

title: Learn on Source, Refine on Target:A Model Transfer Learning Framework with Random Forests
Abstract:
This abstract provides an overview of a comprehensive model transfer learning framework called "Learn on Source, Refine on Target (LoSTR) with Random Forests." Our proposed framework offers a novel approach to model transfer learning, enabling the efficient utilization of pre-trained models for facilitating quick adaptation to a target domain. The core idea behind LoSTR lies in leveraging a pre-trained source domain model to learn the representation of features while simultaneously refining its structure to fit the target task. This synergy is achieved through a carefully designed amalgamation of transfer learning and fine-tuning techniques, offering an adaptive approach that balances the exploitation of rich source domain knowledge with the minimization of the risk of overfitting.

Our framework is predicated upon the Random Forests algorithm, a highly versatile and robust method for feature learning and classification. By using Random Forests as the backbone, LoSTR successfully navigates the complexities of model transfer learning, including dataset shifts, feature mismatches, and varying levels of label scarcity. Furthermore, LoSTR integrates advanced data augmentation techniques to supplement the source domain data and tackle issues associated with limited data availability, thereby guaranteeing a smooth and efficient adaptation process to the target domain. Evaluation carried out on various benchmark datasets verifies the efficacy and robustness of LoSTR, showcasing its potential as a universally applicable framework for many real-world transfer learning applications.

title: Understanding symmetries in deep networks
Abstract: Deep neural networks have emerged as a cornerstone of modern computer vision and machine learning, achieving exceptional performance in a wide range of tasks, including image classification, object detection, and segmentation. A key to their success lies in their compositional nature, which enables the creation of complex hierarchical feature representations from simple building blocks. One fundamental property of these deep networks that underlies their behavior is the presence of symmetries, which manifest as invariances or equivariant properties under various transformations, such as translations, rotations, and scalings. The understanding and manipulation of these symmetries are crucial for developing more interpretable and robust neural networks. However, analyzing symmetries in deep networks is a challenging task due to their high complexity and the presence of many interacting components. This work aims to shed light on the role of symmetries in deep networks, by identifying key structural and dynamical properties that underlie their behavior. Using a combination of theoretical and numerical tools, we will investigate the relationships between symmetry, invariance, and learning in deep networks, and explore strategies for harnessing these symmetries to improve the performance and interpretability of neural networks. By gaining a deeper understanding of symmetries in deep networks, we hope to pave the way for the development of more effective and transparent machine learning models.
