title: An intelligent extension of Variable Neighbourhood Search for labelling graph problems
Abstract: This research proposes an intelligent extension of the Variable Neighbourhood Search (VNS) algorithm, specifically tailored for tackling labelling graph problems. Labelling graph problems involve assigning labels to graph vertices based on given constraints, aiming to satisfy conditions such as connectivity and separation. The proposed intelligent extension, referred to as VNS-lg, incorporates a novel neighbourhood structure that leverages graph-theoretic properties to efficiently explore the solution space. By adaptively adjusting the neighbourhood radius and incorporating a learning mechanism to update the neighbourhood structure, VNS-lg is designed to efficiently handle problems with complex constraints, diverse solution structures, and varying graph sizes. The proposed approach also integrates a compact and interpretable representation scheme for labelling graph problems, enabling easier solution visualization and understanding. Through a series of mathematical proofs, theory-driven computational experiments, and case studies on benchmark instances, this research demonstrates the effectiveness of the VNS-lg algorithm for solving labelling graph problems. Results highlight significant improvements in solution quality, computational efficiency, and adaptability when compared to existing VNS variants and other state-of-the-art labelling algorithm. The novel hybrid framework and insights gained from this work aim to bridge the gap between VNS variants and labelling graph problems, providing a powerful tool for a wide range of applications, including planning, scheduling, network topology inference, and social network analysis.

title: Approximation and Heuristic Algorithms for Probabilistic Physical Search on General Graphs
Abstract: This paper investigates approximation and heuristic algorithms for solving probabilistic physical search problems on general graphs. In this domain, a source node with a non-perfect fuel supply is located at a particular node within a general graph, and the goal is to probabilistically traverse the graph to a target node before exhausting the available fuel. The authors develop novel approximation algorithms that accurately estimate a near-optimal solution, with a bounded increase in objective function value compared to the optimal solution. Furthermore, this paper presents a range of efficient heuristic algorithms that leverage local search and tabu search methods, exploiting domain-specific constraints. An extensive experimental evaluation demonstrates the efficacy of the proposed algorithms on diverse graph instances and fuel capacities, exhibiting strong performance in terms of solution quality and computation time compared to existing methods. A comprehensive analysis of the performance gains achieved by the proposed approximation and heuristic algorithms is presented, including a comparison with the state-of-the-art exact algorithms. The results show a significant improvement in scalability and solution quality, making the proposed heuristics suitable for tackling complex probabilistic physical search problems on large-scale general graphs. The findings of this work have significant implications for various real-world applications, including autonomous robots, ambient assisted living, and surveillance systems.

title: Optimal Release Time Decision from Fuzzy Mathematical Programming Perspective
Abstract: This paper investigates the optimal release time decision-making from a fuzzy mathematical programming perspective to cope with the uncertainties inherent in complex projects. Fuzzy mathematical programming is utilized to model the vague and imprecise relationships between project parameters and the project release time. By employing trapezoidal fuzzy numbers and an integrated fuzzy decision-making approach, this study develops a framework that enables project managers to robustly identify the optimal release time. The investigation considers multiple key performance indicators, including development time, cost, quality, and customer satisfaction, which are often conflicting requirements in project management. A case study of a large-scale construction project is employed to exemplify the practical application of the proposed framework. The results demonstrate that the fuzzy mathematical programming approach effectively captures the uncertainties and complexities of project parameters, leading to more accurate estimates of the optimal release time. Furthermore, the sensitivity analysis of the framework reveals the impact of varying parameters on the optimal release time, providing project managers with valuable insights for making informed decisions. The outcome of this study offers practical suggestions for project managers and contributes to the development of fuzzy mathematical programming applications in project management.

title: Discovery and Visualization of Nonstationary Causal Models
Abstract: Abstract: Nonstationary causal models, which can adapt to changing relationships between variables over time, have garnered significant attention in recent years due to their ability to improve the accuracy and robustness of predictions in dynamic environments. However, discovering and visualizing such complex models remains a challenging task, particularly when faced with large datasets and sparse data. This paper introduces a novel approach that leverages statistical learning techniques and graph embedding methods to identify causal relationships in nonstationary systems. Our method, named Causal-Edge, employs a time-series clustering algorithm to segment data into temporally homogeneous clusters, followed by a gradient boosting model to detect causal relationships within each cluster. To facilitate visualization, we develop a custom graph layout algorithm that incorporates temporal information, enabling users to intuitively understand the evolution of causal relationships over time. Our comprehensive evaluation, based on both simulated and real-world datasets, demonstrates that Causal-Edge outperforms state-of-the-art methods in terms of accuracy, robustness, and interpretability. The results of this study have significant implications for various fields, such as economics, finance, and public health, where nonstationary causal models can provide crucial insights into complex phenomena and inform data-driven decision-making.

title: Training Deep Networks with Structured Layers by Matrix Backpropagation
Abstract: Traditionally, training deep neural networks focuses on optimizing the weights and biases in fully connected or convolutional layers, often in isolation from other layer types such as recurrent or attention mechanisms. Recent advancements in deep learning have shown that introducing structured layers within a neural network can lead to improved performance and efficiency. Structured layers offer the potential for learning complex patterns, achieving efficient computation, and exploiting recent advancements in attention and memory mechanisms. However, integrating these benefits within the framework of backpropagation remains a research challenge, notably how to address the complexities that arise when different layers learn patterns of various structures and patterns. This research works revolves around introducing matrix backpropagation, an unconventional yet remarkably useful approach that aims to make training neural networks with structured layers more practical. By leveraging matrix factorization techniques and exploiting properties of orthogonal and symmetrical matrices, we could establish an efficient method that circumvents traditional backpropagation limitations with deep, heterogeneous networks and hence permits their wider practical use in real-world applications.

title: Deep Multimodal Embedding: Manipulating Novel Objects with Point-clouds, Language and Trajectories
Abstract: This paper proposes an innovative approach to deep multimodal embedding, enabling the manipulation of novel objects using a combination of point clouds, language inputs, and trajectory representations. Building upon recent advancements in computer vision and natural language processing, we have developed a unified deep learning framework that integrates three primary modalities – visual, linguistic, and kinematic – to learn a shared embedding space. The visual modality is represented by 3D point clouds, enabling the model to capture complex object geometries, whereas the linguistic modality is captured through text descriptions of objects, facilitating the understanding of object meanings and functions. The kinematic modality is represented by object trajectories, encoding the dynamics of object behavior and motion patterns. By jointly training these modalities, our approach learns a compact and informative multimodal representation that can generalize across various object categories and scenarios. This paper demonstrates the potential of our framework by evaluating its performance on a novel object manipulation task, where the model must predict optimal trajectories for placing objects in a grasping challenge. Our results show that the proposed approach outperforms state-of-the-art methods in object recognition, manipulation, and imitation learning tasks, leading to a significant advancement in the field of multimodal learning and robotics.

title: Computational Intelligence Challenges and Applications on Large-Scale Astronomical Time Series Databases
Abstract: This paper delves into the realm of computational intelligence and its application to the intricate task of analyzing large-scale astronomical time series databases, encompassing a multitude of challenges and opportunities for innovation. As the field of astronomy continues to advance, the sheer magnitude and complexity of astronomical time series data pose significant hurdles in terms of data management, processing, and pattern recognition. Consequently, computational intelligence techniques are being increasingly integrated into data analysis pipelines to mitigate these challenges, leveraging the power of machine learning, neural networks, and other advanced algorithms to uncover meaningful insights from this vast and intricate data repository. With the primary focus on understanding the impact of solar activity on Earth's climate using longitudinal datasets, this research undertakes an extensive investigation of various computational intelligence methods for filtering noise, identifying patterns, and predicting future trends in astronomical time series data, thereby opening up avenues for breakthrough discoveries in astrophysics and climatology. The study, based on a case study using the Solar and Heliospheric Observatory (SOHO) and the Mauna Loa Observatory's Solar Radiation dataset, examines the efficacy of these applied computational intelligence methods against conventional statistical techniques, demonstrating their robustness and scalability in handling large datasets.

title: Feature Evaluation of Deep Convolutional Neural Networks for Object Recognition and Detection
Abstract: Object recognition and detection in images have garnered significant attention in the field of computer vision, and deep convolutional neural networks (CNNs) have emerged as a prominent approach for achieving state-of-the-art performance. The key to the success of CNNs lies in their ability to learn hierarchical features from input images, allowing them to capture complex patterns and relationships. However, with the growing complexity of CNN architectures, the process of evaluating the feature representations learned by these networks has become increasingly important. This paper presents a comprehensive study on the evaluation of deep CNNs for object recognition and detection, with a focus on understanding the significance of different layers and feature extraction mechanisms. By using various evaluation metrics, such as feature saliency, classification performance, and detection accuracy, we investigate the impact of different feature extraction techniques, including convolutional, pooling, and normalization layers, on the performance of CNNs. Our results demonstrate the importance of carefully designing and tuning the feature extraction mechanisms in CNNs to achieve optimal performance, and highlight the need for a more robust and principled approach to feature evaluation in deep learning. The findings of this study have implications for the development of more efficient and effective deep CNN architectures for object recognition and detection tasks, and contribute to a deeper understanding of the role of feature representation in the success of CNNs.

title: Constructing Abstraction Hierarchies Using a Skill-Symbol Loop
Abstract: This paper presents an approach to constructing abstraction hierarchies for complex cognitive tasks by exploiting the interplay between symbolic and skill-based representations. The proposed technique, known as the Skill-Symbol Loop (SSL) framework, is designed to iteratively refine and expand abstraction hierarchies in a way that is adaptive to the task's requirements and the learner's skills. At the core of the SSL framework lies a two-way loop where symbolic reasoning processes continuously cross-reference and refine skill-based representations of the task, while simultaneously triggering skill acquisition and practice to fill knowledge gaps. By dynamically adjusting the abstraction hierarchy to match the learner's evolving skill profile, the SSL framework provides a robust mechanism for developing more accurate and nuanced abstractions that can better inform decision-making under uncertainty. Empirical evaluations using a suite of cognitive tasks reveal significant improvements in abstraction accuracy and efficiency, compared to traditional methods that rely on pre-defined abstraction hierarchies. The results demonstrate the potential of the SSL framework to mitigate the abstraction hierarchy's fragility and instability in complex and dynamic environments, making it a valuable tool for intelligent systems and cognitive architectures in numerous fields. Furthermore, the proposed approach could have important implications for human-robot collaboration, skill acquisition, and adaptive decision-making.

title: Linear-time Learning on Distributions with Approximate Kernel Embeddings
Abstract: This work delves into the realm of distribution learning, specifically focusing on developing linear-time learning algorithms that can handle complex distributions. Traditional approaches to learning distributions often rely on expensive kernel computations, which limit their applicability to large-scale datasets. To address this challenge, we introduce a novel framework that leverages approximate kernel embeddings to approximate the input distribution. Our proposed method, dubbed Kernel Approximation for Distribution Learning (KADL), utilizes a variant of the Nyström method to efficiently approximate the kernel matrix, thereby reducing the computational cost of kernel-based learning. By doing so, we enable learning on distributions with significantly lower computational overhead. We demonstrate the effectiveness of KADL through rigorous theoretical analysis and extensive empirical evaluations on benchmark datasets, showcasing its performance competitiveness with, if not surpassing, state-of-the-art methods in various distribution learning tasks. Our results highlight the potential of KADL to revolutionize distribution learning in real-world applications, where scalability and efficiency are paramount. Furthermore, we explore the limitations of KADL and discuss avenues for future research to further optimize its performance and improve its robustness.

title: Speech Dereverberation in the STFT Domain
Abstract: Speech dereverberation is a critical problem in signal processing that aims to recast convolutive reverberation, characterized by the interaction of sound reflections and the direct sound, into simply additive components. This study explores a novel approach to speech dereverberation based on the short-time Fourier transform (STFT) domain, where the reverberant speech signal is decomposed into multiple frequency bins in order to manage the reverberation. By performing spectral subtraction on these frequency bins through either frequency domain enhanced speech degradation or frequency domain spectral amplitude modification, the study aimed to discern the direct and reverberant components separately and effectively restore a clean speech signal to the desired level. Experiments conducted on an ensemble of test datasets revealed that application of inverse mel filterbank to unsharp masking for de-reverberation showed impressive results. Estimations have shown average suppression level of reverberation at 90% while maintaining 4 dB in signal-to-noise ratio to demonstrate the feasibility and fidelity of this frequency domain approach. This result exhibited the influence of frequency domain strategy on performance, where the signal-to-noise ratio to reverberation output effectively revealed robustness. The output results of this research demonstrate promising options for design and application in real-time conferencing settings.

title: CRDT: Correlation Ratio Based Decision Tree Model for Healthcare Data Mining
Abstract: This study presents a novel Correlation Ratio Based Decision Tree (CRDT) model specifically designed for efficient data mining in the healthcare domain. The conventional decision tree algorithms are plagued by oversimplification and inconsistency issues when dealing with multi-scale and nonlinear relationships inherent in healthcare datasets. To address these concerns, this research integrates Correlation Ratio (CR), a measure of dependence and heterogeneity, into the Decision Tree algorithm to retain vital information in intricate medical datasets. Employing Entropy and Conditional Entropy reduction-based feature selection aims to minimize the dimensionality of the data while preserving the utmost diagnostic information. Such advancements empower the model to grasp highly nonlinear relationships between health features, and thus accurately predict clinical conditions. Experiments on distinctive clinical datasets validate the efficacy of CRDT, displaying superior performance over the state-of-the-art decision tree and ensemble methodologies. CRDT accomplishes improved predictive power while being robust against high dimensionality, missing values, and overfitting, making it an attractive alternative for healthcare data mining. By harnessing CRDT, data-driven healthcare solutions can effectively discern high-stakes therapeutic, preventive, and prognostic insights, ultimately aiding clinicians and researchers in optimizing personalized care. Furthermore, an in-depth theoretical discussion is presented to provide a solid understanding of the intrinsic workings of CRDT, supplementing the technical material to foster further investigations in the field of healthcare data science.

title: Exploration and Exploitation of Victorian Science in Darwin's Reading Notebooks
Abstract: This study delves into the under-examined aspect of Charles Darwin's reading notebooks to investigate how he navigated the scientific landscape of Victorian Britain, characterized by an explosion of new scientific theories, discoveries, and disciplines. Darwin's reading notebooks, a collection of annotated texts and marginalia spanning decades, offer a unique window into his intellectual processes and reading habits, shedding light on his exploration of natural history, geology, botany, and the nascent fields of evolutionary biology and anthropology. By examining the notebooks from 1831 to 1863, this research reveals that Darwin selectively engaged with the works of prominent scientists of his age, from Sir Charles Lyell's uniformitarian geology to Alfred Russel Wallace's early theories on species variation. This selective engagement facilitated both the exploration of new ideas and the exploitation of their relevance to his own intellectual pursuits. As Darwin navigated the rapidly evolving scientific landscape, his notebooks reflect a dialectical tension between the desire for novelty and the need to reconcile competing theories. By situating Darwin's reading notebooks within their historical and intellectual context, this study aims to contribute to our understanding of the social and cognitive dynamics underlying the development of scientific theories, particularly in the context of Victorian science, where the boundaries between disciplines were still fluid and ever-shifting.

title: Quantification of sand fraction from seismic attributes using Neuro-Fuzzy approach
Abstract: This study presents a novel approach to quantify sand fraction from seismic attributes using a Neuro-Fuzzy methodology. Traditional seismic interpretation relies heavily on the experience and expertise of interpreters, often resulting in subjective and variable results. To address this limitation, a Neuro-Fuzzy system is proposed to integrate expert knowledge and seismic attributes to automate sand fraction prediction. The Neuro-Fuzzy system, comprising a Radial Basis Function (RBF) neural network and a Mamdani fuzzy inference system, is trained with a dataset containing seismic attributes and corresponding sand fractions from well logs. The proposed approach utilizes a genetic algorithm for RBF network architecture optimization and for the fuzzy membership function parameters to ensure optimal system performance. The results indicate a significant improvement in sand fraction estimation, with enhanced accuracy and reduced variability compared to traditional methods. The Neuro-Fuzzy system demonstrates its ability to generalize to unseen data, resulting in robust performance across various seismic scenarios. This research demonstrates the potential of Neuro-Fuzzy methodologies to enhance seismic interpretation and support more accurate sand fraction prediction, ultimately contributing to more reliable reservoir characterization and resource estimation.

title: Boolean Hedonic Games
Abstract: Boolean hedonic games are a class of cooperative game that extends the traditional cooperative game theory by incorporating the concept of player's preferences over the coalition they form. These games involve a set of players having different preferences and capabilities, making it crucial to understand the formation of coalitions and their impact on the overall outcome. This paper examines the properties and solutions of Boolean hedonic games, where players have Boolean queries over their coalition members, with true or false preferences. The games are defined as a pair of a set of players and a preference relation on the power set of these players, where each player's preference gives the acceptance of the coalition in terms of a Boolean query. The query, which serves as the basis of the player's preference, is either accepted or rejected, and in the event of rejection, a simple strategy for each player needs to be employed for reaching an agreement. The main focus of this paper lies in characterizing the Boolean hedonic games, classifying them, and proposing efficient solution concepts, such as competitive and cooperative equilibria, for them. The outcome of this work is a comprehensive framework for handling complex problems in areas of group decision-making, coalition formation, and cooperative games.

title: Designing Behaviour in Bio-inspired Robots Using Associative Topologies of Spiking-Neural-Networks
Abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to designing behaviour in bio-inspired robots utilizing associative topologies of spiking-neural-networks (SNNs). By leveraging the principles of neuroplasticity and synaptic plasticity, we propose a framework for adaptative reconfiguration of SNNs in real-time, enabling robots to learn and exhibit complex behaviours through self-organization. The key idea is to employ a network of interconnected SNNs, where each module represents a spatially distributed population of neurons, to model a behaviourally-relevant cognitive process. The proposed framework capitalizes on the associative properties of SNNs to dynamically reorganize the connections between modules, allowing the robot to adapt and learn from its environment. This is achieved through a bio-inspired learning rule, inspired by long-term potentiation and long-term depression, which facilitates synaptic plasticity and allows the network to refine its connectivity based on experience. Simulation results demonstrate the effective adoption of complex natural-like navigation within the systems and furthermore show how reorganization facilitates learning of increasingly complex navigational scenarios, outperforming comparable non-adaptive counterparts in terms of both navigation speed and efficiency. Experimental validation on a robotic platform, showcases the potential of the framework as a fundamental component for the development of goal-oriented autonomous behaviour in robots.

title: A Survey of Digital Privacy Rights Under CISA
Abstract: This paper provides a comprehensive analysis of the digital privacy rights of individuals and organizations under the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA), a federal agency tasked with protecting the United States' critical infrastructure from cyber threats. With the increasing reliance on digital technologies and the subsequent rise in cyber-attacks, there is a growing need to balance individual and organizational digital privacy rights with the need for effective cybersecurity measures. The CISA's directives and guidelines on cybersecurity practices, while intended to enhance national cybersecurity, raise concerns about the potential infringement on digital privacy rights. This paper scrutinizes key provisions under the CISA that may impact digital privacy rights, including the mandatory vulnerability disclosure guidelines, the Secure Cloud Services initiative, and the Continuous Diagnostics and Mitigation (CDM) program. It assesses the impact of these measures on individual and organizational digital privacy, and examines the current regulatory framework that ensures a proper balance between the protection of national security interests and the safeguarding of digital privacy rights. Furthermore, the study explores the recent changes brought about by the Cybersecurity and For the People Act of 2020, which may redefine the CISA's role in national cybersecurity and potentially impact digital privacy rights. Through a critical analysis and examination of current cases and the legislative landscape, this paper aims to offer insights on the digital privacy rights under the CISA and contribute to ongoing debates on the nature of this dynamic relationship.

title: The Ethics of Hacking: Should It Be Taught?
Abstract: The ethics of hacking has become a pressing concern, particularly in the context of modern cybersecurity. With the increasing prevalence of hacking incidents, there is a growing need to educate individuals on the ethical implications of hacking. However, this raises a pressing question: should hacking be taught in educational institutions? Proponents of hacking education argue that by teaching students the principles of hacking, we can equip them with the skills necessary to protect our digital assets and infrastructure from malicious attacks. On the other hand, critics contention that teaching hacking techniques can create a generation of would-be hackers, perpetuating a cycle of crime. This dichotomy highlights the complexity of the issue and necessitates a nuanced investigation into the ethics of hacking education. This study seeks to provide a comprehensive analysis of the arguments for and against teaching hacking, including the perspectives of educators, policymakers, and industry experts. By examining the historical development of hacking as a discipline, the current state of hacking education, and the potential impacts on society, this research aims to provide a thoughtful and informed contribution to the ongoing debate. Ultimately, this study aims to shed light on the most effective ways to balance the need for cybersecurity awareness with the potential risks associated with teaching hacking techniques.

title: HTML5 Zero Configuration Covert Channels: Security Risks and Challenges
Abstract: This paper delves into the previously undiscovered and unexplored security risks posed by HTML5 zero-configuration covert channels. Despite the increasing adoption of HTML5 for web development, its security implications have largely been overlooked. By leveraging its underlying protocol features and APIs, attackers can potentially exploit these covert channels to subvert data confidentiality, integrity, and authenticity. We identify and demonstrate three main types of HTML5 zero-configuration covert channels, including storage-based, communication-based, and metadata-based channels. These channels can be used to extract sensitive information, inject malicious scripts, and bypass existing security controls. By performing a thorough analysis of the HTML5 specification and common web development practices, our research reveals a range of vulnerabilities and misconfigurations that can be exploited by attackers. Furthermore, we assess the security risks and challenges associated with these covert channels, including their potential impact on user privacy, data security, and overall web application security. Our findings highlight the need for web developers, security researchers, and organizations to be aware of these risks and to take proactive measures to mitigate them. By developing and implementing robust security measures, we can prevent the exploitation of HTML5 zero-configuration covert channels and ensure the secure development of web applications.

title: Interception in Distance-Vector Routing Networks
Abstract: This paper delves into the realm of distance-vector routing networks, specifically targeting the phenomenon of interception attacks, which substantially undermine the security, reliability, and trustworthiness of these networks. Distance-vector routing protocols, used in many modern network infrastructures, rely on their peers to convey information about the available paths and distances between nodes. However, an adversary initiating an interception attack can jeopardize the integrity of the network by manipulating routing information and convincing neighboring nodes to redirect traffic through unwanted sources or sinks. To counter this threat, researchers and practitioners have proposed detection methods based on anomaly detection, traffic analysis, and robustness verification. These proposals include constructing monitoring systems to scrutinize traffic patterns, developing trust metrics to distinguish between genuine and synthetic routing information, and devising techniques for estimating the propagation speed of routing information in the entire network. By integrating these diverse approaches, researchers aim to devise effective tools and mechanisms that facilitate quick detection and reaction to interception attacks in distance-vector routing networks, thereby bolstering their robustness and overall security.

title: Protection and Deception: Discovering Game Theory and Cyber Literacy through a Novel Board Game Experience
Abstract: This study explores the intersection of game theory, cybersecurity, and education through the design and implementation of a novel board game experience. By merging these seemingly disparate fields, the game aims to foster an in-depth understanding of strategic decision-making in the context of online protection and deception. Researchers posit that the complex and dynamic nature of cyber threats necessitates a nuanced approach to education, emphasizing the need for experiential learning to supplement traditional teaching methods. Through the development and testing of the board game, the study delves into the efficacy of this novel approach to teaching cybersecurity fundamentals and game theory concepts. The game's underlying mechanics are grounded in insights from psychology and cognitive science, aiming to cultivate a profound understanding of human decision-making and information processing in uncertain environments. title: Towards a Systematic View on Cybersecurity Ecology
Abstract: Cybersecurity has emerged as a pressing concern in today's interconnected world, with a plethora of emerging threats and vulnerabilities. Comprising of networks, systems, and organizations, a cybersecurity ecosystem comprises various components, including humans, physical devices, and software. This research aims to delve into an ecological perspective on cybersecurity, defining a hypothetical model of interconnected elements that impact an organization's vulnerability and resilience. The ecosystem view encourages stakeholders to consider the interactions and interdependencies between human, process, technology, environment, and organization - the five pillars of cybersecurity ecology. This requires understanding of the complex network of relationships that shape an ecosystem, thus enabling ecologists, managers, and practitioners to make informed decisions. It also requires understanding the intricate balance that must be achieved to preserve the resilience and security of the ecosystem. Drawing on ecology's well-established principles and theories, we establish a foundational framework that highlights the organizational capacity for resilience under threat and the interconnected nature of cybersecurity efforts. Our study contributes to current debates in information security, presenting insights on a new avenue for addressing vulnerabilities and bolstering the ecosystem's resilience against cyber threats and threats in general.

title: Security Toolbox for Detecting Novel and Sophisticated Android Malware
Abstract: This paper introduces a novel security toolbox, dubbed "AndroDetect," designed to effectively detect sophisticated and novel Android malware. AndroDetect employs a hybrid approach, seamlessly integrating static, dynamic, and machine learning-based analysis techniques to provide a comprehensive threat detection framework. Through static analysis, the toolbox scrutinizes app binary files for suspicious codes and behavioral patterns, while dynamic analysis relies on emulator-based execution to identify malicious activities during runtime. Additionally, machine learning algorithms are utilized to categorize and annotate suspicious behaviors, which are then employed to train and improve the model over time. AndroDetect's arsenal is further augmented by an advanced feature extraction engine that identifies obfuscated and self-modifying codes, ensuring that even the most sophisticated malware strains are caught. The toolbox's effectiveness has been empirically confirmed through extensive experiments involving a vast dataset of known malwares, demonstrating a detection rate of 97.5% and a false positive rate of 2.1%. Furthermore, AndroDetect has been successfully applied in real-world scenarios, showcasing significant potential as an essential tool for Android security audit and analysis.

title: Controlled Data Sharing for Collaborative Predictive Blacklisting
Abstract: This paper investigates the challenges and potential solutions of implementing controlled data sharing for collaborative predictive blacklisting. As the increasing threat of cyber attacks demands a collective effort from cybersecurity professionals, it becomes apparent that information sharing is a critical component of a more effective defense strategy. However, current data sharing practices often raise concerns regarding data privacy, ownership, and the lack of a unified framework for sharing sensitive security-related information. Building on existing work in this area, this research proposes a novel data sharing framework focused on predictive blacklisting, a crucial component of modern cybersecurity infrastructures. This framework addresses the trade-off between data sharing and data protection by introducing a dynamic access control system and utilizing innovative data anonymization techniques to maintain a balance between information disclosure and confidentiality. Furthermore, our solution incorporates trusted third-party agents, multi-party computation and secure multi-party protocols, to ensure data authenticity and reliability. A comprehensive evaluation of our proposed framework is conducted through a set of simulations and experiments, demonstrating its efficiency, scalability, and security. This work highlights the potential of collaborative data sharing in predictive blacklisting and provides insights into creating a more robust and adaptive cybersecurity defense system, paving the way for future research in this direction.

title: Emergent Behavior in Cybersecurity
Abstract: Emergent behavior in cybersecurity refers to complex and unpredictable patterns of interaction that arise from the dynamic interactions among various components, networks, and systems. In the context of cybersecurity, emergent behavior often manifests as novel attacks, vulnerabilities, and threats that cannot be anticipated by solely examining individual system components or network structures. These emergent phenomena are frequently driven by the continuous evolution of malware, sophisticated social engineering tactics, and the increasing interconnectedness of modern networks. As a result, traditional security measures and analytical tools often struggle to keep pace with the rapidly changing threat landscape. This research investigates the concept of emergent behavior in cybersecurity, focusing on the underlying factors and mechanisms that give rise to these complex patterns. By examining the intersections of human and artificial intelligence, cryptography, network science, and game theory, we aim to gain a deeper understanding of how emergent behavior in cybersecurity arises and evolves. Furthermore, we explore the implications of emergent behavior for cybersecurity policy, strategy, and practice, with a focus on developing effective defensive and predictive capabilities that can mitigate the risks associated with these complex threats. title: Cybersecurity Dynamics

title: Internet of Things for Residential Areas: Toward Personalized Energy Management Using Big Data
Abstract: The proliferation of Internet of Things (IoT) technology has opened up new avenues for enhancing residential energy management. This paper explores the use of big data techniques to create intelligent energy management systems for residential areas. Our analysis shows that applying advanced big data analytics and machine learning algorithms to residential energy usage data can enable personalized energy management practices, leading to significant reductions in energy consumption and corresponding greenhouse gas emissions. title: Triggered star formation in giant HI supershells: ionized gas
Abstract: Triggered star formation in giant HI supershells likely plays a significant role in the distribution and density of neutral hydrogen (HI), affecting subsequent star-burst activation. Observations of extragalactic HI supershells have indicated a spatial relationship between dense-gas structures created within these supershells and regions of intense star formation. The ionized gas within supershells, the endproduct of previous high-mass star activity, can disrupt the large-scale dynamics of gas distribution. title: Group Centric Networking: A New Approach for Wireless Multi-Hop Networking to Enable the Internet of Things
Abstract: Group centric networking is a novel approach that has been proposed to overcome the limitations of traditional wireless multi-hop networking in the context of the Internet of Things (IoT). In traditional wireless multi-hop networking, nodes in the network forward data packets towards the destination based on their location and hop count. However, this approach becomes impractical as the number of IoT devices grows, due to the resulting interference, high latency and the resulting decreased power efficiency. Group centric networking is a more efficient and scalable solution that views the network as a collection of distinct groups with designated gateways, rather than a network of individual nodes. In this approach, nodes transmit data packets to the nearest gateway in their group, rather than directly to the destination node, exploiting spatial diversity and better utilizing available bandwidth. As a result, overall network performance is significantly enhanced, with reduced interference, lower latency, and increased power efficiency, making it more suitable for the IoT where devices often operate with limited power supplies and are geographically scattered over large areas. Since the design focuses on maintaining groups' stability and network connectivity as key architectural traits., numerous IoT applications can benefit such features of this particular approach.

The research centers on exploring the relationships between these complex sequences and prime numbers, aiming to uncover novel patterns and phenomena associated with such recurrences. By investigating properties like divisibility by higher powers of primes, the emergence of periodic patterns, and the relationship between the initial conditions and subsequent terms, we gain a deeper understanding of the intricate behavior of these sequences. The theoretical foundations of linear recurrences and number theory serve as the groundwork for developing new insights and theorems that illuminate the underlying mechanisms governing these sequences. Through a combination of mathematical derivations, computational verifications, and insightful analyses, we establish novel connections between prime power divisibility, periodicity, and combinatorial properties of binary strings, and reveal intriguing links to the binomial expansion, resulting in a comprehensive treatment of the subject matter that not only advances the current understanding of second-order recurrences but also opens up new avenues for investigation and future research.

title: Are Compton-Thick AGN the Missing Link Between Mergers and Black Hole Growth?
Abstract: Compton-thick Active Galactic Nuclei (AGN) are extremely luminous yet heavily obscured objects thought to represent the highest accretion states around supermassive black holes (SMBHs). They occupy a critical regime where the torus of dust and gas surrounding the AGN is sufficiently dense to absorb nearly all the radiation produced by the accretion process, rendering them nearly invisible to both optical and X-ray observations. A connection between mergers of galaxies and the triggering of AGN has long been proposed as a fundamental paradigm to explain the growth of SMBHs. However, the presence of Compton-thick AGN in the local universe has largely been overlooked, and their relationship to galaxy mergers remains unclear. Recent studies suggest that Compton-thick AGN may represent a phase of massive black hole growth and fuelling, and potentially a gateway between stellar mass loss and super-Eddington accretion. Using a combination of spectral energy distribution (SED) fitting, multi-wavelength photometry, and hydrodynamical simulations, we investigate the link between galaxy mergers and the emergence of Compton-thick AGN, shedding light on the possible mechanism driving the observed properties of these enigmatic objects. Our research aims to clarify the roles of mass and energy transfer mechanisms in regulating the growth of SMBHs during galaxy interactions, potentially unearthing a crucial "missing link" between mergers and black hole evolution.

title: ptp++: A Precision Time Protocol Simulation Model for OMNeT++ / INET
Abstract: PTP++ is an open-source simulation model designed for OMNeT++ and INET, aiming to accurately replicate the Precision Time Protocol (PTP) in networked systems. PTP is a widely adopted standard for generating and synchronizing timestamp data in layer 2 of the OSI model. The increasing demand for high reliability, flexibility, and scalability in modern networked systems necessitates the inclusion of more comprehensive simulation models. The design of the PTP++ model is centered around capturing the behavior of PTP-enabled devices, particularly the precision time synchronization mechanism, to enable researchers and developers to comprehensively evaluate the performance and limitations of PTP implementations within diverse network configurations. By leveraging OMNeT++ and INET, the PTP++ model can simulate complex networks comprising multiple PTP-enabled devices, allowing users to assess real-world PTP behavior, power consumption patterns, and other critical factors without the need for expensive physical infrastructure. The use of a modular architecture allows users to integrate their custom components or modify existing ones to suit their specific simulation requirements. Overall, the PTP++ model provides an invaluable tool for harnessing the full potential of PTP technology across various networking scenarios and applications, while offering an extremely efficient and scalable simulation environment for large-scale deployments.

title: uIP Support for the Network Simulation Cradle
Abstract: This study explores the integration of user-driven internet protocol (uIP) support within the Network Simulation Environment Cradle (NSE-C) framework. The NSE-C was initially designed to mimic real-world network deployments, allowing researchers and developers to simulate various network topologies and test their system's performance. However, the original implementation relied heavily on idealized IP models that do not accurately reflect real-world network conditions. The proposed addition of uIP support aims to bridge this gap by introducing more realistic and adaptive network behavior within the simulated environment. This enhancement is achieved through the incorporation of IP packet-level simulation, simulation of real-time data streaming, and network performance analysis. The implementation of uIP support in NSE-C is demonstrated through case studies involving various network scenarios, including high-latency satellite connections and IoT sensor networks. Results show significant improvements in simulation accuracy and ability to model real-world network behavior. Furthermore, the introduction of uIP support facilitates the development and testing of applications that rely on IP communications, such as routing protocols and traffic management systems. Overall, this research contributes to the advancement of network simulation technologies by introducing more accurate and realistic models of network behavior, thereby enabling more effective testing and development of network-centric applications.

title: Federating OMNeT++ Simulations with Testbed Environments
Abstract: This abstract presents a novel approach to bridging the gap between simulation-driven research and hands-on experimentation in the context of Network Simulators. Specifically, we focus on OMNeT++, a widely used network simulator, and propose a platform-agnostic federation mechanism to couple OMNeT++ simulations with real-world testbed environments. Our solution leverages the OMNeT++ API and existing testbed management frameworks to provide a seamless integration experience. This enables researchers to execute simulations in tandem with physical experiments, thereby enhancing the validity and generalizability of their results. By facilitating the sharing of data between simulated and real-world testbeds, our framework fosters a more comprehensive understanding of network behavior and characteristics. We demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach through a case study involving the deployment of an OMNeT++ model on a testbed emulator, showcasing its potential for improved network research and development. Key features of our solution include the ability to dynamically spawn Omnet++ simulations in response to testbed events and accommodate various communication protocols. Furthermore, our implementation ensures that the coupling between simulated and real-world environments remains transparent to the end-user, thereby streamlining the development process. Our work aims to contribute to the advancement of next-generation network systems, particularly in the context of the ever-evolving landscape of IoT, Cloud, and 6G networks.

title: On Capacity Formulation with Stationary Inputs and Application to a Bit-Patterned Media Recording Channel Model
Abstract: This paper develops a new approach to formulate the capacity of discrete memoryless channels with stationary input distributions. Theoretical results establish that the treatment of unnormalized and normalized message probability distributions leads to capacity expressions that differ by a single additive term, characterized by the mutual information at the input. This equivalence enables the extension of established capacity bounds to computationally tractable forms that encompass both statistical and deterministic considerations, while accounting for probability space shrinkages induced by input samples' correlations. A capacity lower bound is introduced, known as the effective information bound, which forms a natural upper limit for estimating capacities in discrete memoryless channels under finite alphabet constraints. We apply these advances to analyze the information-theoretic capacity limits of a bit-patterned media recording channel, in which the noise channel is modeled as a compound channel, with statistically interacting outputs and stationary noise inputs. Taking into account probabilistic descriptions of sample correlations and interaction among probabilistic bits, this work provides a unique perspective on studying bit-patterned media recording systems under constrained sampling contexts, ultimately broadening our understanding of channel behavior and the fundamental limits of data storage.

title: A classical postselected weak amplification scheme via thermal light cross-Kerr effect
Abstract: In this paper, we propose and experimentally demonstrate a classical postselected weak amplification scheme via the thermal light cross-Kerr effect. This scheme utilizes the cross-Kerr nonlinearity to achieve heralded amplification of weak coherent states, leveraging the non-classical correlations present in the output of a non-degenerate optical parametric oscillator (OPA). We initially study the properties of the cross-Kerr effect in thermal light and provide a detailed analysis of the amplification process, highlighting its postselection sensitivity and efficiency. The experimental implementation is demonstrated utilising off-the-shelf optical components, reaching an average gain of 2.85 dB for weak coherent states, which is the first time experimentally observed phenomenon of small noise when amplifying states in optics via cross-Kerr effect. Moreover, we systematically investigate the effect of various parameters on the amplification performance, including pump power, input state intensity, and detection threshold. The demonstrated technique exhibits potential advantages over traditional linear optical amplifiers, particularly in applications where optical quantum information is fragile or susceptible to noise. Furthermore, our findings have significant implications for the development of novel optical quantum resources and the exploration of unconventional amplification schemes in both classical and quantum optical communication systems.

title: Two-Dimensional Oxide Topological Insulator With Iron-Pnictide Superconductor LiFeAs Structure
Abstract: The recent discovery of topological insulators has brought significant attention in the field of solid-state physics, as they are able to conduct electricity on their surface while staying insulators on the inside, suggesting a great potential for innovative electronic devices. In pursuit of pushing the boundaries of these unique materials, scientists have been working on the two-dimensional (2D) realization of oxide topological insulators (OTIs). One crucial aspect of achieving this goal is by incorporating superconducting properties to the OTIs. Here, we report on the successful synthesis of a 2D OTI with an iron-pnictide superconductor LiFeAs structure. Through a combination of molecular beam epitaxy (MBE) and pulsed laser deposition (PLD), we were able to deposit high-quality layers of La2-xSrxNiO3 on a SrTiO3 substrate with superconducting LiFeAs thin films above. The unique crystal structure of this hybrid material is characterized by a combination of band inversion from the d-orbitals of Ni and Fe in the LiFeAs layer, yielding a topological band structure as desired. Furthermore, our Raman and Hall effect measurements demonstrate the coexistence of superconductivity with OTI phases. Our results not only showcase the exciting possibility of integrating OTI and iron-pnictide superconducting properties in a single material but also offer insights into the potential applications of this unique class of materials in ultra-low power dissipation electronics and topological quantum computing.

title: Decomposition of Brownian loop-soup clusters
Abstract: This work investigates the decomposition properties of Brownian loop-soup clusters, a collection of intersecting Brownian loops in three-dimensional space. The Brownian loop-soup model is a stochastic process characterized by the sampling of closed paths or loops from a Poissonian ensemble with varying lengths and intensities. Brownian loop-soup clusters emerge as connected aggregates of these loops, exhibiting intricate branch-like structures and possessing self-similar characteristics at various scales. Motivated by recent advances in theoretical and computational analysis, we develop a novel algorithmic framework to systematically decompose Brownian loop-soup clusters into distinct sub-components. Our decomposition approach hinges on the identification and segmentation of loops according to topological properties and geometric features, such as the length, volume, and connectivity of individual loops. Employing a careful computational implementation of this framework, we evaluate the efficacy of our decomposition method in discerning fine-grained structures and patterns within Brownian loop-soup clusters. Ultimately, our research aims to elucidate the intricate mechanisms governing the formation and organization of Brownian loop-soup clusters, shedding new insights into the mathematical and physical underpinnings of stochastic sampling processes in three-dimensional space.

title: On the relation of three theorems of analysis to the axiom of choice
Abstract: The relationship between three fundamental theorems of analysis and the axiom of choice has been a subject of interest among mathematicians for several decades. Specifically, results such as the Banach-Tarski paradox, the Hahn-Banach theorem, and the Lebesgue measure theory have sparked intense debate regarding the necessity of the axiom of choice. On one hand, it is argued that the existence of non-trivial models of set theory where the axiom of choice does not hold could undermine the validity of these theorems, potentially extending the scope of their applications in the broader mathematical landscape. On the other hand, proponents of the axiom of choice propose that without this powerful principle, the development of these theorems could be hindered, rendering certain results and techniques in analysis inaccessible. This study undertakes an in-depth analysis of these interconnected concepts, examining the interplay between Zermelo-Fraenkel set theory, the axiom of choice, and the three aforementioned theorems of analysis. Through a critical examination of key literature and examples, we aim to contribute to the ongoing discourse on the relationship between the axiom of choice and the foundations of analysis, shedding light on the consequences for our understanding of mathematical rigor and the potential implications for research in analysis.

title: Backreaction for Einstein-Rosen waves coupled to a massless scalar field
Abstract: The Einstein-Rosen bridge, a type of wormhole, is a theoretical passage through spacetime connecting two distant regions. When a massless scalar field is introduced into the Einstein-Rosen geometry, the spacetime topology is altered, and the properties of the wormhole are influenced. This paper investigates the backreaction effect, which describes how the Einstein-Rosen waves interact with the coupled massless scalar field, leading to spacetime oscillations and distortions. Utilizing a numerical approach, the interplay between the scalar field and the wormhole geometry is analyzed, focusing on the massless scalar field's influence on the gravitational wave modes and the resulting impact on the wormhole's stability and geometry. The analysis reveals that the coupling between the massless scalar field and the Einstein-Rosen waves induces significant variations in the wormhole's structure, particularly in the throat region, where the gravitational field is stronger. The backreaction effect becomes more pronounced as the amplitude of the scalar field increases, leading to enhanced spacetime oscillations and a destabilization of the wormhole. This study provides new insights into the dynamics of coupled field geometries and has implications for our understanding of gravitational wave interactions with matter and energy in extreme astrophysical environments.

title: Supernovae as cosmological probes
Abstract: Supernovae have emerged as a powerful tool for probing the fundamental properties of the universe, offering a unique window into the underlying cosmology. By harnessing the light from distant explosions, scientists can infer the expansion history, chemical composition, and dynamical properties of the cosmos. Type Ia supernovae (SNe Ia), in particular, have proven to be reliable "standard candles" for measuring distances and probing the acceleration of the universe's expansion. The observation of SNe Ia has led to the conclusion that the universe's expansion is accelerating, driven by a mysterious component known as dark energy. However, the nature of dark energy remains an open question, and continued observations of SNe Ia, as well as other types of supernovae, will be crucial for shedding light on this enigma. The study of supernovae also provides valuable insights into stellar astrophysics, including the final stages of massive star evolution, the explosion mechanisms, and the role of metallicity in shaping the chemical composition of the cosmos. By combining observations with state-of-the-art simulations and theoretical models, researchers can gain a deeper understanding of the complex interplay between supernovae and the early universe. The future of supernova astronomy promises to be replete with new discoveries, innovative techniques, and a deeper understanding of the universe's most violent and spectacular events.

title: Anomaly Detection for malware identification using Hardware Performance Counters
Abstract: This paper delves into the realm of anomaly detection for malware identification by leveraging the capabilities of Hardware Performance Counters (HPCs). HPCs provide a means to monitor and analyze various performance metrics, such as cache misses, branch mispredictions, and instruction pipeline stalls, at the hardware level. By employing machine learning algorithms on these features, we can detect anomalous system behaviors indicative of malicious activity. Specifically, we explore the application of deep learning techniques to identify subtle patterns in system performance that may resonate with malware strains. To demonstrate the feasibility of this approach, we designed and implemented an anomaly detection system that can accurately identify zero-day malware samples by analyzing performance counter data. Our system achieved remarkably high detection rates, with accuracy exceeding 95%. Moreover, we conducted a thorough analysis of the feature importance, revealing significant correlations between HPC features and malware behaviors. These findings provide valuable insights into the essential characteristics that differentiate benign and malicious system activities, underscoring the utility of HPC-based anomaly detection in combating modern malware threats.

title: Graphulo: Linear Algebra Graph Kernels for NoSQL Databases
Abstract:
Graphulo: Linear Algebra Graph Kernels for NoSQL Databases

Graphulo is a proprietary, open-source graph kernel framework pioneered by Graphcore, designed to run on top of NoSQL databases, which enables users to utilize linear algebra routines to process graph data stored in scalable, distributed databases. This framework is specifically optimized for Intel's Nervana-based Graphcore Machine (GCN) chip solution, allowing for greater compatibility between the Graphcore hardware and Graphulo. In this research, we examine the characteristics and applications of the Graphulo framework as it relates to NoSQL databases. We analyze this particular design leveraging its original use for general database use as well as exploring potential for use in multiple applications. The characteristics of scalability and compatibility discussed here represent an essential new step for wide application of the Graphulo framework due to limitations that prevent broad adoption as suggested earlier in user satisfaction and accessibility test studies. Specifically, Graphulo provides a means to store, process, and query large-scale graph datasets by incorporating fast, graph-based computations directly into the graph kernel. On another hand, our research evaluates scalability and performance of multiple NoSQL databases, including GraphCompute, GraphSON, Apache Giraph, Neo4j and Amazon Neptune, as Graphulo is implemented. Additionally, this research compares the results of implementing linear algebra and graph computation frameworks on GraphCompute and Apache Giraph. Further findings ultimately illuminate path to scalable, efficient deployment with adequate computational resources of Graphulo for applications in computational chemistry, physics, financial analysis systems, graph querying systems, machine learning, social networking and distributed computing.

It delves into various AI domains, where children's participation can enhance system performance, foster transparency, and guide the mitigation of potential risks associated with AI adoption. title: Topologically protected acoustic helical edge states and interface states in strongly coupled metamaterial ring lattices
Abstract: Acoustic materials and structures with helical edge states and interface states have garnered significant interest for their potential in robust acoustic wave manipulation and sensing applications. Recent advancements in strongly coupled metamaterials have led to the development of topologically non-trivial acoustic systems, which exhibit unique topological protection properties. This study explores the emergence of topologically protected acoustic helical edge states and interface states in strongly coupled metamaterial ring lattices. Using a combination of theoretical modeling and finite element simulations, we investigate how strong acoustic coupling between ring-shaped elements in a two-dimensional lattice give rise to topological non-trivial band structures. Specifically, we demonstrate the emergence of helical edge states at the 'edges' of the lattice, which are found to be topologically protected against defects and disorders. Moreover, we identify interface states that originate at the interface between two independent lattices and exhibit exceptional mobility along the interface. Our findings highlight the potential of strongly coupled metamaterial ring lattices as topological acoustic systems that can be engineered for robust wave guidance, sensing, and manipulation in various acoustic frequency regimes. These results have far-reaching implications for the design of novel acoustic devices and systems that leverage topological protection principles.

title: Deconstructing Bataknese Gorga Computationally
Abstract: This study presents a comprehensive computational deconstruction of the Bataknese Gorga, a traditional Batak Toba song from North Sumatra, Indonesia. By analyzing the song's musical structure and its performances, we aimed to identify and model the underlying patterns and rules that govern its creation. Our approach relied on audio and video recordings of various Gorga performances, sourced from both local archives and online platforms. We leveraged machine learning and natural language processing techniques to extract and tag relevant acoustic features, such as pitch, tempo, and intensity, as well as symbolic representations of the Gorga's lyrics and poetic structure. Our analysis revealed complex patterns and correlations between acoustic features, linguistic components, and melodic structures, teasing apart the intricate relationships between Bataknese musicians and the cultural context in which they operate. Furthermore, our exploration of the Gorga's production process allowed us to document and computationally generate novel compositions, effectively 'composing' the Bataknese Gorga through data-driven analysis. The results of this research provide new insights into the unique sonic landscape and creative processes of the Bataknese community and open avenues for interdisciplinary studies on the intersection of musicology, cultural anthropology, and artificial intelligence.

Through a meticulous examination of geometric and algebraic properties, the study demonstrates that $L^p$ -norms of polynomials on the $n$ -dimensional torus yield valuable information regarding the polynomial's Mahler's measure. The research sheds light on several pivotal theorems and their connections to the application of $L^p$ -norms, including a detailed consideration of $L^p$ -norms on the $n$ -dimensional torus. title: Snow Leopard Permutations and Their Even and Odd Threads
Abstract: This paper delves into the intricate patterns of the snow leopard's coat, examining the permutations that give rise to their unique and highly variable coloration. By analyzing the possible combinations of genes that control the snow leopard's coat color and pattern, we have identified a hierarchical structure of permutations that underlies their coat's even and odd threads. Our research reveals that the snow leopard's coat is composed of distinct repeating units, which we will refer to as 'blocks.' Each block itself consists of an intricate pattern of colored cells, allowing for a vast array of possible permutations that contribute to the snow leopard's recognizable dappled appearance. We identify statistical similarities and correlations in the color arrangements within blocks and throughout individual coats, shedding light on the evolutionary pressures that have driven the development of this remarkable adaptability in the snow leopard's coat. Furthermore, we explore the topological relationships between the different color permutations, including the frequency distributions of preferred and proscribed color combinations in different geographical and climatic contexts. title: Fractal percolation, porosity, and dimension
Abstract: This study explores the intricate relationships between fractal percolation, porosity, and dimension, offering new insights into the complex properties of disordered systems. By employing a variety of mathematical and computational techniques, we investigate the scaling behavior of percolation clusters in fractal lattices, revealing a rich interplay between porosity, connectivity, and spatial organization. Our analyses reveal that fractal percolation exhibits a fascinating blend of Euclidean and fractal properties, with porosity scaling non-trivially with the system size and the fractal dimension. Specifically, we find that the percolation threshold is closely related to the fractal dimension of the underlying lattice, and that the porosity of percolation clusters exhibits a crossover from a Euclidean to a fractal scaling regime as the system size increases. These findings have significant implications for our understanding of disordered systems in various fields, including materials science, geology, and biology, and can inform the development of new models and algorithms for simulating percolation processes in complex media. Furthermore, our work contributes to the ongoing debate on the role of fractals in percolation theory, highlighting the importance of considering multifractal and hierarchical structures in the analysis of percolation phenomena.

title: Thou shalt not take sides: Cognition, Logic and the need for changing how we believe
Abstract: Critical flaws in reasoning, inherent cognitive biases, and the widespread influence of misinformation highlight the urgent need to reevaluate our understanding of belief formation and cognition. For centuries, philosophy, science, and social constructs have led us to associate conviction with evidence and logic; however, a growing body of research uncovers the complexities and intricacies of the human thought process. Furthermore, the emergence of the internet and social media has significantly amplified the dissemination of both truthful and misleading information to the point of overwhelming indistinguishability. As a result, this paper posits that changing our approach to belief is essential to mitigating cognitive distortions and strengthening our ability to reason objectively. In essence, cognitive flexibility and openness to self-revision must be redefined as virtues of intelligent thinking, thereby fostering a more rationally reflexive society. In order to effect such a paradigm shift, it is necessary to underscore the inherent limitations of language and cognition while developing clear methodologies and pedagogical strategies to cultivate self-aware critical thinking. Ultimately, by comprehensively understanding the intricacies of human thought, we can evolve our approach to evidence, objectivity, and conviction, aligning them with a more realistic, increasingly reflexive, and above all, rational framework for understanding the complexities of our selves and the world around us.

title: The SP theory of intelligence: distinctive features and advantages
Abstract: The Surprisingly Powerful (SP) theory of intelligence is a novel and innovative framework that provides a comprehensive understanding of the intricate mechanisms that underlie human cognitive abilities. This theory posits that intelligence is not solely dependent on traditional measures of intelligence quotient (IQ) or cognitive abilities, but rather is a multifaceted construct that encompasses various cognitive and non-cognitive factors. The SP theory identifies three core features that distinguish it from previous theories: the capacity for cognitive flexibility, the ability to engage in self-directed learning, and the inclination towards open-ended exploration. These features enable individuals to adapt, learn, and innovate in complex and dynamic environments, thereby facilitating exceptional performance in real-world settings. A key advantage of the SP theory is its ability to explain the remarkable achievements of individuals who have attained exceptional status in diverse domains, such as science, art, and sports, despite average or even below-average IQ scores. Furthermore, the SP theory has significant implications for educational and training practices, suggesting that traditional approaches to learning and intelligence assessment may be limiting and in need of revision. Empirical evidence from cognitive psychology, neuroscience, and education has provided initial support for the SP theory, and continued research is necessary to fully explore its potential.

title: Wireless Coverage Area Computation and Optimization
Abstract: The rapid growth of wireless communication systems has led to the increasing demand for efficient and effective methods to compute and optimize wireless coverage areas. title: Flats in spaces with convex geodesic bicombings
Abstract: Convex geodesic bicombings have garnered significant attention in the realm of geometric group theory and metric geometry, particularly in the context of spaces with rich geometric structures. This study delves into the concept of flats in spaces equipped with convex geodesic bicombings, aiming to elucidate their properties and interconnectedness with established geometric theories. By definition, a flat in a space is a totally geodesic submanifold that is isometric to Euclidean space. When a space has a convex geodesic bicombing, it is endowed with a set of paths that join every pair of points, thus allowing the space to be explored through a versatile and flexible framework. Our investigation reveals that the structure of flats in such spaces exhibits a profound interplay between their combinatorial and geometric aspects, influenced by the properties of the bicombing. Notably, we demonstrate that the set of flats in a convex geodesic bicombing can be tessellated into a hierarchical structure, reflecting the combinatorial intricacies of the bicombing. Furthermore, we establish connections between flats in a space with a convex geodesic bicombing and other fundamental geometric concepts, such as CAT(0) groups and spaces, to provide a comprehensive understanding of the intrinsic geometric properties of this class of spaces. This research contributes to the growing body of knowledge on convex geodesic bicombings and flats, shedding light on the intricate relationships between the geometry, combinatorics, and group theory involved.

title: Type-Constrained Representation Learning in Knowledge Graphs
Abstract: This paper explores the integration of type constraints into representation learning in knowledge graphs, addressing the limitations of traditional graph neural networks in capturing semantic relationships between entities. We propose a novel approach, Type-Constrained Graph Neural Networks (T-GNN), which adopts entity types as an important aspect of knowledge graphs, enabling more accurate and interpretable representations of entities and relationships. By incorporating type constraints into the learning process, T-GNN infuses entity representations with semantic meaning and improves their discriminative power. To evaluate the proposed method, we conduct extensive experiments on several benchmarks, showing its superior performance in knowledge graph completion tasks and demonstrating its ability to capture nuanced relationship nuances. Additionally, ablation studies and error analysis reveal the significance of type constraints in improving model performance and interpretability. Extensive comparisons with state-of-the-art models further highlight the effectiveness of T-GNN in representing knowledge graphs with type constraints. The findings of this study open up new avenues for leveraging type constraints to enhance representation learning and contribute to the development of more robust and accurate knowledge graph embeddings.

title: Multi-Comm-Core Architecture for Terabit/s Wireless
Abstract: This research proposes a pioneering multi-comm-core architecture, engineered to support the massive scalability demands of Terabit/s wireless communication networks. The advent of 6G and Terabit/s wireless technology necessitates the development of more efficient and agile architectures that can seamlessly integrate diverse network functions and handle exponentially increasing demands with minimal latency. Our proposed multi-comm-core architecture uniquely combines heterogeneous computing engines, with distinct cores dedicated to processing control, management, and user data. This segmentation of computing functions enables significant improvements in system performance, power consumption, and security. Employing innovative edge computing techniques, our multi-comm-core framework enables highly customized and adaptive processing of diverse traffic patterns, thereby effectively reducing latency and maximizing network capacity. Comprehensive simulations reveal significant performance gains, showcasing up to a 30% reduction in latency, coupled with a substantial 25% power reduction, in comparison to established architectures. Furthermore, the proposed multi-comm-core framework is successfully shown to provide greater flexibility, facilitating easy integration with emerging technologies like artificial intelligence, machine learning, and quantum computing. Overall, this research paves the way for the development of scalable, high-performance, and adaptable wireless networks, poised to facilitate the widespread adoption of Terabit/s wireless technology.

title: Allocation of Heterogeneous Resources of an IoT Device to Flexible Services
Abstract:
Abstract: 
This research focuses on developing an optimal resource allocation framework for Internet of Things (IoT) devices to cater to various flexible services. The proposed solution addresses the challenge of efficiently managing the heterogeneous resources of IoT devices, such as CPU, memory, storage, and power supply, to meet the requirements of diverse and dynamic services. An IoT device can undertake various tasks simultaneously, including data processing, storage, and communication, posing difficulties in allocating resources efficiently. Traditional resource allocation approaches often rely on static and rigid models, failing to accommodate the dynamic nature of services and the heterogeneity of resources. To address these limitations, we introduce a novel meta-heuristic algorithm, called Hybrid Bio-Inspired Flexible Resources Allocation (Hybrid FARA). Hybrid FARA effectively combines the benefits of simulated annealing, particle swarm optimization, and genetic algorithms to achieve optimal resource allocation for IoT devices. The proposed approach is evaluated using a comprehensive set of experiments and scenarios, demonstrating significant improvements in terms of performance, efficiency, and adaptability compared to existing methods. The outcome of this research is expected to have substantial implications for the efficient operation of IoT devices in various application domains, including smart cities, healthcare, and industrial automation, potentially revolutionizing the way resources are allocated and managed in these critical areas.
